title: Air-Fried Chicken Drumsticks
ingredientLines: ½ teaspoon sweet or smoked paprika
4 (4- to 6-ounce) chicken drumsticks (about 1 pound total), pat dry with paper towels
steps: In a small bowl, stir together the paprika, garlic powder, black pepper, and salt.
Coat the drumsticks with the olive oil.
Sprinkle the drumsticks with the seasoning mixture, rubbing to coat evenly.
Preheat an air fryer to 400°F.
Place the drumsticks in the basket of the air fryer and cook for 10 minutes.
Use tongs to flip the drumsticks over and cook for 8 minutes.
Check the internal temperature for a doneness of 165-175°F. If not cooked through, cook for 2-5 minutes until done.
Serve warm.
notes: Remove the skin before cooking to reduce the fat content, if desired.

title: Anything Baked Burritos
ingredientLines: 1 teaspoon chili powder or chipotle powder
½ teaspoon sweet or smoked paprika
1 pound (16 ounces) protein (e.g. chicken, beef, pork, shrimp, tofu, tempeh; about 3 cups)
2 cups diced fresh vegetables (e.g. bell pepper, onion, mushrooms, carrots, tomatoes)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Spray the inside of a 9x13-inch baking dish with nonstick cooking spray and set aside.
In a small bowl, stir together the cumin, coriander, garlic powder, chili powder or chipotle powder, paprika, black pepper, salt, and cayenne (if using). Set aside.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering. Add the selected protein, selected vegetables, and the seasoning mixture.
Cook until the protein is cooked through (if applicable) and the vegetables are tender, about 8-12 minutes, stirring and breaking the protein into crumbles or shreds as needed.
Divide the mixture between the tortillas (about 1 cup each), then roll each tortilla up into a burrito.
Place the burritos in the prepared baking dish, with their sides touching. Spread the salsa over the top, then sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake until warmed through and the cheese is melted, about 15-20 minutes.
Serve warm.
categories: Main Dishes: Lamb, Goat, and Game Meat

title: Apple and Onion Salad
ingredientLines: 1 medium sweet onion, thinly sliced (about 1½ cups)
steps: In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the vinegar, oil, and black pepper.
Add the apples and onion. Toss to combine.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: Try using 2 cups chopped or shredded cabbage for 2 of the apples.
For a creamier consistency, replace the olive oil with olive oil mayonnaise or plain Greek yogurt.
This salad will keep in the refrigerator for 3-4 days.

title: Apple-Cinnamon Microwave Oatmeal
ingredientLines: 1 small apple (e.g. Gala, Fuji, Delicious, Pink Lady), cored and finely chopped (about ¾ cup)
½ cup uncooked old fashioned (rolled) oats
¼-½ teaspoon ground cinnamon, to taste
1 tablespoon unsalted chopped, slivered, or sliced nuts (e.g. almonds, walnuts, pecans)
1-3 teaspoons sweetener, to taste (optional; e.g. maple syrup, honey)
steps: Place the apple, oats, milk, water, cinnamon, and salt in a microwave-safe bowl. Stir to combine.
Cook on high power (default setting) in the microwave until thickened and bubbly, about 3-5 minutes, removing once or twice during the cooking time to stir.
Top with the selected nuts and sweetener (if using). Serve warm.
notes: For an overnight option, place all of the ingredients, except the selected nuts, in a container with a lid. Cover and refrigerate overnight, at least 8-12 hours. In the morning, serve cold or heat in the microwave for 1 minute and serve warm. Add the nuts just

title: Apple Coleslaw
ingredientLines: ¼ cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt
1-3 teaspoons lemon juice or apple cider vinegar, to taste
½ small (¾-1 pound) cabbage head, shredded (about 2 cups)
1 medium apple, cored and chopped (about 1 cup)
½ cup raisins or dried cranberries
steps: Add the yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice or vinegar, and salt to a large mixing or serving bowl. Stir together to make a dressing.
Add the cabbage, carrot, raisins or dried cranberries, and apple. Toss to combine and coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: This recipe goes well with pork burgers or pulled pork sandwiches.
Coleslaw tastes best when it is made on the same day it’s served. If not serving right away, wait to add the dressing until ready to serve.
Use pre-shredded cabbage and carrots to save time.
If you prefer a bit more sweetness, try adding 1-3 teaspoons honey to the dressing.

title: Apple Oatmeal Custard
ingredientLines: ½ medium apple, cut into ¼- to ½-inch chunks (about ½ cup)
1 teaspoon sweetener (e.g. honey, maple syrup, brown sugar)
steps: Add the almond milk, apple, oats, egg, selected sweetener, and cinnamon to a microwave-safe bowl or large mug.
Stir with a fork to combine.
Microwave on high (default power) for 1½ minutes, then stir with the fork.
Continue cooking until creamy, about 30 seconds.
Serve warm.
notes: Stir in an additional 1-2 teaspoons of almond milk if the custard is too thick.
The egg in this recipe adds extra protein and fat-soluble vitamins to a classic oatmeal dish.
Another milk – dairy or non-dairy – can be substituted for the almond milk, if desired.

title: Apple-Pear Sauce
ingredientLines: 4 medium (5- to 6-ounce) sweet apples (e.g. Gala, Macintosh, Fuji), peeled, cored and sliced (about 1½ pounds)
4 medium (5- to 6-ounce) ripe pears, peeled, cored and sliced (about 1½ pounds)
1-3 tablespoons maple syrup or honey, to taste (optional)
steps: In a large saucepan or other large pot, add the apples, pears, water, lemon juice, cinnamon, ginger, and salt.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook until the apples and pears are very soft, about 25-30 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Use an immersion (handheld) blender to blend the mixture into a smooth sauce, or use a potato masher for a chunkier sauce.
Taste and add maple syrup or honey if more sweetness is desired.
Serve warm, or chill before serving if desired. This sauce will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: Apple Pork Tenderloin
ingredientLines: ½-1 tablespoon ground cinnamon, to taste
steps: Place the carrots and potatoes in the bottom of a slow cooker.
Using a paring knife, make a series of small, parallel cuts across the length of the pork tenderloin.
Fill each cut in the pork tenderloin with an apple slice.
Place the apple-filled pork tenderloin on top of the carrots and potatoes in the slow cooker.
In a small bowl, make a glaze by whisking together the honey, soy sauce, mustard, balsamic vinegar, cinnamon, and garlic.
Pour the glaze mixture over the pork tenderloin.
Cover the slow cooker with the lid.
Cook on high for 3-4 hours, or on low for 6-8 hours.
credit: Submitted by Diane M. Longerbone MA, RD, CD, Richard L. Roudebush VAMC

title: Apple-Walnut Salad
ingredientLines: 1 (10-ounce) bag mixed salad greens or spinach
2 medium apples, cored and chopped (about 2 cups)
3 tablespoons red wine vinegar or apple cider vinegar
steps: In a small bowl, make the dressing by whisking together the olive oil, vinegar, honey, mustard, and garlic. Set aside.
In a large mixing or serving bowl, add the greens or spinach, apples, feta, and walnuts.
Just before serving, add the dressing to the vegetable mixture and toss to coat.
Serve immediately.
notes: Try swapping out the feta for blue cheese or crumbled goat cheese.

title: Apricot Chicken Tagine
ingredientLines: ½ teaspoon hot sauce or hot chili oil
4 (3- to 4-ounce) boneless skinless chicken thighs (thigh fillets; about 1 pound)
1 large sweet onion, thinly sliced (about 3 cups)
1 (15-ounce) can low-sodium garbanzo beans (chickpeas), drained and rinsed
¾ cup dried apricots, sliced or chopped
1 cinnamon stick (or 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, added to step 7)
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together the sour cream, parsley, and hot sauce or chili oil. Set in the refrigerator to chill.
In a separate small bowl, stir together the salt and pepper.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels, then sprinkle evenly with the salt-pepper mixture.
Heat a tagine, a Dutch oven, or a large stockpot over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Place the chicken in the pan and cook until golden-brown but not cooked through, about 3-5 minutes on each side. Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium, then add the onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the garlic and allspice. Cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the beans, tomatoes with their juice, apricots, and cinnamon. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.
Return the browned chicken to the pan and cover with a lid, Cook until the chicken is cooked through (internal temperature of 175°F), about 33-35 minutes.
Serve warm, with a heaping tablespoon of the sour cream mixture on top of each portion.
notes: This recipe also does very well in a pressure cooker. Follow steps 1-4 on “sauté” mode, then add the chicken, seal the lid, and pressure cook on high for 20 minutes. Allow the pressure to release naturally after cooking.
Instead of the allspice, a spice blend may be used such as Ras el Hanout, garam masala, or Chinese five-spice.

title: Arepas (Cornmeal Flatcakes)
ingredientLines: 2 cups corn flour (masa harina; see Recipe Notes)
½ medium onion, finely chopped (about ½ cup)
Optional toppings: Shredded cheese, Pico de Gallo, black beans or pinto beans (drained and rinsed)
steps: Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and garlic. Cook, stirring often, for 3 minutes.
Add the corn and continue cooking until the onion is softened, about 2-4 minutes.
Add the water and cilantro, then remove from the heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together the corn flour and salt. Add the onion-corn mixture and stir to combine and form a dough. The texture should look like mashed potatoes.
Wipe out the skillet, then coat the inside with nonstick cooking spray and place over medium heat.
Divide the dough into eight equal portions. Flatten each portion into a disc, about ¼-inch thick and 4-inches across, then add to the skillet.
Cook until lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes on each side.
Serve warm, adding toppings as desired.
notes: If you cannot find corn flour, you can use cornmeal. Note that the texture will be more gritty. To make corn flour from cornmeal, grind the cornmeal to a flour consistency in a blender or food processor.

title: Asian Ginger-Rice Soup
ingredientLines: ½ cup uncooked long-grain white rice
4 cups (32 ounces) low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
½-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled if desired, thinly sliced
4 scallions (green onions), thinly sliced, divided (about ½ cup)
steps: Add the rice, broth, and ginger to In a medium to large saucepan or stockpot. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cook uncovered until the soup thickens, about 40-45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve warm, topping each portion with a quarter of the scallions (~2 tablespoons each), ½ tablespoon of the soy sauce, and ½ teaspoon of the sesame oil.
notes: This soup will keep in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.
Add cubed tofu or a cooked animal protein (e.g. chicken, pork, shrimp) and a cooked or frozen vegetable (e.g. carrots, bell peppers, cabbage) to make this a meal.
Bone broth can be used, if desired, for additional nutrients and protein.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Asian-Inspired Chicken Kebabs
ingredientLines: 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger (or ¼ teaspoon ground dried ginger)
1 pound (16 ounces) boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into ¾- to 1-inch pieces
Optional garnishes: Toasted sesame seeds, sliced scallion (green onion)
steps: In a small mixing bowl, make a marinade by whisking together the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, honey, scallion, garlic, ginger, lemon zest, and white pepper.
Transfer the marinade mixture to a quart- or gallon-sized ziptop plastic bag. Set the bag inside the bowl, then add the chicken to the bag and toss to coat with the marinade.
Seal the bag, squeezing out the excess air. Let sit for 1-4 hours (in the refrigerator if longer than 1 hour).
Fill a 9x13-inch baking dish about halfway with warm water. Place four wooden skewers in the water and set aside.
Heat the grill to medium-high heat or the broiler to high heat. If the broiler is in an oven, move one rack to the top.
After 15 minutes of soaking, remove the skewers from the water and thread the chicken onto the skewers. Discard the excess marinade.

Brush the chicken with the oil, then place on the grill or on a broiler-safe baking sheet under the broiler (top oven rack). Cook to an internal temperature of 165°F, about 8-10 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes.
Serve warm, adding garnishes as desired.

title: Asian Salmon and Vegetable Packets
servingSize: 1 salmon fillet and 1 cup of the vegetables
ingredientLines: 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger (or 1 teaspoon ground ginger)
1 teaspoon Sriracha chili sauce or ½ teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional)
4 cups chopped or sliced raw vegetables, any variety (e.g. mushrooms, bell peppers, onions, zucchini, broccoli, cabbage)
steps: Preheat the oven to 450°F
In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, garlic, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, ginger, and Sriracha or red pepper flakes (if using).
Lay out 4 large sheets of heavy-duty foil.
Mound 1 cup of the selected vegetables onto the center of each piece of foil.
Place a salmon fillet on top of each pile of vegetables.
Divide the honey mixture evenly over each salmon and vegetable pile. This will be about 2 tablespoons for each pile.
Create four foil packets by bringing the short ends of each piece of foil together and folding twice to seal, then folding in the sides to seal, leaving room for steam.
Place the foil packets on a baking sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes.
Remove the baking sheet from the oven and open each foil packet, then preheat the boiler.
Place the baking sheet with the opened packets back in the oven and broil until the inside of the fish 145°F when measured with a thermometer, about 3-5 minutes.
Serve warm, garnishing each packet with the scallions and sesame seeds.
credit: Adapted from www.foodnetwork.com | Submitted by Jessica Long, MS, RDN, CD

title: Asian Slaw with Peanut Dressing
ingredientLines: 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger (or 1 teaspoon ground dried ginger)
1 tablespoon lite soy sauce or tamari
5 cups thinly sliced Napa cabbage (about ½ medium head Napa cabbage)
2 scallions (green onions), sliced thin (about ⅓ cup)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh delicate herb (e.g. cilantro, mint, basil, parsley)
steps: In a large mixing bowl, make a dressing by whisking together the peanut butter, vinegar, honey, ginger, lime juice, sesame oil, soy sauce or tamari, and black pepper.
Add the cabbage, bell pepper, carrot, jalapeño or serrano, scallions, and selected fresh herb.
Toss to combine and coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving. This slaw will keep in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

title: Asian Tempeh Lettuce Cups
servingSize: 1 lettuce cup with filling (without optional toppings)
ingredientLines: ¼ teaspoon ground dried ginger (or 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger)
1 tablespoon canola oil or avocado oil
¼ cup warm or room temperature water
4 sturdy lettuce leaves (e.g. Romaine, butter lettuce)
steps: In a small bowl, whisk 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of the vinegar, and 2 teaspoons of the maple syrup with the garlic powder and ginger. Set aside.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the tempeh and cook until lightly browned, about 4-6 minutes, stirring often.
Add the soy sauce mixture. Cook and stir for 2 minutes, then remove from the heat and set aside.
In the small bowl used previously, whisk the peanut butter and water with the remaining 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of vinegar, and 2 teaspoons of maple syrup.
Divide the tempeh mixture between the lettuce leaves, then drizzle with the peanut sauce.
Serve warm, adding toppings as desired.
notes: For a softer texture and more subtle flavor, boil the tempeh for 10 minutes before crumbling and cooking in oil.
Add 1 cup of cooked rice noodles to the tempeh at the end of step 4, if desired.
If you like a bit of heat, try adding some sriracha or crushed red pepper flakes to the sauce in step 1.

title: Asparagus and Spinach Risotto
ingredientLines: 4 cups (32 ounces) low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
¼-½ teaspoon ground black pepper, to taste
1 pound asparagus, cut into bite-sized pieces (about ½- to 1-inch-long)
¼ cup grated or shredded parmesan cheese
1-2 tablespoons lemon juice or white wine vinegar (optional)
steps: Add the broth to a large saucepan or stockpot and bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce the heat to low.
Place a separate large skillet or sauté pan on a different burner over medium heat.
Add the oil to the pan and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion to the pan with the oil and cook until softened, about 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the rice to the pan with the onion and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add ½ cup of the hot broth, salt and pepper. Bring to simmer and cook, stirring constantly, until the broth is absorbed.

Continue adding the hot broth about ½ cup at a time and cook, stirring constantly, until it is absorbed before adding more. Cook until all the broth has been added and absorbed, about 17-20 minutes, adding the asparagus once you have added about half of the broth.
Add the spinach and cook, stirring often, until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in the parmesan cheese and lemon juice or vinegar (if using), then serve warm.

title: Avocado Chocolate Mousse
ingredientLines: ½ cup dark chocolate or semi-sweet chocolate chips (regular or mini)
2 ripe avocados, halved, pits and peels removed
¼ cup sugar-based sweetener (e.g. sugar, honey, maple syrup, agave)
3 tablespoons lowfat (1%) milk (or non-dairy milk alternative)
steps: Add the chocolate chips, cocoa powder, and milk to a small microwave-safe dish and stir to combine.
Microwave on high power (default setting) for 15-30 seconds at a time, stirring before starting again, until the chocolate chips are fully melted.
Add the avocado, selected sweetener, vanilla, salt, and melted chocolate mixture to a blender or food processor. Blend until completely smooth, about 2-3 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: This mousse will keep in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
Consider serving topped with fresh berries, banana slices, and/or whipped cream. It can also be served as a dip for fresh fruit, pretzels, or graham crackers.

title: Avocado Deviled Eggs
ingredientLines: ¼ ripe avocado, peeled and pit removed
½-1 teaspoon lemon juice or vinegar (e.g. white distilled, apple cider), to taste
½-1 teaspoon olive oil or avocado oil, as needed to adjust the consistency
steps: Peel the hardboiled eggs, then slice in half lengthwise.
Remove the yolks from the egg halves and transfer to a small bowl. Mash into small pieces with a fork.
Add the avocado, lemon juice or vinegar, oil, salt, and black pepper. Mash with the fork to combine, adding more lemon juice or vinegar and/or oil to adjust the flavor and consistency as desired.
Using two spoons, one to scoop and one to scrape, divide the egg yolk-avocado mixture between the egg white halves (~1 tablespoon each).
Sprinkle the paprika over the tops of the filled eggs.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: These deviled eggs are best served right away, or within a few hours of placing in the refrigerator, as the avocado will brown over time.
Consider adding other spices such as garlic powder, onion powder, or cayenne.

To hard-boil eggs, place in a medium to large saucepan and cover with water by about 1 inch. Bring the water to a boil, then turn off the heat and cover with a lid. Let sit for 12-13 minutes, then carefully transfer to ice water.
Check avocados for ripeness by pressing gently on the skin. They are ripe when soft enough to push into slightly.

title: Baked Balsamic Tofu
ingredientLines: 1 (14- to 16-ounce) block extra-firm or firm tofu, cut into 8 slabs and then cut diagonally into triangles
steps: In a medium mixing bowl, make a marinade by whisking together the oil, vinegar, garlic, honey or maple syrup, lemon zest, basil, oregano, thyme, sage, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Transfer the marinade to a quart- or gallon-size ziptop plastic bag.
Add the tofu and toss gently to coat with the marinade.
Seal the bag, squeezing out as much air as possible.
Place in the refrigerator and let marinate, at least 30 minutes and up to overnight.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or aluminum foil.
Remove the tofu from the marinade and place on the baking sheet in a single layer.
Bake until crispy, about 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway through the cooking time.
Serve warm.

title: Baked Eggplant Parmesan
servingSize: 2 slices eggplant and half the sauce
ingredientLines: 1 medium eggplant (about 1 pound), trimmed and cut lengthwise into four planks about
¾-inch in thickness, halve middle planks crosswise and cube outer planks, divided
½ cup panko or whole-wheat breadcrumbs
½ cup grated parmesan cheese, divided
½ teaspoon ground black pepper, divided
Pinch-¼ teaspoon red pepper flakes, to taste
¼ cup shredded Italian blend cheese
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) chopped fresh basil, divided
steps: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Add the flour to a shallow dish. Add the egg to a second dish. Add the breadcrumbs, ¼ cup of parmesan, and ¼ teaspoon of black pepper to a third dish.

Coat each piece of sliced eggplant lightly with the flour, then the egg, and then the breadcrumb mixture. Transfer the breaded eggplant slices to a wire cooling rack set inside a rimmed baking sheet and let sit for 5 minutes.
Spray the breaded eggplant lightly on both sides with nonstick spray and bake until tender and golden-brown, about 20-22 minutes, flipping halfway through the time.
Meanwhile, heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chopped eggplant and salt. Cook, stirring often, until lightly-browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the garlic, red pepper, and the remaining ¼ teaspoon of black pepper. Cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds, then add the diced tomatoes with their juice.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the eggplant is tender and the sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes. Set aside.
Combine the remaining ¼ cup parmesan and the Italian cheese in a small mixing bowl. Top the baked eggplant slices with cheese and bake until melted, about 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the eggplant slices to plates and spoon the sauce over the top. Serve warm, sprinkling each serving with 2 tablespoons of chopped basil.

title: Baked Enchilada Casserole
ingredientLines: 1½ pounds cooked protein, chopped or shredded if needed (about 4 cups; e.g. chicken, pork, beef, shrimp, beans, lentils, tempeh, tofu)
3 cups enchilada sauce (homemade or store-bought; one 28-ounce can)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Coat the inside of a 9x13-inch baking pan with nonstick cooking spray and set aside.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted or thawed.
Add the selected protein and green chiles. Cook until warmed through, then remove from the heat.
Pour the enchilada sauce into a shallow microwave-safe dish (e.g. glass pie dish, shallow bowl) and warm in the microwave, about 1-2 minutes.
Set up a station with the following items, in this order: tortillas, warmed enchilada sauce, prepared baking pan, protein-spinach mixture, and shredded cheese.

Working one tortilla at a time, dip one tortilla in the sauce to coat and then place in the baking pan. Add ¼ cup of the protein-spinach mixture, then roll into a tube. Push to the side of the pan or next to the previous enchilada. Repeat with 11 more tortillas and protein-spinach mixture.

Spread any remaining protein-spinach mixture over the enchiladas. Dip the remaining 6 tortillas in the sauce and layer over the top. Spread any remaining sauce over the top, then sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake uncovered until warmed through, about 25-30 minutes. Serve warm.
categories: Main Dishes: Lamb, Goat, and Game Meat

title: Baked French Toast
ingredientLines: 8 slices whole-grain or multigrain sandwich bread
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Spray a rimmed baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray, then set aside.
Add the butter to a small microwave-safe bowl. Microwave on high power (default setting) until melted, about 15-30 seconds. Set aside to cool slightly.
In a separate medium mixing bowl, whisk together the eggs, vanilla, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt.
Add the cooled melted butter and milk. Whisk to combine.
Pour the egg mixture into the prepared baking sheet. Tilt the pan to each side until the liquid covers the bottom.
Working quickly, place the slices of bread onto the baking sheet in a single layer, then flip the slices over. Let sit to absorb the egg mixture, about 1-2 minutes.
Bake until the bottoms of the bread slices are golden-brown, about 12-15 minutes.

With the pan still in the oven, switch the oven to broil on high. Continue cooking until the tops of the bread slices are lightly-browned, about 1-3 minutes. This happens quickly, so watch closely to make sure the bread doesn’t burn.
Serve warm.

title: Baked Pumpkin Oatmeal
ingredientLines: 2 teaspoons pumpkin pie spice or ground cinnamon
¾ cup canned pumpkin puree (about half of a 15-ounce can)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Spray the inside of an 8x8-inch baking dish or 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick cooking spray. Set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, stir together the oats, brown sugar, pumpkin pie spice or cinnamon, baking powder, and salt.
Add the pumpkin and eggs. Stir until the egg yolks and whites are combined.
Add the milk and vanilla. Stir to combine.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish or divide between the muffin tin cups.
Bake until fully set, about 30-35 minutes in an 8x8-inch baking dish or 25-30 minutes in a 12-cup muffin tin. Center should be firm when tapped and not indent.
Let cool for 5 minutes before slicing or removing from the muffin tin, then serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk (e.g. almond milk, soy milk), if desired.
This baked oatmeal will keep in an airtight in the refrigerator for up to 7 days, or freezer for 6 months.
If you cut the recipe in half, use 2 eggs. If making it in a baking dish, reduce the cook time by about 10 minutes.

title: Banana-Oatmeal Protein Pancakes
ingredientLines: ⅓ cup old fashioned (rolled) or quick-cooking oats
steps: Put the banana in a medium mixing bowl and mash with a fork.
Add the eggs and mix with the fork until well combined.
(Optional) Put the oats in a blender or food processor and blend until finely ground (skip this step if using quick-cooking oats).
Add the oats and cinnamon to the banana mixture. Stir to combine.
Heat a medium or large nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Working ¼ cup at a time and around the perimeter of the skillet, portion the mixture into the pan, leaving at least ½ inch between each portion of batter.
Cook on one side until golden-brown, about 1-3 minutes.
Flip all of the pancakes over and cook on the other side until golden-brown, about 1-2 minutes.
Repeat steps 7-9 with any remaining batter.
Serve warm, topping as desired
credit: Submitted by Dana Herring MS, RDN

title: Barbecue Chicken Sandwiches
ingredientLines: ½ cup shredded carrots (about 1 medium carrot)
1 tablespoon olive oil mayonnaise or plain Greek yogurt
2 whole-wheat burger buns or sandwich thins
4 leaves crunchy lettuce (e.g. Romaine lettuce, green leaf lettuce)
steps: In a medium bowl, stir together the chicken, carrots, and barbeque sauce.
Mix until the chicken and carrots are well coated with the sauce.
Spread half of the mayonnaise or Greek yogurt on the top halves of each bun or sandwich thin.
Top the bottom half of each bun or sandwich thin with half of the chicken mixture and two lettuce leaves.
Add the top bun.
Serve immediately, or warm briefly in the microwave before serving, about 15-30 seconds.
notes: This recipe works well with leftover chicken, rotisserie chicken, or canned chicken.
The chicken mixture could be served in a wrap or pita bread as well.
If making ahead, wait to assemble the buns or sandwich thins until serving.
Try mashed avocado or hummus as a spread in place of the mayonnaise or Greek yogurt.

title: Barbecue Pork Sheet Pan Dinner
servingSize: 1 pork chop and ¼th of the vegetables
ingredientLines: 2 sweet potatoes, peeled and diced (about 4 cups)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F
Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Coat the pork chops on both sides with the barbecue sauce.
Place the coated pork chops in the middle of the prepared baking sheet.
Place the sweet potatoes in a medium size bowl and toss with 1 tablespoon of the oil and 1 tablespoon of the seasoning.
Spread the sweet potatoes onto one side of the baking sheet.
In the same bowl, add the Brussels sprouts and toss with remaining 1 tablespoon oil and 1 tablespoon seasoning.
Spread the Brussels sprouts onto the other side of the baking sheet.
Bake until the pork chops fully cooked and the vegetables are tender, about 30 minutes.
Serve warm.
credit: Adapted from www.stockpilingmoms.com | Submitted by Kristen Bertram RDN

title: Basil Pesto
ingredientLines: 4-6 garlic cloves, unpeeled and left whole
3 cups packed fresh basil leaves (about 3 ounces)
⅓ cup finely grated parmesan cheese
¼-½ teaspoon ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.

Add the unpeeled garlic cloves and the walnuts to the pan. Toast, shaking the pan occasionally, until the garlic cloves are softened and spotty brown and the walnuts are golden and fragrant, about 7-10 minutes. Remove from the pan and set aside to cool.
When the garlic cloves are cool enough to handle, remove and throw away the peels, then chop into large pieces.
Place the basil leaves in a gallon-size ziptop plastic bag. Squeeze out the excess air and seal the bag closed.
Pound the basil in the sealed bag with the flat side of a meat mallet or a rolling pin until all the leaves are bruised.
Add the garlic, walnuts, basil, oil, parmesan, lemon juice, black pepper, and salt to a food processor. Puree until smooth, scraping down the bowl as needed.
Serve as desired.
notes: Keep covered in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Pesto can also be frozen for up to 3 months.

title: Bean and Barley Soup
ingredientLines: 4 cups (32 ounces) no-salt-added chicken or vegetable broth
1 (15.5-ounce) can no-salt-added great northern beans, drained and rinsed
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes
steps: Heat a large saucepan (pot) over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, celery, carrots, and garlic.
Sauté until the vegetables are soft, about 4-5 minutes.
Stir in the broth, beans, diced tomatoes and their liquid, barley, oregano, thyme, and crushed red pepper flakes.
Bring to a simmer and cover, stirring occasionally. Allow barley to cook and flavors to blend for about 20 minutes.
Stir in the spinach.
Continue to simmer until fully cooked, about 5 minutes.
Serve warm.
credit: Inspired by a recipe submitted by Georgina Hignell RD, Northport VAMC
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Bean and Vegetable Tacos
ingredientLines: 1 portabella mushroom, sliced (or 1 cup sliced white button or cremini mushrooms)
½ cup canned tomato sauce (or 1 tablespoon tomato paste plus ⅓ cup water)
1 cup canned beans, drained and rinsed
Optional toppings: Diced or sliced avocado, salsa, shredded cheese, chopped fresh cilantro, plain Greek yogurt
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Wrap the tortillas in foil and bake for 10 minutes. Remove from the oven and set aside, still wrapped in the foil
Meanwhile, heat a medium skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the mushroom, bell pepper, onion, and salt. Cook, stirring often, until the vegetables are soft and starting to brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the chili powder and cumin. Stir together and cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the beans, tomato sauce (or tomato paste and water), and brown sugar. Cook until warmed through, about 2-3 minutes.
Add a quarter of the bean-vegetable mixture to the center of each tortilla.
Serve warm, adding optional toppings as desired.
notes: To make ahead, keep the filling separate and heat and fill tortillas when ready to eat
credit: Adapted from HealthySeasonalRecipes.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Beef and Root Vegetable Puree
ingredientLines: 4 ounces beef stew meat, cut into 1-inch chunks (about ½ cup)
1 large carrot, peeled if desired, chopped into ½-inch pieces (about 1 cup)
1 medium (8- to 10-ounce) sweet potato, peeled and chopped (about 1½ cups)
steps: Add the beef, carrot, sweet potato, and broth to a medium saucepan.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.

Cover the pan with a lid and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 20-25 minutes. Halfway through the cooking time, check to make sure the vegetables are still covered by broth. If not, add enough water to cover them.
Blend until completely smooth with an immersion (handheld) blender or transfer to a standing blender, with the center piece of the lid removed and covered with a hand towel or folded-up paper towel.
If the puree is too thick, add an additional 1-3 tablespoons of water or broth and continue blending.
Serve warm.
notes: Add more flavor with dried herbs or spices. Salt can be added to adjust the seasoning, if needed.
This puree can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 4 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months.
Another broth can be used in place of the beef broth, if desired. Look for low-sodium if you need to limit sodium.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Beet and Bean Burger
servingSize: 1 burger patty without serving vessel or toppings
ingredientLines: 1 cup small diced onion (about 1 medium onion)
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added white beans (e.g. great northern, cannellini), drained and rinsed
1 cup grated raw beets (about ¼ pound or 1 medium beet)
Desired serving vessel (e.g. whole-wheat buns, whole-wheat sandwich thins, lettuce wrap)
Desired toppings (e.g. condiments, lettuce, spinach, arugula, tomato, onion)
steps: Heat a medium to large skillet over medium heat.
Add 1 tablespoon of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, salt, and black pepper. Cook until softened and lightly-browned, about 8-10 minutes. Set aside.
Add the walnuts to a food processor and pulse to break down into small crumb-like pieces.
Add the beans, beets, panko, garlic powder, coriander, cumin, and onion. Pulse until the mixture is crumbly.
Transfer the mixture to a large mixing bowl and add the egg. Mix until well combined.
Using clean hands that are slightly wet, divide the mixture into four equal portions and form each portion into a patty about 4 inches wide and ½-inch-thick.
Return the skillet to the stovetop over medium heat. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil.
Working in batches if needed, cook the patties until crisp and well-browned, about 6-8 minutes on each side.
Serve warm, on the desired serving vessel and topped as desired.

title: Berry-Beet Smoothie
ingredientLines: 1 medium beet, cut into ½-inch-thick wedges (about 1 cup)
steps: Place a steamer basket inside a large saucepan or stockpot and add just enough water fill the area under the steamer.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-high to maintain a rapid simmer (just below boiling).
Add the beet wedges to the steamer basket and cover the pot with a lid. Cook until the beets are tender, about 12-17 minutes.
Remove the steamer basket from the pot and set aside to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Pour the milk into the pitcher of a blender. Add the berries, selected sweetener, salt, and steamed beets.
Blend until smooth and fully combined, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve immediately. Leftovers may be frozen, thawing in the microwave at 30% power for 3-5 minutes.
notes: Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk, if desired.
Look for cooked beets in the produce section for an easy option.

title: Berry-Lime Banana Sorbet
ingredientLines: 2 frozen medium bananas, peeled and sliced before freezing
1 cup frozen berries (one type or a combination; e.g. strawberries, blueberries, mixed berries, berry-cherry blend)
¼ teaspoon grated fresh ginger (or 1 pinch ground dried ginger)
steps: Add the frozen bananas, berries, cranberry-pomegranate juice, lime zest, and ginger to a food processor or high-powered blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.
Serve immediately for a soft-serve texture. For a firmer texture, put it in the freezer for 2-3 hours, stirring every 20-30 minutes.
notes: Blending the frozen bananas will take a few minutes. It will be very loud, similar to adding ice cubes to a blender. Within a few minutes though, you should be seeing a thick, creamy ice-cream-like mixture in the blender.
Any 100% juice product can be used in this recipe.
The zested lime will keep in a plastic ziptop back for up to 7 days in the refrigerator, or up to 3 months in the freezer. Use the juice in other recipes as desired.

title: Berry Pudding Parfait
ingredientLines: 1 (3.4-ounce) package instant pudding mix (any flavor; e.g. vanilla, lemon, banana, cheesecake)
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) sliced or slivered almonds, divided
steps: Empty the package of pudding mix to a medium mixing bowl.
Add the milk and stir until thickened, about 2-3 minutes.
Gather four serving glasses or parfait dishes. Divide the pudding and berries between each of the glasses, alternating layers of berries with layers of pudding.
Top each glass with 1 tablespoon of the almonds.
Serve immediately, or chill up to 3 hours before serving.
notes: Substitute your favorite chopped nuts for the almonds.
To decrease the sugar content, use a sugar-free instant pudding mix.
Swap out your favorite fresh or frozen fruit for the strawberries and/or blueberries.
Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk if desired.

title: Berry-Vanilla Overnight Oats
ingredientLines: ½ cup uncooked old fashioned (rolled) oats
1 (5.3-ounce) container vanilla nonfat Greek yogurt (about ½ cup)
½ cup frozen berries (one type or a combination; e.g. blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, mixed berries, sliced strawberries)
steps: In a small (~2-cup) jar, bowl, or storage container, stir together the oats, milk, yogurt, and cinnamon.
Add the berries and stir to combine.
Cover with a lid or plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator. Chill overnight, or at least 5 hours.
Serve cold, or warm briefly (about 1 minute) in the microwave.
notes: These overnight oats will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Consider making multiple batches for a quick breakfast option throughout the week.
For more texture and protein, try adding a nut and/or seed (e.g. chopped walnuts, sliced or slivered almonds, pepitas, hemp hearts).
Another flavor of Greek yogurt can be used, if desired.

Any frozen or drained canned fruit (e.g. peaches, cherries, mango, pears) can be used in place of the berries. Avoid mixing pineapple with the dairy in this recipe since this can create a bitter flavor.

title: Berry-Yogurt Protein Bowls
ingredientLines: ¼ cup sweetener (e.g. honey, maple syrup, agave)
4 cups fresh or frozen berries (one type or a combination; e.g blueberries, sliced or chopped strawberries, raspberries, blackberries), thawed if frozen unless making ahead, divided
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) hemp hearts (hulled hemp seeds), divided
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) flax meal (ground flaxseed), divided
steps: In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the yogurt, selected sweetener, and cinnamon.
Divide the yogurt mixture between four individual serving bowls or storage containers (about 1 cup each).
Top each serving with 1 cup of the berries, 1 tablespoon of the hemp hearts, and 1 tablespoon of the flax meal.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: These protein bowls will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days.
Chopped or sliced toasted nuts can be substituted for the hemp seeds and/or flax meal.

title: Black Bean and Corn Salsa
ingredientLines: 1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
2 cups corn kernels (cooked from fresh, frozen, or canned; thawed if frozen)
2 large tomatoes, seeded and diced (about 3 cups)
1 lime, juiced (about 2 tablespoons), plus more to taste if desired
¼ teaspoon black pepper, plus more to taste if desired
steps: In a large mixing bowl, stir together the beans, corn, onion, cilantro, jalapeño, lime juice, vinegar, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Taste and add more black pepper or lime juice, if desired.
Serve with tortilla chips or as a topping for tacos or grilled chicken.
notes: Add diced avocado or any color bell pepper an extra pop of flavor

title: Black Bean Burgers
ingredientLines: ½ cup old fashioned (rolled) oats or cubes of whole-wheat bread
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added black beans, chilled in the refrigerator, drained and rinsed
1 teaspoon soy sauce or Worcestershire sauce
steps: Add the oats or bread cubes to a food processor. Pulse or blend on low speed until crumbs form.
Add the chilled black beans, egg, onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper, cumin, coriander, and soy sauce or Worcestershire sauce.
Pulse or blend on low speed until the mixture is partially mashed and holds together. It should not be pureed.
Using slightly wet hands, divide the mixture into three equal portions and form each portion into a patty.
Spray a large skillet with nonstick cooking spray and place over medium-high heat.
Once the pan is hot, add the patties and cook until they are well-browned and hold together, about 5 minutes per side.
Serve warm on their own, with a dipping sauce, or on a bun with your choice of toppings.
notes: If you don’t have black beans, you can swap just about any other bean in as a substitute. You can also try experimenting with different herb and spice combinations to change up the flavors.
These are best eaten right away, but can keep in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Freezing is not recommended.

title: Black Bean-Covered Sweet Potato
servingSize: 1 medium sweet potato (or ½ large) with 1 cup bean mixture
ingredientLines: 2 medium sweet potatoes (about 6 ounces each) or 1 large sweet potato, cut in half in step 6 after cooking (about 12 ounces total)
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
2 tablespoons nonfat plain Greek yogurt, divided
steps: Wash the sweet potatoes and prick with a fork in several places. Wrap in parchment paper or a paper towel.
Microwave the sweet potatoes on high power (default setting) until tender all the way to the center, about 7-10 minutes, flipping halfway through the cooking time.
Set the sweet potatoes aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, combine the beans, tomato, oil, cumin, and coriander in a medium microwave-safe bowl.
Microwave the bean mixture on high power (default setting) until heated through, about 2-3 minutes.

When the sweet potatoes are just cool enough to handle, cut a slice in each sweet potato lengthwise, just enough to open it but not to cut all the way through. Press the ends of each sweet potato to make a well in the center.
Spoon the bean mixture into the well of each sweet potato.
Top each sweet potato with 1 tablespoon of the Greek yogurt and 1 tablespoon of the cilantro. Serve warm.
notes: Instead of microwaving, place the sweet potatoes in a baking dish and cook in the oven at 425°F until tender all the way to the center, about 1 hour, then heat the bean mixture in a small saucepan over medium heat.

title: Blueberry Kombucha Spritzer
ingredientLines: 1-2 tablespoons lemon juice, to taste (about ¼-½ lemon)
2 teaspoons sweetener (e.g. sugar, honey, maple syrup)
Optional: Lemon slices or twists and/or fresh blueberries, for garnish
steps: Add the blueberries, lemon juice, and sweetener to the pitcher of a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth, adding some of the kombucha to assist with blending if needed.
Add the remaining amount of the kombucha to the blender or food processor and stir by hand or pulse briefly to combine.
Pour into two glasses, dividing equally between the glasses.
Serve cold, garnishing with lemon and/or fresh blueberries as desired.
notes: For a boost of flavor, consider adding 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger or ¼ teaspoon ground cinnamon.
If you cannot find or do not have kombucha, plain seltzer water can be substituted in a pinch – though, it does not have the same probiotic benefits of kombucha, which is fermented.
Kombucha is made from tea, which usually has caffeine.

title: Blueberry Oatmeal Pancakes
ingredientLines: 1 cup lowfat buttermilk (can substitute 1 cup milk plus 1 tablespoon lemon juice or vinegar)
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted and cooled
½ cup fresh or frozen blueberries
steps: Combine the oats and buttermilk in a medium mixing bowl and let sit, covered, in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. If you don’t have time to let it sit, microwave the oat-buttermilk mixture until the oats have absorbed the liquid and the mixture is batter-like, about 1-2 minutes).
In a separate medium mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda.
Add the flour mixture, egg, melted butter, and blueberries to the oat-buttermilk mixture. Stir to combine.
Spray a nonstick skillet with nonstick spray and set over medium heat.
Working ¼ cup at a time and around the perimeter of the skillet, portion the batter into the pan, leaving at least ½ inch between each portion of batter.
Cook on the first side until bubbles form and pop on the top surface and the edges are dry, about 3-4 minutes.
Flip all of the pancakes over and cook on the other side until golden-brown, about 1-2 minutes.
Repeat steps 5-7 with any remaining batter.
Serve warm.

title: Blueberry Protein Pancakes
ingredientLines: ½ cup fresh or frozen blueberries (do not thaw, if frozen)
Optional toppings: Maple syrup, yogurt, unsalted butter, nut or seed butter, applesauce
steps: In a medium mixing bowl, mash the banana with a fork.
Add the eggs, flax meal, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt. Whisk together with the fork to combine.
Add the oats and blueberries, then stir to combine.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat, then coat the inside of the pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Working ¼ cup at a time and around the perimeter of the pan, portion the batter into the pan, leaving at least ½ inch between each portion of batter.
Cook on the first side until bubbles form and pop on the surface and the edges begin to dry, about 3-5 minutes. Flip and finish cooking on the second side, about 1-2 minutes.
Repeat steps 5-6 with any remaining batter.
Serve warm, adding toppings as desired.
notes: If desired, steps 1-3 can be done in a blender or with an electric mixer, stirring in the blueberries at the end.
If you don’t have quick oats, add 1¼ cup old-fashioned (rolled) oats to a food processor or blender and pulse or blend to a breadcrumb-like consistency.

title: Braised Chicken and Vegetable Skillet
ingredientLines: 1 pound small red or yellow potatoes, cut into quarters
1 pound carrots, peeled cut into 1-inch pieces
1 pound green beans (fresh or frozen), ends trimmed if fresh
steps: Heat a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken and sear until browned, about 4-5 minutes on each side.
Add the potatoes, carrots, broth, and thyme
Reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cover the pan with lid and simmer for 25-30 minutes.
Remove the lid. Add the green beans and onion.
Place the lid back on the pan. Continue to simmer until the chicken is fully cooked and vegetables are tender, about 10-15 minutes.
credit: Adapted from www.lyndasrecipebox.com | Submitted by Jessica Long MS, RDN, CD

title: Braised Cod and Green Beans with Pesto
servingSize: 1 cod fillet with ¼ of the green beans and sauce
ingredientLines: 2 medium shallots or 1 small onion, thinly sliced (about ¾ cup)
1½ cups (12 ounces) low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
steps: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the green beans and shallot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the shallot starts to soften, about 1-2 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix together the salt and pepper and sprinkle both sides of each cod fillet with the mixture.
Spread the green beans into a flat layer in the pan and gently place the cod fillets on top.
Add the broth and bring to a boil over high heat.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook until the cod is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, about 4-6 minutes.
With a slotted spoon or spatula, transfer the cod and green beans to a serving dish. Cover with foil to keep warm.
Continue to cook the broth over high heat, uncovered, until it is reduced to about ½ cup, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the pesto.
Pour the sauce over the fish and green beans.
Garnish with lemon wedges if desired and serve warm.

title: Braised Mustard Greens with Red Beans
ingredientLines: ¼ cup raw unsalted nuts (e.g. peanuts, walnuts, almonds), roughly chopped
2 bunches mustard greens, destemmed and torn into 1- to 2- inch pieces (about 8 cups)
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added kidney beans, drained and rinsed
3 thinly sliced scallions (green onions; about ⅓ cup)
steps: Heat a large sauté pan or skillet over medium heat.
Add the nuts to the pan and cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant and lightly toasted, about 2-5 minutes. Remove the nuts from the pan and set aside.
Add the oil to the now-empty pan and place over medium heat. Heat the oil until it is shimmering.
Add the onion and sauté until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the garlic, curry powder or turmeric, black pepper, and salt. Sauté until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes with their juice. Stir to combine.
Add the mustard greens to the pan and cook, tossing or stirring occasionally, until they begin to wilt, about 1-2 minutes. Work in batches if needed.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and cover the pan with a lid. Cook until the greens are tender, about 7-10 minutes.
Add the beans, scallions, and toasted nuts. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
notes: Substitute another hearty leafy green, such as kale or collard greens, for the mustard greens if desired.

title: Bread Stuffing with Apples and Celery
ingredientLines: 4 cups cubed white or whole-wheat bread
1 medium apple, cored and chopped (about 1 cup)
3 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley (or 1 teaspoon dried
steps: Preheat the oven to 275°F.
Place the cubed bread on a baking sheet. Bake until the bread is dried out, about 10-15 minutes. Set aside.
Increase the oven temperature to 350°F. Coat an oven-safe casserole dish with nonstick cooking spray. Set aside.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the butter and oil. Heat until melted and shimmering.
Add the apple, onion, celery, sage, thyme and salt. Cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat and add the dried bread cubes, chicken broth, and parsley. Stir gently to combine.
Transfer the bread mixture into the oven-safe dish. Cover with foil and bake for 35 minutes.
Remove the foil and continue baking for 10 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: If you like garlic, mince 6 cloves garlic (about 1 tablespoon) and add to the pan in step 6.
To increase the protein, dice 1 cooked apple chicken sausage and add to the pan in step 7.
credit: Adapted from Delicious on a Dime | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Breakfast Burritos
ingredientLines: ½ medium onion, diced (about ½ cup)
½ medium bell pepper, diced (about ½ cup)
4 large eggs (can substitute half of a 16-ounce block of soft or firm tofu, crumbled into chunks and pat dry with paper towels)
4 (10-inch) whole-wheat tortillas, warmed in the microwave for 15-30 seconds
steps: Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, bell pepper, broccoli, and black pepper. Cook, stirring often, until tender, about 5-7 minutes.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs together.

Move the vegetables to the sides of the pan and pour the eggs into the middle. Scrape the bottom of the pan with a rubber spatula as the eggs cook, keeping the eggs in the middle and the vegetables on the sides.
Once the eggs are cooked, mix in the vegetables and stir in the cheese. Remove the pan from the heat.
Top each warmed tortilla with a quarter of the egg mixture and 1 tablespoon of the salsa. Wrap into a burrito and set aside. Repeat with the remaining tortillas, egg mixture, and salsa.
Serve warm.
notes: These burritos freeze well. To freeze, let cool and wrap each burrito in plastic wrap, then place in a zip-top plastic bag. Freeze for up to 3 months. To thaw, unwrap a burrito and place it on a microwave -safe plate. Cover with a paper towel and microwave until the burrito is hot in the center, about 2 minutes.

title: Breakfast PB&J Wrap-Up
steps: Place the wrap or tortilla on a clean flat surface.
Spread the peanut butter on one half of the wrap or tortilla and the fruit preserves on the other half.
Place the banana at the edge of the wrap, on the preserves side, along the line between the peanut butter and the preserves.
Roll the wrap or tortilla up around the banana, rolling towards the peanut butter side. The peanut butter should act like a glue and keep the wrap together.
Enjoy whole as a grab-and-go breakfast, slice into pieces to share, or serve as a side.
notes: Try using almond butter in place of the peanut butter.
Look for fruit preserves that have fruit listed as the first ingredient.
To reduce the total carbohydrates, consider leaving out the fruit preserves.

title: Bright Beet and Orange Salad
ingredientLines: 1 cup chopped or sliced cooked beets, cooled
1 large navel or Cara Cara orange, peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces (about 1 cup)
2 ounces fresh mozzarella, cut into bite-sized pieces (about ¼ cup)
steps: In a medium mixing or serving bowl, whisk together the oil, vinegar, mustard, salt, and black pepper.
Add the beets, orange, arugula, and mozzarella.
Toss to combine and coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: To make this dish a complete meal, add a cooked protein (e.g. chicken, lean beef, shrimp, beans, tempeh).
Look for cooked beets in the produce section for an easy option.
Try substituting crumbled feta or goat cheese for the mozzarella.

title: Bright Broccoli Salad
ingredientLines: 1 cup finely diced onion (about 1 medium onion)
1 large carrot, shredded (or 2 medium; about 1 cup)
⅓ cup slivered or sliced almonds
steps: Add the mayonnaise and vinegar to a large bowl. Stir together until smooth to make a dressing.
Add the broccoli, onion, grapes, carrots, and almonds.
Toss together to coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: To add color, consider using a red onion or include a variety of different colored grapes.
If you are out of grapes, try substituting ¼ cup raisins instead.
For a smoky flavor, crumble in 2 slices of cooked bacon.
To cut down on the raw onion flavor, let the onion sit in the bowl with the red wine vinegar while you prepare the other ingredients.

title: Broccoli Cheese Soup
ingredientLines: ½ medium onion, diced (about ½ cup)
1 medium head broccoli, cut into bite-sized florets (about 3 cups)
2 cups (16 ounces) low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
steps: Heat a large saucepan or stockpot over medium heat.
Add oil and heat until shimmering.
Add onion and carrots. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the flour and cook while stirring for 1 minute.
Add the broccoli, broth, milk, and mustard. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil then reduce heat to maintain a simmer and cook for about 5 minutes or until broccoli is tender.
Remove from heat and stir in the cheese and pepper.
Serve warm.
notes: Store in the fridge for up to 4 days or freeze leftovers up to 3 months.
If you prefer a smooth soup, puree the mixture with an immersion or standing blender.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Broccoli Salad
ingredientLines: 2 pounds broccoli, cut into large florets
¼ cup finely chopped red onion
steps: Place the currants in a small heatproof bowl. Pour the boiling water over the currants and set aside for 5 minutes, then drain off the water.
Meanwhile, add the dressing ingredients to a large bowl and whisk to combine.
Using a box grater or the shredding disk on a food processor, shred the broccoli.
Add the shredded broccoli to the bowl with the dressing.
Add the currants, red onion, and almonds and toss to combine.
Let the mixture sit for 30 minutes at room temperature or 1 hour in the refrigerator before serving.
Serve cold or at room temperature.
credit: Adapted from TheKitchn.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix RD, CSO

title: Broccoli Sesame Noodle Salad
ingredientLines: 4 ounces whole-grain spaghetti (a quarter of a 16-ounce box)
2 cups fresh or frozen broccoli florets
1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger (or ¼ teaspoon ground dried ginger)
1 medium carrot, thinly sliced (abut ½ cup)
steps: Fill large saucepan or stockpot halfway full with water. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the pasta and cook 4 minutes, then add the broccoli to then continue cooking until the pasta is tender, about 4-5 minutes.
Drain the pasta and broccoli into a colander and briefly rinse with cold water.
In a large bowl, whisk together the vinegar, hoisin sauce, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, and garlic.
Add the pasta, broccoli, and carrot. Toss to combine.
Serve cold, chilling in the refrigerator if needed. Toss again before serving to recombine with the dressing.
notes: If you do not have hoisin sauce, you can substitute 1 teaspoon of honey.
To increase the spice, add ½ teaspoon of crushed red pepper or 1 teaspoon sriracha to the dressing.
To make this dish a complete meal, serve with a protein such as cooked chicken, tofu, shrimp, or pork.

title: Brussels Sprout and Apple Salad
ingredientLines: 3 cups fresh Brussels sprouts, shredded or thinly sliced
1 tart sweet apple, such as a honey crisp, chopped
steps: Combine the Brussels sprouts, apple, and shallot in a medium bowl.
In a small dish or jar, combine the oil, vinegar, honey, salt and pepper. Whisk or shake to combine.
Pour the dressing over the Brussels sprouts, apple and shallot and stir well.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Garnish with nuts and cheese just before serving.
notes: Substitute shredded cabbage for the Brussels sprouts if desired.
Omit salt to reduce the sodium content.
credit: Adapted from Onceuponachef.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Calabacitas con Elote
ingredientLines: 2 medium tomatoes, cut into 1-inch pieces (about 2 cups)
½ medium onion, diced (about ½ cup)
2 medium zucchini, trimmed, halved lengthwise and cut into 1-inch chunks (about 4 cups)
steps: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, and salt.
Cook, stirring often, until the tomatoes release their juice and the onion is softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the zucchini and corn.
Increase the heat to high and cook, stirring occasionally, until the zucchini is just starting to soften and the corn is thawed, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the cilantro and lime juice. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
notes: A little charring on the vegetables is okay and adds a nice flavor.
If a crust forms on the bottom of the pan, use a rubber spatula to scrape it up and mix it into the vegetables. Adding the lime juice at the end will help to remove any that is still stuck on.

title: Caramelized Bananas
servingSize: 4 banana quarters with half the sauce
ingredientLines: 2 bananas, halved crosswise then split lengthwise into quarters
½-1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, to taste
steps: Heat butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, swirling to coat the bottom of the pan.
Add honey or brown sugar and cinnamon. Stir to combine with the butter.
Add the bananas and cook, gently flipping every 1-2 minutes until they are softened and coated with the butter-sugar mixture, about 4-5 minutes in total.
Serve warm.
notes: Use firm but ripe bananas. Overripe bananas may turn to mush when cooking over heat.

title: Caramelized Onion Dip
ingredientLines: ¾ cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt (about 6 ounces)
¼ teaspoon ground white pepper (black pepper is okay, but you may want to use less)
steps: Heat a medium-sized sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and allow it to heat up (about 20-30 seconds).
Add the onion and salt and cook until the onions are caramelized, about 20-30 minutes, stirring every 5-10 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat and set aside to cool.
While the onions caramelize, add the Greek yogurt, mayonnaise, garlic powder, and white pepper to a small mixing bowl. Stir to combine.
Add the cooled caramelized onions to the yogurt mixture and stir to combine.
Serve immediately or refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, up to 7 days. Stir before serving to recombine.
notes: The flavor of this dip improves with time. If possible, make it the day before you plan to serve it. The dip will thicken as it sits in the refrigerator. If needed, add 1-2 tablespoons of water and mix well to thin.
This dip goes well with whole-grain chips (e.g. tortilla chips) or crackers, as well as raw crunchy vegetables such as carrots, celery, cucumbers, bell peppers, broccoli, cauliflower, and snap peas.

title: Carrot and Coriander Soup
ingredientLines: 1 medium Russet or Yukon Gold potato, chopped (about 6-8 ounces)
6 tablespoons chopped cilantro or parsley, divided
steps: Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the carrots, potato, coriander, salt, and cayenne. Cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the broth and water. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the carrots and potatoes are tender, about 20-25 minutes.

Transfer a third of the broth-vegetable mixture to the pitcher of a blender. Remove the plastic piece from the center of the blender lid and place a towel over the hole. Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes, then transfer the mixture to a large heatproof bowl. Repeat with any remaining broth-vegetable mixture.
Return the soup to the pot and place over high heat. Bring to a simmer, then remove from the heat.
Add the lime juice and black pepper. Stir to combine.
Serve warm, topping each serving with 1 tablespoon of the cilantro or parsley.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Carrot and Jicama Salad
ingredientLines: ½ cup shredded or grated carrot (about 1 medium carrot)
steps: In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the lime juice, oil, and honey.
Add the jicama, carrot, and cilantro. Toss to combine and coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving.

title: Carrot and Raisin Slaw
ingredientLines: ¼ cup orange juice (about 1 medium orange)
2 cups grated or shredded carrots (about 4 medium carrots)
steps: Add the orange juice, oil, lemon juice, cinnamon, and salt to a medium mixing or serving bowl. Whisk together to make a dressing.
Add the carrots and raisins. Toss to combine and coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: Use pre-shredded carrots to save time.
For a different flavor, try substituting coriander for the cinnamon.
Try substituting another dried fruit (e.g. cranberries, cherries) for the raisins if desired, chopping if large.

title: Carrot Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Grease a 12-cup muffin tin with cooking spray.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, whole-wheat flour, oats, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt. Stir to combine.
In a separate medium mixing bowl, whisk together the sugar, yogurt, oil, eggs, and vanilla.
Add the yogurt mixture and the carrots to the flour mixture. Gently fold to combine.
Divide the batter between the prepared muffin tin cups, filling each about three-quarters of the way full.
Bake for 22-25 minutes. Press down gently on the top of one of the muffins to test for doneness. If it springs back up, the muffins are done.
Let the muffins sit in the muffin tin for 5 minutes, then remove and allow to cool completely on a cooling rack.
Serve room temperature or warm.
notes: Muffins freeze well for up to 4 months. Simply remove from the freezer and warm in the microwave.

title: Cashew Crunch Salad
ingredientLines: ¼ cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt
6 cups shredded cabbage or coleslaw mix (about one 15-ounce bag)
1 cup thinly sliced or shredded carrot (about 2 medium carrots)
½ cup frozen shelled edamame, thawed or cooked and cooled
8 tablespoons (½ cup) chopped toasted cashews, divided
8 tablespoons (½ cup) crunchy chow mein noodles, divided
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, sugar, vinegar, olive oil, sesame oil, salt, and black pepper.
Add the cabbage or coleslaw mix, carrot, and edamame. Toss to combine.
Serve cold, adding 2 tablespoons of the cashews and 2 tablespoons of the chow mein noodles to each portion right before serving.

title: Cauliflower Fried Rice
ingredientLines: 1 (12-ounce) bag frozen riced cauliflower (or about 3 cups fresh riced cauliflower)
1 cup fresh or frozen vegetables, trimmed and chopped as needed (one type or a combination; e.g. carrots, onions, green beans, peas, broccoli)
steps: Spray a large skillet or sauté pan with cooking spray and place over medium heat.
Add the eggs and cook to scrambled, stirring often. Transfer the scrambled eggs to a small bowl and set aside.
Increase the heat to medium-high and add the oil. Heat until shimmering.
Add the riced cauliflower and cook until most of the liquid from the cauliflower is evaporated, about 4-6 minutes.
Add the selected vegetables, scallions, and garlic.
Cook, stirring often, until the liquid is evaporated and the vegetables are not releasing liquid, about 7-10 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, sesame seeds, and scrambled eggs.
Cook, stirring constantly, until the soy sauce is absorbed, about 1-2 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: A partial package of frozen mixed vegetables works well for this recipe, but its also a great way to use up any leftover vegetables in your refrigerator.
You can also use a mixture of cooked rice and riced cauliflower.

title: Cauliflower-Quinoa Meatballs
ingredientLines: 3 cups cauliflower florets (about 1 medium head of cauliflower)
steps: In a medium cooking pot, bring water to a boil, add cauliflower florets and boil for about 5 minutes (until fork- tender). Drain well.
In a food processor, pulse the quinoa and cauliflower until semi-smooth. Transfer mixture to a large mixing bowl.
Add breadcrumbs, eggs, chili powder, paprika, cumin, and salt and mix well.
Roll into small balls, about the size of 2 tablespoons.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add olive oil and heat until shimmering.
Working in batches, add the meatballs to the skillet allowing enough room to turn the meatballs.
Cook for a 2-3 minutes on each side, gently turning the meatballs until equally browned on all sides.
Repeat until all meatballs are cooked. Serve warm.
notes: Instead of pan-frying, these meatballs may be baked at 350°F for 20 minutes, rotating half way through cooking.
Substitute brown rice for the quinoa if desired.
credit: Adapted from pinchofyum.com | Submitted by Alexa Grant, RDN, LDN

title: Cherry-Peach Fruit Compote
steps: Add the peaches and cherries to a medium saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to medium-low to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cook until the fruit mixture is warm and syrupy, stirring occasionally, about 10-12 minutes.
Serve warm or cold over Greek yogurt, pancakes, or oatmeal.
notes: Substitute any other unsweetened fruit for the peaches or cherries as desired. Consider one of these flavor combinations: peach and raspberry, strawberry and rhubarb, or mixed berries.

This recipe can be prepared in the microwave. Microwave the fruit in a microwave-safe bowl at high power (default setting) for 2 minutes, then stir. Continue to microwave in 1-minute increments, stirring after each minute, until the fruit is syrupy.
Refrigerate any leftovers for 5-7 days.

title: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry
servingSize: 1½ cups chicken-vegetable mixture over ½ cup rice
ingredientLines: 2 tablespoons grated fresh ginger (or 1 teaspoon ground dried ginger)
1 pound (16 ounces) boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
4 cups of fresh or frozen stir-fry vegetables, trimmed and chopped as needed (e.g. asparagus, broccoli, carrots, mushrooms, onions, peppers, zucchini, snap peas, cabbage)
2 cups cooked brown rice, warmed if needed
steps: In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, water, cornstarch, vinegar, honey, ginger, garlic to create a sauce. Set aside.
Heat a medium skillet over medium heat.
Add 1 tablespoon of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken and cook until cooked through (internal temperature of 165°F), about 5-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from pan and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil to the pan and heat until shimmering.
Add the vegetables and cook, stirring often, until fork-tender but still firm, about 6-10 minutes.
Add the sauce and cook, stirring often, until the sauce is heated through and slightly thickened, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the cooked chicken and stir to combine.
Serve warm over the cooked brown rice.
notes: Add ½ cup chopped fresh or canned pineapple with the sauce for a sweet twist.

title: Chicken Cauliflower Enchilada Skillet
ingredientLines: 1 can (10-ounce) diced tomatoes and green chilies, undrained
½ cup shredded cheddar and Monterey jack blend cheese
steps: Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the ground chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Add the diced tomatoes and their juice, tomato sauce, enchilada sauce, and cauliflower rice.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the cauliflower is tender.
Reduce the heat to low and stir in the cheese until melted and well mixed.
Serve warm.
notes: If you make your own cauliflower rice, 10-12 ounces cauliflower rice is equivalent to about 2½-3 cups.
Ground chicken not available? Try substituting ground turkey.
credit: Inspired by a recipe submitted by Kimberly George, MS, RD, CDN, Syracuse VAMC

title: Chicken Chow Mein
ingredientLines: ½ pound (8 ounces) boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized strips
½ medium onion, thinly sliced (about ½ cup)
2 stalks celery, thinly sliced on the bias (diagonal; about 1 cup)
3 white or cremini mushrooms, thinly sliced (about ½ cup)
1 (8-ounce) can bamboo shoots, drained and rinsed
1 (8-ounce) can sliced water chestnuts, drained and rinsed
½ cup crunchy chow mein noodles, divided
steps: Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring often, until cooked through (internal temperature of 165°F), about 6-8 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
Set the pan back over medium heat. Add the onion, celery, and mushrooms. Cook until softened, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the cabbage, broth, bamboo shoots, and water chestnuts. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook until the cabbage is tender, about 5-7 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together the cornstarch and water with a fork to make a slurry.
Add the slurry, sugar, and black pepper to the vegetable mixture. Stir to combine.
Cook until a slightly thickened sauce forms, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir to combine.
Serve warm, topping each serving with ¼ cup of the chow mein noodles.
notes: Tofu can be used in place of the chicken, if desired.
Try substituting bok choy for the Napa cabbage.

title: Chicken Couscous Paella
ingredientLines: ½ teaspoon fennel seed or dill
½ pound cooked chicken breast, cubed
steps: Heat a skillet or sauté pan over medium-low heat.
Coat the pan with cooking spray.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 4-5 minutes.
Add the garlic, peas, celery, bell pepper, thyme, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, and paprika.
Cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes and broth.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the couscous.
Cover the pan with a lid and remove from heat. Let stand for about 5 minutes.
Stir in the chicken and cook until heated through.
Fluff with a fork, then serve warm.
notes: For seafood paella, substitute 4 ounces shrimp and 4 ounces scallops for the chicken breast.
credit: Submitted by Sean Walsh RD, CSC, Ioannis A. Lougaris VAMC

title: Chicken Fajitas
ingredientLines: ½ pound (8 ounces) boneless skinless chicken breasts, sliced into thin strips
½ cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt
½ cup salsa or Pico de Gallo (homemade or store-bought)
steps: In a medium mixing bowl, mix together the garlic powder, chili powder, cumin, and cayenne.
Add the raw chicken and toss to coat with the spice mixture.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add ½ tablespoon of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken. Cook, stirring often, until the chicken is fully cooked and no longer pink, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pan and place on a clean plate. Cover the plate with foil and set aside.
Return the pan to the stovetop and turn the heat up to high.
Add the remaining ½ tablespoon oil.
Add the onion and bell pepper. Cook, stirring often, until crisp-tender, about 3-5 minutes.
Divide the chicken, onion-pepper mixture, tomato, avocado Greek yogurt, and salsa over the tortillas.
Serve warm.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16-ounces) boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite sized pieces
1 tablespoon fresh ginger, grated (or ½ teaspoon ground ginger)
1 cup (½ can) lite coconut milk or 6oz plain Greek yogurt
steps: Stove-Top: Heat medium sized pot over medium high heat. Add 1 tablespoon oil. Once hot, add chicken and sauté for 5 minutes. Add ginger, garlic, spices and salt. Sauté for another 5 minutes. Add the tomato sauce. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the coconut milk or yogurt. Serve warm.

Instant Pot/Electric Pressure Cooker: Set to sauté mode. Add oil. Once hot, add chicken. Sauté for 5 minutes. Add ginger, garlic, spices and salt. Sauté for another 5 minutes. Add tomato sauce and stir to combine. Set to manual pressure cook for 10 minutes, then quick release. Stir in coconut milk or yogurt. Serve warm.

Slow Cooker/Crockpot: Omit oil. Add chicken, ginger, garlic, spices, salt and tomato sauce to crockpot. Cook on high for 4 hours or low for 8 hours. Turn off, add coconut milk or yogurt. Stir to combine. Serve warm.
notes: Serve over whole grain rice or with naan bread and a fresh salad.
Omit added salt to reduce sodium content.
credit: Submitted by Robin LaCroix RD, CSO

title: Chicken Tortellini Soup
ingredientLines: 1 (10-ounce) package frozen chopped kale (spinach and/or string beans work well too)
steps: In a Dutch oven over medium heat, combine stock, tomatoes, kale, Italian seasoning, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer.
Cook uncovered for 10 minutes.
Add pasta and chicken.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer.
Cook covered until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Top with cheese and serve.
notes: Additional fresh or frozen vegetables may be added in step 1 if desired.
Sodium content varies based on the type of chicken broth you use.
credit: Submitted by Robin LaCroix

title: Chickpea Shakshuka
ingredientLines: 1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added chickpeas (garbanzo beans), drained and rinsed
steps: Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and garlic.
Sauté, stirring frequently, until the onion and peppers are soft, about 4-5 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes and their liquid, paprika, cumin, chili powder, and cinnamon. Stir to combine.
Increase the heat to high and bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat back to medium.
Continue cooking for 2-3 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the chickpeas and stir to combine.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 15-20 minutes to allow the flavors to blend.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve warm.
credit: Adapted from minimalistbaker.com | Submitted by Georgina Hignell RD

title: Chickpea Stir-Fry
ingredientLines: 2 tablespoons white vinegar or rice vinegar
1 (15.5-ounce) can chickpeas (garbanzo beans), drained and rinsed
steps: Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil, garlic powder, vinegar, soy sauce, and flour. Whisk together to create a sauce.
Cook, while whisking, until the sauce thickens.
Add the chickpeas, stir-fry vegetables, pineapple, and water chestnuts.
Continue to cook until warmed through and the vegetables are tender.
credit: Inspired by a recipe submitted by Diane M. Longerbone MA, RD, CD

title: Chocolate Chip Cheesecake Bars
ingredientLines: ⅓ cup graham cracker crumbs (from about 3 full crackers)
4 ounces reduced-fat cream cheese (Neufchatel), softened to room temperature
⅓ cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line the bottom and sides of a 7x4-inch rectangle baking pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang of the paper on all sides. Set aside.
Add the graham cracker crumbs and melted butter to a small mixing bowl. Stir to combine.
Press the crumb mixture into the bottom of the prepared pan and bake for 8 minutes. Set aside, leaving the oven on.
In a medium mixing bowl, use an electric mixer to beat together the cream cheese, yogurt, egg white, sugar, flour, lemon juice, and vanilla until smooth, about 3-4 minutes.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Pour the mixture into the pan with the crust and bake for 25 minutes, covering the pan with foil after 20 minutes.
Allow to cool at room temperature for 20 minutes, then set in the refrigerator to chill completely, at least 3 hours.
Lift out of the pan by the paper and slice into bars. Serve.
notes: Store the cheesecake bars in a covered container in the refrigerator, up to 7 days.
These cheesecake bars can be frozen up to 3 months. Thaw them overnight in the refrigerator before serving.

title: Chocolate Chip Chickpea Cookie Dough
ingredientLines: ½ cup semisweet or dark chocolate chips (mini chips work best)
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added garbanzo beans (chickpeas), drained and rinsed
2 tablespoons sugar-based sweetener (e.g. agave, honey, maple syrup)
steps: Add the chocolate chips to a medium mixing bowl and set aside.
Add the garbanzo beans, peanut butter, selected sweetener, and vanilla to a food processor. Pulse to chop and then blend until completely smooth, about 3-5 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to the bowl with the chocolate chips and fold to combine.
