Use a 2-tablespoon disher (spring-loaded cookie scoop) to portion the dough out.
Serve right away, or chill before serving.
notes: Try substituting another nut or seed butter for the peanut butter.
Try substituting chopped nuts or dried fruit for half or all of the chocolate chips.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months. If frozen, be sure to thaw slightly (about 10 minutes at room temperature) before eating.

title: Chocolate Chip Pumpkin Muffins
ingredientLines: 1 teaspoon pumpkin pie spice or ground cinnamon
1¼ cups pumpkin puree (about three-quarters of a 15-ounce can)
⅓ cup 2% fat plain Greek yogurt (can substitute nonfat if desired)
¼ cup mini semi-sweet or dark chocolate chips
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Prepare a 12-cup (regular-size) muffin tin or mini muffin tin by spraying each cup with nonstick spray. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the whole-wheat flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and pumpkin pie spice or cinnamon. Set aside.
In a separate medium mixing bowl, whisk together the pumpkin puree, sugar, eggs, oil, and yogurt.
Add the flour mixture to the pumpkin mixture, along with the chocolate chips. Fold together gently until just combined.
Fill the muffin tin cups three-quarters-full with the batter.
Bake until the muffins bounce back when gently pressed, about 20-22 minutes for regular-size muffins or 13-15 minutes for mini muffins.
Cool slightly, about 5 minutes, then remove from tin. Serve warm or place in an airtight container when completely cool. Keep at room temperature for 5-7 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months.
credit: Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Chocolate-Hazelnut Truffles
ingredientLines: ½ cup toasted hazelnuts (filberts) or almonds
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added garbanzo beans (chickpeas), drained and rinsed
steps: Add the oats and hazelnuts or almonds to the bowl of a food processor. Pulse or blend on low until finely ground into a powder.
Add the beans, chocolate-hazelnut spread, and vanilla extract. Pulse to chop the beans into small pieces.
Blend until the mixture resembles a thick dough, about 4-6 minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.
Line a baking sheet or casserole dish with parchment paper or wax paper, then place it next to the food processor.
Carefully remove the blade from the food processor, then use a 2-tablespoon disher (spring-loaded cookie scoop) to portion the mixture onto the baking sheet.
Use clean hands to gently roll each portion into a ball.
Place the truffles in the refrigerator to chill, at least 1 hour and up to overnight.
Serve cold or at room temperature.
notes: For a stronger chocolate flavor, roll the truffles in unsweetened cocoa powder before chilling.
These truffles will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days, or in the freezer for up to 6 months.

title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Smoothie
steps: Set up your blender. You can use an immersion blender standing blender or single cup blender.
Place dried date in a small dish and cover with hot water. Let sit a few minutes or microwave for 40 seconds. Drain water.
Place ice, milk, date, sliced banana, cocoa powder and peanut butter in the blender.
Cover and blend on high speed for about 1 minute, until well blended.
Pour into a glass and enjoy!
notes: If you do not have dates, substitute 1 teaspoon of maple syrup.
Substitute any nut or seed butter for the peanut butter if desired.
Substitute your favorite non-dairy milk. If you are using a sweetened milk, consider omitting the added sweetener.
credit: Adapted from minimalistbaker.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Chocolate-Raspberry Banana Sorbet
ingredientLines: 2 frozen medium bananas, peeled and sliced before freezing
steps: Add the bananas, raspberries, and milk to a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth and creamy, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.
Add the cocoa powder and chocolate chips. Blend to combine.
Serve immediately for a soft-serve texture. For a firmer texture, put it in the freezer for 2-3 hours, stirring every 20-30 minutes.
notes: Blending the frozen bananas will take a few minutes. It will be very loud, similar to adding ice cubes to a blender. Within a few minutes though, you should be seeing a thick, creamy ice-cream-like mixture in the blender.
Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk if desired.

title: Chocolate Zucchini Muffins
ingredientLines: ½ cup plain yogurt (regular or Greek)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin with cooking spray and set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, cinnamon, baking soda, salt, and baking powder.
In a separate medium mixing bowl, whisk together the eggs, yogurt, oil, and sugar.
Add the yogurt mixture, zucchini, and chocolate chips to the flour mixture. Gently fold to combine.
Divide the batter between the prepared muffin tin cups, filling each about three-quarters of the way full.
Bake for 22-25 minutes. Press down gently on the top of one of the muffins to test for doneness. If it springs back up, the muffins are done.
Let the muffins sit in the muffin tin for 5 minutes, then remove and allow to cool completely on a cooling rack.
Serve room temperature or warm.
notes: For traditional zucchini muffins, omit the cocoa powder and chocolate chips.
Substitute dried fruit (chopped if large) or chopped toasted nuts for the chocolate chips, if desired.

title: Cinnamon-Banana Overnight Oats
ingredientLines: ½-¾ cup lowfat (1%) milk, adding more for a thinner consistency if desired
1-3 teaspoons sweetener (e.g. maple syrup, brown sugar, honey), to taste
steps: Add the banana to a pint-sized jar or other container with a lid. Mash with a fork.
Add the oats, milk, hemp seeds, selected sweetener, and cinnamon. Stir with the fork to combine.
Place in the refrigerator and chill overnight, or at least 5 hours.
Serve cold, or warm briefly in the microwave before serving.
notes: Ground flaxseed (flax meal) or chia seeds can be substituted for the hemp seeds, if desired. If making this change, increase the milk by ¼ cup.
After the overnight soak, try sprinkling on some chopped toasted nuts for additional texture and flavor.
Overnight oats will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Make multiple batches for an easy breakfast option throughout the week.

title: Cinnamon-Glazed Baby Carrots
ingredientLines: 4 cups baby carrots, cut in half lengthwise (about 2 pounds)
½-¾ teaspoon ground cinnamon, to taste
steps: Place the carrots in a medium or large saucepan and add enough water to just cover the carrots.
Cover the pot with a lid and bring the water to a boil. Then reduce the heat to medium-low to maintain a simmer.
Cook until the carrots are easily pierced with a fork, about 7-9 minutes.
Drain the carrots into a colander (strainer) and set aside.
Return the pot to the stovetop over medium heat.
Add the butter, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt. Cook, stirring constantly, until the butter and sugar melt to make a sauce, about 1-2 minutes.
Return the carrots to the pot with the sauce mixture.
Cook, stirring often, until the carrots are coated and the sauce is slightly thickened, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: This recipe goes well with most meat, poultry, and seafood main dishes.
If you don’t have baby carrots you can substitute sliced carrots.

title: Cinnamon-Walnut Overnight Oats
steps: In a mason jar or single-serving storage container, stir together the oats, milk, chia seeds, and cinnamon.
Add the fruit and walnuts.
Cover with a lid and refrigerate at least 8 hours, or overnight.
In the morning, grab and go or heat in the microwave for 1-2 minutes if desired.
notes: If you can’t have regular milk, substitute a non-dairy alternative like soy or almond milk.
Try hemp seeds or ground flax seed instead of chia seeds.
Add ¼ cup dried fruit such as raisins or craisins instead of fresh fruit.
Swap slivered almonds or other chopped nuts for the walnuts.
For more crunch, add the walnuts in the morning before serving.
credit: Submitted by Janelle York, MS, RD

title: Citrus-Tomato Fish over Quinoa
servingSize: 6 ounces fish with a quarter of the quinoa and the citrus-tomato mixture
ingredientLines: 2 cups (16 ounces) low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth
½-inch piece ginger, peeled and minced or grated (about ½ teaspoon ginger paste, or a pinch of ground dried ginger)
1 pint grape or cherry tomatoes, halved (about 2 cups)
1 orange, peeled, sectioned, and cut into small chunks
steps: Add the quinoa and broth to a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cover with a lid and cook until the quinoa is fluffy and tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat a medium nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 1 tablespoon of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 30-60 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and ¼ teaspoon of the salt. Cook, stirring often, until they start to break down, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the orange pieces and cook, stirring often, until heated through, about 1-2 minutes.
Transfer the citrus-tomato mixture to a plate or bowl and cover to keep warm. Place the pan back over the heat.
Pat the fish dry with paper towels. Sprinkle the remaining ¼ teaspoon salt and the black pepper on both sides.
Add 1 tablespoon oil to the pan and heat until shimmering.
Place the fish in the pan. Heat until fish is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, about 2-4 minutes per side.
Portion the quinoa, fish, and citrus-tomato mixture into four dishes, then serve warm.

title: Colorful Quinoa Salad
ingredientLines: Zest and juice from 1 orange (about 1 tablespoon zest and about ¼ cup juice)
2 cups fresh spinach or arugula, chopped
4 scallions (green onions), thinly sliced (about ½ cup)
steps: Add the quinoa and broth to a medium saucepan.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-low to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the quinoa is tender, about 10-15 minutes.
While the quinoa is cooking, in a large mixing bowl, whisk together the oil, orange zest, orange juice, red wine vinegar, and mustard to make a dressing.
Transfer the cooked quinoa to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine.
Set the quinoa aside to cool for about 5-10 minutes, stirring every 1-2 minutes to allow for quicker cooling.
Add the spinach or arugula, scallions, dried cranberries, parsley, and pecans. Stir to combine.
Add the feta and gently fold to combine.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: Substitute goat cheese for the feta if desired.

title: Confetti Couscous
ingredientLines: 1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Add the water and cumin to a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the couscous and stir to combine.
Cover the pot with a lid and remove it from heat. Let sit until the couscous is tender, about 5 minutes.
While the couscous cooks, add the oil and lime juice to a large mixing bowl and whisk together to make a dressing. Add the onion and cilantro. Stir to combine, then set aside.
Fluff the cooked couscous with a fork, then stir in the corn.
Place the lid back on the pot and let sit until the corn is thawed, about 3-5 minutes.
Combine the dressing-onion mixture with the couscous and corn mixture. Add the bell pepper, cucumber, and beans. Toss to combine.
Serve warm, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: Substitute fresh basil or parsley for the cilantro if desired.
Try using quinoa or millet instead of the couscous.

title: Corn and Celery Sauté
steps: Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the butter and heat until melted.
Add the celery and cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes.
Stir in the corn and continue cooking until the celery is tender and the corn is cooked or thawed, about 5 minutes.
Add the salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
notes: Add 1 teaspoon minced garlic (about 2 cloves) with the celery, if desired.

title: Country Lentil Soup
ingredientLines: 1 cup uncooked brown lentils, picked through to remove any stones and rinsed
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) chopped fresh parsley, divided
steps: Warm a large saucepan or pot over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, celery, carrots, and garlic. Cook until softened, about 5-8 minutes.
Add the oregano, thyme, and black pepper. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the broth, water, lentils, and tomatoes with their juice.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the lentils are tender, about 20-30 minutes.
Divide the soup between four serving bowls and top each with 1 tablespoon of the parsley.
Serve warm.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Cranberry-Almond Breakfast Quinoa
steps: Add the quinoa, water, and milk to a small saucepan over high heat.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low.
Add the cinnamon and vanilla.
Cover the pot with a lid and simmer until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Stir in the cranberries and almonds and serve warm, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: For a sweeter flavor, add 1-3 teaspoons of honey or maple syrup to taste.
Consider using other dried fruit such as raisins or chopped apricots in place of the dried cranberries.
Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk if desired.

title: Cranberry-Glazed Turkey Meatballs
ingredientLines: 1 pound lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher)
1 (14-ounce) can whole berry cranberry sauce (or 1½ cups homemade cranberry sauce)
½ cup low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
In a medium mixing bowl, gently toss together the ground turkey, egg, oats, onion, milk, garlic powder, thyme, salt, pepper, and lemon zest (if using).
Use 2-tablespoon cookie scoop (disher) to divide the mixture up and roll into balls. Place the meatballs onto a baking sheet.
Bake the meatballs until they reach an internal temperature of 165°F, about 25-30 minutes.
While the meatballs are cooking, add the glaze ingredients to a small saucepan (pot).

Place the pot over medium-high heat, bring to a rapid simmer, and stir as needed until the glaze is slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes. Keep warm over low heat until the meatballs are done cooking,
Toss the meatballs with the glaze and serve, or place the glazed meatballs in a slow cooker set to warm and serve from the slow cooker.

title: Cranberry-Orange Banana Sorbet
ingredientLines: 2 frozen medium bananas, peeled and sliced before freezing
¼ teaspoon grated fresh ginger (or a pinch of ground dried ginger; optional
steps: Add the bananas, cranberries, orange juice, milk, and ginger (if using) to a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth and creamy, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.
Serve immediately for a soft-serve texture. For a firmer texture, put it in the freezer for 2-3 hours, stirring every 20-30 minutes.
notes: Swap out your favorite fruit combinations. Instead of the cranberries try raspberries, peaches, or strawberries for a different tasty treat.
Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk if desired.

title: Cranberry-Orange Smoothie
ingredientLines: 1 small (or ½ large) fresh or frozen banana
⅓ cup fresh or frozen cranberries
¼ teaspoon fresh grated ginger or pinch of dried ginger (optional)
3-5 ice cubes (optional; recommended if not using frozen fruit)
steps: Pour the milk and orange juice into the pitcher of a blender.
Add the banana, cranberries, carrots, cinnamon, ginger (if using), and ice cubes (if using).
Blend until smooth and fully combined, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve immediately.
notes: If you can’t find cranberries, raspberries make a good substitute.
For additional protein, try adding 1-2 scoops protein powder, 1-2 teaspoons chia seeds or hemp hearts, 1 teaspoon ground flaxseed (flax meal), ¼-½ cup Greek yogurt, or ¼-½ cup cottage cheese.
Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk if desired.

title: Cranberry-Rosemary Sparkler
ingredientLines: ¼ cup whole fresh or frozen cranberries, thawed if frozen
⅔ cup soda water or seltzer (flavored or unflavored), chilled
Optional garnish: Whole cranberries, rosemary sprig
steps: Add the cranberries, rosemary, and sugar or agave to a liquid measuring cup.
Using a muddler or the handle of a wooden mixing spoon, smash the cranberries and rosemary until they are broken down and juicy.
Add the soda water and ice. Gently stir to combine.
Pour the cranberry-soda water mixture through a strainer into a drinking glass.
Serve right away, garnishing with cranberries or rosemary if desired.

title: Cream of Celery Soup
ingredientLines: 1 large Russet potato, peeled and diced (about 8-10 ounces)
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) chopped fresh parsley, or celery leaves divided
steps: Heat a large pot over medium heat. Add the oil and butter. Heat until the butter is melted and the oil is shimmering.
Add the celery, potatoes, onion, sage, salt, and black pepper. Stir to combine. Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the celery and onion are softened, about 13-15 minutes.
Remove the lid and add the garlic and lemon zest. Cook while stirring for 1 minute.
Add the broth and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer. Cook uncovered until the potatoes are tender, about 15-20 minutes.

Working in batches, transfer the broth-vegetable mixture to the pitcher of a blender. Remove the plastic piece from the center of the blender lid and place a towel over the hole. Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes, then transfer the mixture to a large heatproof bowl.
Return the pureed mixture to the pot and stir in the lemon juice. Reheat over the stovetop if needed.
Serve warm, topping each serving with 1 tablespoon of the parsley or celery leaves.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Creamless Creamy Tomato Soup
ingredientLines: 3 slices whole-wheat sandwich bread, torn into 1-inch pieces
2 cups (16 ounces) low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
¼ cup chopped fresh chives or basil
steps: Heat a large pot over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, garlic, and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook, stirring frequently, until the onion is softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes with their juice and the bread. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the bread is completely saturated and starts to break down, about 3-5 minutes.

Transfer half the tomato mixture to the pitcher of a blender, along with 1 tablespoon of the oil. Remove the plastic piece from the center of the blender lid and place a towel over the hole. Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes, then transfer the mixture to a large heatproof bowl.
Repeat step 5 with the remaining tomato mixture and 1 tablespoon of oil.
Return all of the blended tomato mixture to the pot. Stir in the broth, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a boil over high heat, then remove the pot from the heat.
Serve warm, topped with the chives or basil as desired.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Creamy Herb Dip
ingredientLines: ½ teaspoon dried basil (or 1 teaspoon fresh basil)
steps: Add the milk, cottage cheese, parsley, chives, basil, curry powder, and garlic to a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth, about 1-2 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: This dip goes will with crisp raw vegetables, whole-grain crackers, pretzels, or pita chips.
Adjust the consistency with more or less milk, as desired.

title: Creamy Potato Salad
ingredientLines: 1½ pounds Yukon Gold or red potatoes (about 4-5 medium potatoes or about 10-12 baby potatoes), unpeeled and cut into ½-inch chunks
⅓ cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt
1 tablespoon white wine vinegar or lemon juice
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
steps: Place a steamer basket inside a large saucepan or stockpot and add just enough water fill the area under the steamer.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-high to maintain a rapid simmer.

Add the potatoes to the steamer basket, cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid, and cook until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 10-15 minutes. Remove the potatoes from the steamer basket and allow to cool completely.

While the potatoes are cooking, place the eggs in a separate medium saucepan. Add enough water to just cover the eggs. Bring to a boil, then turn off the heat and move the pot to a cool burner. Cover the pot with a lid and let sit for 12-15 minutes.
Remove eggs from the pot and place into a bowl of ice-water. Let sit at least 5 minutes, then peel and chop.
In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar or lemon juice, salt, and black pepper.
Gently fold in the potatoes, eggs, peas, and chives.
Cover the bowl with a lid or plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, then serve cold.

title: Creamy Roasted Cauliflower Soup
ingredientLines: 2 pounds cauliflower (about 2 small to medium heads or 1 large head), cut into bite-size florets
1-2 tablespoons lemon juice, to taste (about ½ lemon)
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) finely chopped fresh flat-leaf (Italian) parsley, chives, or scallion (green onion), divided
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the cauliflower with 2 tablespoons of the oil to coat, then sprinkle with ¼ teaspoon of the salt. Arrange the cauliflower in a single layer on a rimmed baking sheet.
Bake until the cauliflower is tender and browned on the edges, about 35-40 minutes, stirring after 20 minutes.
When there is about 10 minutes left on the cauliflower, heat a Dutch oven or large pot over medium heat. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and ¼ teaspoon of the salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds, then add the broth and cauliflower.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20 minutes.
Add the butter, lemon juice, nutmeg, and remaining ¼ teaspoon salt. Blend until smooth using an immersion (handheld) blender.
Garnish each serving with 1 tablespoon of the parsley, chives, or scallion and serve warm.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Creamy Spinach and Pepper Polenta
ingredientLines: ⅓ cup uncooked coarse-grain polenta or corn grits
½ cup frozen chopped spinach, thawed
½ cup frozen chopped bell pepper, thawed
steps: Add the polenta or grits, water, and salt to a medium saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, whisking occasionally to break up any lumps, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered until the mixture is thick and pulling away from the sides of the pan, about 20-30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the spinach, bell pepper, butter, and parmesan. Stir to combine.
Continue cooking until heated through, about 2-4 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: Cooked vegetables can be used in place of the thawed frozen spinach and/or bell pepper, if desired. Consider using another vegetable such as mushrooms, onions, asparagus, or broccoli.
Store in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or in the freezer for up to 6 months.

title: Creamy Tomato Chicken Skillet
servingSize: 4 ounces chicken with ⅓ cup sauce
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) boneless, skinless chicken breasts
steps: In a small bowl, combine the cumin, paprika, oregano, cayenne (if using), salt, and pepper.
Pat the chicken breast dry with a paper towel and rub with the spice blend on all sides.
Heat medium skillet over medium heat.
Add oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the seasoned chicken breast and cook 5-7 minutes on each side, until cooked through and the internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Add the diced tomatoes and cook until heated through.
Stir in the coconut milk and heat for 2-3 more minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: Dairy or unsweetened non-dairy milk can be used in place of coconut milk.
Substitute chicken thighs for the chicken breasts if desired.
credit: Adapted from diethood.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Crispy Baked Cod
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Spray a baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray or line with parchment paper and set aside.
Pat the cod dry with paper towels.
Crack the egg into a shallow dish and beat lightly with a fork. Set aside.
In another shallow dish, combine the cornmeal, flour, parmesan, garlic powder, paprika, dill, and black pepper. Set aside.
One fillet at a time, dip the cod in the beaten egg and then dip in the cornmeal mixture, covering both sides. Shake off any excess coating and lay the breaded cod on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake until the cod flakes easily with a fork and is golden-brown (minimal internal temperature of 145°F), about 10-15 minutes.
Serve right away.
notes: Substitute other mild flavored white fish for the cod if desired.

title: Crispy Garlic-Ginger Tofu
ingredientLines: ¼ cup low sodium soy sauce
2 cloves garlic, minced (or ¼ teaspoon garlic powder)
1 tablespoon rice vinegar or white vinegar
steps: Press the tofu: Line a plate with a paper towel and place tofu on plate. Set another large plate on top of the tofu and weigh it down with a heavy object (such as a large can of vegetables). Allow to press for 15-30 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl make the garlic-ginger sauce by combining the soy sauce, garlic, honey, water, ginger, vinegar and 1 teaspoon cornstarch. Whisk until well combined and set aside.
Cut pressed tofu into 1-inch cubes.
In a bowl, sprinkle tofu with 2 tablespoons of cornstarch and toss until coated.
Heat large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add oil and heat until shimmering.
Add tofu to skillet and brown on all sides.
Stir in garlic-ginger sauce (sauce will begin to thicken).
Toss tofu to coat in sauce, stir until crispy and remove from heat. Serve warm.
notes: Leftovers will keep refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
credit: Adapted from tablefortwo | Submitted by Alexa Grant, RDN, LDN

title: Crispy Lemon Fish
ingredientLines: 10-12 ounces white fish fillets, (e.g. cod, haddock, tilapia)
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a medium bowl, mix lemon juice, 1 tablespoon olive oil and melted butter. Set aside.
In another medium bowl, mix flour, spices, salt and pepper.
Pat fish dry with paper towels.
Dip fish into the lemon mixture to coat and then dredge in the flour mixture, covering both sides.
Heat skillet over medium heat and add 1 tablespoon oil.
Add fish filets and cook for 3 minutes on each side (fish will not be cooked through).
Place fish on a baking pan. Drizzle leftover oil and lemon mixture over the fish.
Bake for 8-10 minutes until cooked through and fish flakes easily with a fork.
Remove from the oven and sprinkle with fresh parsley.
notes: Serve over rice with a side of vegetables or salad.
To reduce the sodium content, omit or reduce the salt.
credit: Adapted from themediterraneandish.com| Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Crispy Oven-Fried Chicken
ingredientLines: ¼ cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt
¼-½ teaspoon ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Lightly spray a baking sheet with nonstick spray and set aside.
Add the flour to a plate or shallow dish.
In a separate bowl or shallow dish, whisk together the egg, milk, yogurt, and mustard.
Add the cornflakes to a zip-top plastic bag and crush with a rolling pin, meat mallet, or your fist to create crumbs.
Transfer the cornflake crumbs to a medium mixing bowl, along with the black pepper and cayenne. Stir to combine.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels.
Dip the chicken in the flour, coat well, and shake off the excess.
Dip the chicken in the egg mixture, shaking off the excess.
Dip the chicken into the cornflake crumbs, pressing to make the crumbs stick.
Place the chicken on the prepared baking sheet. Bake uncovered until crispy and cooked through (minimum internal temperature of 165°F), about 15-20 minutes.
Serve warm.

title: Crunchy Oat Nut Cookies
ingredientLines: ⅓ cup chopped nuts (one type or a combination; e.g. pecans, walnuts, almonds)
⅓ cup dried fruit (one type or a combination; e.g. raisins, dried cherries, dried cranberries)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, stir together the peanut butter and maple syrup.
Add the baking soda and salt. Stir to combine.
Add the oats, nuts, dried fruit, and chia seeds (if using). Stir to combine.
Using a tablespoon and filling it until it is heaping over, spoon the dough onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 13 minutes.
Let cool slightly, about 5-10 minutes, before serving.
notes: If you don’t have parchment paper, you can coat the baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray.
Another nut butter or a seed butter can be substituted for the peanut butter.
You can substitute ¼ cup chocolate chips for the dried fruit.
Honey can be substituted for the maple syrup if desired.

title: Crunchy Taco Salad
ingredientLines: ½ pound (8 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher; can substitute canned beans)
½ medium cucumber, chopped (about ½ cup)
½ cup corn, cooked and cooled
steps: Heat a medium nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the ground turkey and cook until no longer pink, about 6-8 minutes, breaking it into crumbles as it cooks.
Add the taco seasoning and water. Stir to combine.
Cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes, then remove from the heat and set aside.
Add the lime juice, vinegar, oil, sugar, and cumin to a small jar with a lid. Shake to combine, making a dressing. Set aside.
Divide the lettuce, tomato, cucumber, and corn between two large serving bowls.
Top each bowl with half of the cooked ground turkey.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon of the cheese and half of the crushed tortilla chips over each bowl. Drizzle each bowl with half of the dressing.
Serve immediately.
notes: To make ahead of time, leave the meat, cheese, chips, and dressing separate and add when you are ready to eat.

title: Crunchy Thai Chicken Salad
ingredientLines: 1 (14-ounce) bag slaw mix (about 6 cups shredded cabbage)
1 red or orange bell pepper, thinly sliced (about 1 cup)
2 cups cooked chicken, cubed or shredded
⅓ cup peanut butter or other nut butter
1 ½ tablespoons reduced sodium soy sauce
⅓ cup chopped peanuts or cashews
steps: Place the shredded cabbage or slaw mix in a large bowl.
Add the bell pepper, cooked chicken and cilantro.
In a small bowl or jar with a lid, combine the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, rice vinegar and honey. Whisk or shake until well combined.
Add the sauce to the vegetable and chicken mixture and stir well.
Top with chopped nuts and toss to combine.
Serve cold. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days.
notes: Chicken can be swapped for baked tofu cubes.
credit: Adapted from The Lean Green Bean Blog Adapted Submitted fromby|Robin LaCroix, Submitted by RD, CSO

title: Crustless Quiche Muffins
ingredientLines: 1 cup cooked vegetables, cut into ¼- to ½-inch pieces (one type or a combination; e.g. onion, mushrooms, bell pepper, broccoli, asparagus)
½ cup shredded cheese or cheese blend (e.g. cheddar, mozzarella, Italian style, Mexican style)
⅓ cup chopped or shredded cooked meat (e.g. steak, turkey, chicken, pork)
¼-½ teaspoon ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Prepare a 12-cup (standard size) muffin tin by spraying each cup with nonstick cooking spray. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, toss together the selected cooked vegetables, cheese, and cooked meat (if using)
Divide the vegetable mixture between the muffin tin cups (~2 tablespoons each).
In the same bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, black pepper, and salt.
Divide the egg mixture between the muffin tin cups (~3 tablespoons each).
Bake until the eggs are fully set, about 12-15 minutes.
Let cool completely in the pan, about 7-10 minutes, then carefully remove from the pan. Serve warm.
notes: This recipe can also be prepared in an 8x8-inch baking dish or an 8- to 9-inch pie plate. Increase the cooking time to about 30-45 minutes, cooking until eggs are fully set.
These quiche muffins will keep in the refrigerator for up to 4 days, or in the freezer for up to 2 months.
Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk alternative, if desired.

title: Cucumber-Herb Tzatziki
ingredientLines: ½ cup grated cucumber, squeezed to drain excess liquid
1 tablespoon finely chopped garlic scapes (or 1 clove minced garlic)
steps: Add the grated and drained cucumber to a medium mixing bowl.
Add the yogurt, mint, basil, garlic scapes, lemon juice, oil, and salt.
Stir to combine.
Serve right away, or chill before serving.
notes: Substitute dill for the basil, if desired.
Add as a spread on a sandwich or wrap, serve with whole-wheat pita, or serve with whole-grain crackers.

title: Curried Lentil and Pumpkin Soup
ingredientLines: 1 cup uncooked brown lentils, picked through to remove any stones and rinsed
steps: Heat a large pot over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, garlic, curry powder, ginger, and cayenne. Cook, stirring often, until the onions are softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the broth, brown lentils, and pumpkin puree. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the lentils are tender, about 20-25 minutes.
Serve warm.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Curried Salmon Patties
ingredientLines: ⅓ cup grated onion (about ½ medium onion)
1 (5-ounce) can salmon in water, bones and skin removed if included, drained (can substitute two 2.5-ounce pouches or one 5-ounce pouch)
1 tablespoon lemon or lime juice (about ¼ medium lemon or ½ lime)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or aluminum foil. Coat with nonstick cooking spray, then set aside.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook until lightly browned, about 3-5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the curry powder and black pepper. Cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes, then transfer to a medium mixing bowl.
Add the salmon, oats, mayonnaise, and lemon or lime juice to the bowl and stir to combine.
Divide the mixture into three portions (⅓ cup each). Shape into patties about ½-inch-thick, then place on the prepared baking sheet.
Spray the patties with nonstick cooking spray, then bake until lightly browned, about 12‐15 minutes. Serve warm.
notes: Old-fashioned (rolled) oats can be used, if desired. Grind into small pieces in a blender or food processor.
The patties can also be cooked in the skillet on the stovetop until browned, about 3‐4 minutes on each side.

title: Edamame Salad with Lime Dressing
ingredientLines: 1 (16-ounce) package frozen shelled edamame (green soybeans or mukimame)
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
1 pint cherry or grape tomatoes, quartered
4 scallions (green onions), thinly sliced (about ½ cup)
steps: In a large mixing bowl, make the dressing by whisking together the apple cider vinegar, olive oil, lime juice, sugar, salt, and garlic. Set aside.
Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the edamame to the boiling water and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the frozen corn to the boiling water with the edamame and continue cooking for 1 minute.
Drain the edamame and corn into a colander or strainer.
Add the drained edamame and corn to the bowl with the dressing.
Add the and black beans, tomatoes, and scallions.
Gently toss to combine.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: Omit the cooking in steps 2-4 by thawing the edamame and corn under running water.

title: Egg Drop Cabbage Soup
ingredientLines: ½ medium onion, diced (about ½ cup)
4 cups (32 ounces) low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth
4 cups thinly sliced napa cabbage (about ½ head)
½ teaspoon ground dried ginger (or 2 teaspoons fresh grated ginger)
2 tablespoons thinly sliced scallion (green onions), divided (about 1 scallion)
steps: Heat a large saucepan or stockpot over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the broth, cabbage, ginger, and black pepper. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a low simmer.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the cabbage is tender, about 8-10 minutes.
Remove the lid. Use one hand to stir the soup in a steady circle. While the soup is moving, use the other hand to slowly drizzle in the beaten eggs.
Stir in the sesame oil.
Serve warm, garnishing each portion with ½ tablespoon of the green onions.
notes: Another type of cabbage can be used in place of the Napa cabbage. You may need to cook it a little longer to ensure that it is tender.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Eggs Benedict
servingSize: 1 English muffin half with bacon, egg, and sauce
steps: Fill a medium saucepan with about three inches of water. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer. Add the vinegar to the water.
Crack one egg into a small cup and lower the egg into the simmering water, gently pouring it out of the cup. Repeat with the second egg.
Cook the eggs in the water for 3-5 minutes, depending on how soft you want your egg yolk. Remove the cooked eggs gently, one at a time, with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
In a small microwave-safe bowl, add all ingredients for the hollandaise sauce. Microwave on high power (default setting) until smooth and frothy, about 60 seconds, stopping to whisk every 15 seconds.
Toast the English muffin.
Place the Canadian bacon on a small microwave-safe plate and heat on high power (default setting) for 30 seconds.
Top each English muffin half with one slice of the bacon, one poached egg, and half of the sauce. Serve right away.
notes: Use pasteurized eggs, if available, to reduce risk of foodborne illness from consuming undercooked egg yolks.
credit: Submitted by Melanya Souza, RD, LD/N

title: Fall Quinoa Salad
ingredientLines: 1 apple, diced (e.g. Red Delicious, Gala, Honeycrisp)
1 cup cubed butternut squash, frozen (or may buy fresh and pre-cook ahead of time)
1 tablespoon fresh rosemary, minced (or 1 teaspoon if dried)
steps: Rinse the quinoa in a fine mesh strainer.
Bring 1 cup water to a boil in a medium saucepan (pot), then add the quinoa.
Cover the saucepan with a lid. Reduce the heat to low and cook until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, add the balsamic vinegar and orange juice. Whisk to combine, then set aside.
Heat a sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the Brussels sprouts and sauté until they begin to brown.
Add the apple and butternut squash.
Continue sautéing until all the items are browned, then turn the heat to low.
Add the cooked quinoa, the balsamic-juice mixture, pecans, and rosemary to the sauté pan. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
notes: The apple can be substituted with other fall fruits, such as pomegranate seeds or dried cranberries.
To cook fresh butternut squash: Cut the squash into cubes, toss with oil, then bake at 375°F for about 45 minutes on a lined baking sheet
credit: Adapted from EmilieEats.com | Submitted by Audrey Ferguson, RDN

title: Fennel-Carrot Slaw
ingredientLines: 1 medium fennel bulb, cored and thinly sliced (about 1 cup)
steps: In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the vinegar, mustard, oil, salt, and black pepper.
Add fennel, carrot, and parsley. Toss to combine.
(Optional) Chill for 1 hour for best flavor.
Serve cold.
notes: Add sliced scallions (green onions), if desired.
Substitute another delicate herb (e.g. basil, cilantro, dill) for the parsley, if desired.

title: Festive Green Bean Salad
ingredientLines: ⅓ cup dried cranberries or dried cherries, chopped if large
¼ cup shaved or finely grated parmesan
steps: Place a steamer basket inside a large saucepan or stockpot.
Add water until it reaches just below the bottom of the steamer basket. Set over high heat and bring to a simmer.
While the water in the pot is heating, fill a large mixing bowl halfway with ice and water. Set near the stovetop.
Add the green beans to the steamer basket inside the pot.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the green beans are tender but still crisp, about 4-6 minutes.

Use an oven mitt or hot pad to carefully remove the steamer basket from the pot. Transfer the green beans to the bowl of ice water, then remove and place on paper towels to dry. Pat dry to speed up the process if needed.
Drain and wipe the bowl dry with paper towels. Add the dressing ingredients and whisk to combine.
Add the green beans, chives, almonds, cranberries or cherries, and parmesan. Toss to combine with the dressing.
Serve, warming or chilling before serving desired.
notes: If preparing ahead, keep the dressing and sliced almonds separate. Toss with the salad just before serving

title: Fish-and-Vegetable Foil Packets
servingSize: 1 fish fillet with ⅔ cup vegetables
ingredientLines: 2 small zucchini, sliced thin or diced small (about 2 cups)
2 small yellow summer squash, sliced thin or diced small (about 2 cups)
1 cup halved grape or cherry tomatoes (can substitute 1 cup peeled and chopped tomato)
2 scallions (green onions), thinly sliced (about ½ cup)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh herb (e.g. dill, basil, thyme)
2 tablespoons lemon juice (about ½ lemon) or white wine vinegar
4 (4- to 6-ounce) firm-textured fish fillets or fish steaks (e.g. catfish, cod, halibut, tilapia)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
In a medium mixing bowl, add the zucchini, summer squash, garlic, tomatoes, scallions, fresh herb, lemon juice or vinegar, and garlic. Stir to combine, then set aside.
Lay four pieces of aluminum foil, each about 12x15 inches, on a clean work surface.
Season each fillet lightly on both sides with the salt (if using) and black pepper.
Place one fish fillet in the enter of each piece of foil.
Divide the vegetable mixture over the pieces of fish.

Leaving space inside for steam, create foil packets around the fish and vegetables by folding the long ends of the foil together first, then folding the sides together and turning the side folds upward to reduce the risk of leakage.
Place the foil packets on a baking sheet and bake for 15 minutes. Remove from the oven and let sit for 5 minutes.

Serve right away, carefully opening each packet to avoid touching the release of steam. Transfer the fish and vegetables to plates if desired, spooning the juice from the packets over the top of each serving.
credit: Adapted from the Low-Fat Soul Cookbook | Submitted by Tamara Sugarek

title: Fish Tacos with Strawberry Salsa
ingredientLines: 1 cup finely diced strawberries (about ½ pound)
½ cup finely diced onion (about ½ medium onion)
¼ teaspoon ground black pepper, divided
Optional garnishes: Shredded lettuce or cabbage, avocado, lime wedges
steps: In a medium bowl, make a salsa by stirring together the strawberries, onion, garlic, cilantro, jalapeño, lime juice, salt, and ⅛ teaspoon of the black pepper. Set aside.
In a small bowl, stir together the cumin, paprika, and the remaining ⅛ teaspoon of black pepper. Set aside.
Pat the pollock dry with paper towels.
Brush the pollock with the olive oil, then sprinkle the seasoning mixture over both sides.
Coat the inside of a medium nonstick skillet with cooking spray and place over medium heat.
When the pan is hot, place the pollock in the pan and cook until a crust is formed and the fish lifts easy from the pan, about 2-4 minutes.
Flip the pollock over and continue cooking until cooked through (flakes easily with a fork, internal temperature of 145°F), about 3-5 minutes. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Heat the tortillas in the pan or in the microwave until warm.
Break the fish into bite-sized pieces. Serve on the warmed tortillas, topped with the strawberry salsa and any other desired garnishes.
notes: Try a variety of toppings such as sliced radishes, cotija cheese, or a dollop of Greek yogurt mixed with lime zest.
To reduce calories and carbohydrates, swap a low-carbohydrate tortilla for whole-wheat. You can also look for a lower-sodium version.

title: Fish Tacos with Tangy Slaw
ingredientLines: 2 tablespoons no-salt-added taco seasoning (store-bought or homemade; try the Taco Seasoning recipe on page 78), divided
1 pound (16 ounces) white fish fillets (e.g. cod)
¼ cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt
steps: In a small bowl, combine 1 tablespoon of the taco seasoning, 1 tablespoon of the lime juice, and 1 tablespoon of the oil. Coat the fish fillets with the mixture.
In a separate small bowl, combine the remaining 1 tablespoon of taco seasoning with the yogurt, mayonnaise, and 1 tablespoon of the lime juice. Set aside.

In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the remaining 2 tablespoons lime juice, 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, cilantro, honey or sugar, black pepper, and salt. Add the shredded cabbage and toss to coat. Set aside.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the fish and cook until it is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, about 3-6 minutes per side. Remove the fish from the pan and let it rest for 1-2 minutes.
Break the fish into bite-sized pieces, then divide the pieces of fish and the dressed cabbage over the warmed tortillas.
Serve warm, drizzling with the yogurt mixture to taste.

title: Flax Muffin in a Mug
ingredientLines: 1 packet stevia (¼ teaspoon powdered stevia) or 10 drops liquid stevia (about ½ teaspoon)
½ cup fresh or frozen blueberries (do not thaw if frozen)
steps: Spray the inside of a microwave‐safe mug with nonstick cooking spray. Set aside.
Crack the egg into a small bowl, then gently whisk the yolk and white together with a fork.
Add the flax meal, cinnamon, baking powder, and stevia. Stir with the fork until well combined, then gently stir in the blueberries.
Pour the mixture into the prepared mug, then microwave on high power (default setting) until fully set but not dry, about 1½-2 minutes.
Let cool in the mug for 2-5 minutes, then turn the mug over and gently shake to remove the muffin.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Two teaspoons of a sugar-based sweetener (e.g. white sugar, brown sugar, honey) can be used in place of the stevia, if desired.
This muffin recipe is loaded with fiber and omega-3 fatty acids, making it a quick and filling addition to your breakfast routine or a grab-and-go snack option.

Another fresh or frozen fruit can be substituted for the blueberries, if desired. Some ideas include cubed mango, sliced strawberries, whole blackberries or raspberries, diced peaches, sliced bananas, and chopped apples.

title: Flourless Almond Butter Cookies
ingredientLines: ½ cup semi-sweet mini chocolate chips
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Line two large baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone baking mats and set aside
In a large mixing bowl, add the almond butter, sugar, egg, vanilla extract, and baking soda. Mix together until very well combined.
Add in the chocolate chips and continue mixing until fully combined.
Use a 1-ounce (2-tablespoon) cookie scoop to make balls of cookie dough on the prepared baking sheets, making sure to leave a little room between each one as they spread during baking
Bake at 350°F for 9-11 minutes or until the cookies are set.
Remove from the oven and allow the cookies to cool completely on the baking sheet to firm up.
notes: This recipe is quite nutritious for a cookie; low in carbohydrates, and high in fiber and protein
The fat is high, but is primarily unsaturated and plant-based which can help to improve HDL cholesterol
Store cookies in an airtight container on the counter for up to one week
credit: Adapted from Live Well Bake Often | Submitted by Melanya Souza, RD, LD/N

title: Flourless Black Bean Brownies
ingredientLines: 1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
1 tablespoon milk (dairy or non-dairy milk alternative)
½ teaspoon ground coffee or instant coffee
¾ cup chopped dark chocolate or dark chocolate chips (≥70% cacao), divided
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Coat the inside of an 8x8-inch baking pan with cooking spray and set aside.
Add the beans to the pitcher of a food processor or blender, and pulse until broken down, about 10-15 pulses.
Scrape down the sides and add the eggs. Pulse until well-combined, about 10-15 pulses.
Add the sugar, cocoa powder, milk, vinegar, oil, baking powder, baking soda, coffee, and salt. Pulse or blend on low speed until fully combined.
Transfer the mixture to a mixing bowl and stir in ½ cup of the chocolate.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking pan, spreading it to the edges.
Sprinkle the top with the remaining ¼ cup of chocolate.
Bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean with no batter or crumbs, about 25-30 minutes.
Let cool in the pan for at least 10 minutes.
Cut the brownies into 16 squares and serve.

title: Foil Packet Fish
servingSize: 1 fillet, about 1 cup of vegetables, and 2 tablespoons sauce
ingredientLines: 2, 6oz boneless, skinless, white fish fillets, (e.g. haddock, cod, flounder, tilapia, mahi-mahi)
2 cups vegetables, fresh or frozen (asparagus, bell peppers, onion, thinly sliced carrots, leeks, thinly sliced potato, mushrooms, cherry tomatoes, zucchini or yellow squash)
2 tablespoons fresh parsley or basil (or 1 teaspoon dried)
steps: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Wash and slice or chop the vegetables into ½-inch pieces or thin slices.

Spread out 2 large sheets of tin foil (use heavy duty or double up if foil is thin). Place half of the vegetables in the center of each foil. Sprinkle with salt, pepper and ½ of the herbs. Place each piece of fish over the vegetables. Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Grab the sides of the foil and fold up to meet each other. Fold down to seal. Wrap the other two sides in to form a packet.
Place packets on a baking sheet; bake for 12 to 15 minutes. Remove from oven, open packets carefully, steam will be hot.
In a small dish, mix the yogurt, lime juice and dash of salt. Mix well. Drizzle over fish and vegetables.
credit: Adapted from Melanya Souza, RD, LD/N| Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Fresh Corn and Roasted Red Pepper Salad
ingredientLines: 3 ears corn (on the cob), husks on
1 cup halved grape or cherry tomatoes
½ cup chopped fresh basil (about 3 ounces)
steps: Place one ear of corn, with the husk on, in the microwave and cook on high (default power) for 2 minutes. Carefully remove from the microwave and set aside. Repeat with the remaining ears of corn.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the oil, ⅓ cup of the lemon juice, 1½ teaspoons of the lemon zest, ginger, honey, turmeric, and salt.
Add the cabbage, roasted peppers, peaches, tomatoes, and basil. Toss to combine and set aside.
When the corn is cool enough to handle, remove the husks but leave stalks on. Cut a small slice off the tip of each ear to create a flat surface.
Place a small bowl upside-down inside a larger bowl.
Working one ear at a time, hold the stalk of an ear of corn and place the tip on top of the small bowl. Cutting lengthwise from the stalk to the tip, cut the kernels off the ear of corn.
Mix the corn kernels into cabbage-pepper mixture.
Serve, topping each serving with a quarter of the avocado and 1 tablespoon of the feta.

title: Fresh Green Salad with Lemony Dressing
servingSize: 1¼ cups of salad with 2 tablespoons of dressing
ingredientLines: 6 cups salad greens, chopped if needed
1 cup halved cherry or grape tomatoes
½ cup shredded carrots (about 1 medium carrot)
1 teaspoon Dijon mustard or brown mustard
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, water, mustard, honey, black pepper, and salt (if using) to make a dressing. Set aside.
Wash and dry the salad greens and place them in a large mixing or serving bowl.
Add the tomatoes, cucumber, and carrots.
Add the dressing and toss to coat.
Serve immediately.
notes: This salad tastes best when it is made on the same day it’s served. If not serving right away, keep the dressing separate, then re-whisk the dressing and toss with vegetable mixture just before serving.
Prepare the dressing by shaking the ingredients together in a jar with tight fitting lid if desired.

title: Fresh Herb Chimichurri
ingredientLines: 2 garlic cloves, peeled and left whole
steps: Put the garlic cloves in a food processor and pulse or blend until fully minced, about 30 seconds.
Add the parsley and oregano and pulse until fully chopped, about 30-60 seconds, scraping down the sides as needed.
Add the vinegar, salt, crushed red pepper (if using), and black pepper. Pulse to combine, about 30 seconds.
Transfer the mixture to a serving bowl or storage container.
Pour the oil over the top and gently stir to combine. Set aside for 15-20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Serve at room temperature, or place in the refrigerator until needed.
notes: Serve with grilled meat, seafood, poultry, vegetables, roasted potatoes, or rice.
Will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Any leftovers can be frozen in ice cube trays, then popped out and placed in a plastic zip-top bag in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: Fresh Herb Pesto
ingredientLines: 2 tablespoons toasted nuts or seeds (e.g. pine nuts, walnuts, sunflower seeds)
2 tablespoons grated or shredded parmesan cheese
steps: Add the basil and/or parsley, nuts or seeds, parmesan, oil, lemon juice, garlic, and salt to the bowl of a food processor or blender.
Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed.
Serve right away, or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
notes: If the mixture is too thick, add an additional 1 tablespoon of olive oil and/or lemon juice and continue blending.
Use with pasta or zucchini noodles, add to pizza in place of pizza sauce, or spread on a sandwich.
This pesto will stay fresh in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Any

title: Fruit and Nut Overnight Oats
ingredientLines: ½ cup uncooked old fashioned (rolled) oats
⅛-¼ teaspoon ground cinnamon, to taste
1 cup fresh fruit (e.g. berries, apple, banana), chopped
2 tablespoons unsalted chopped, slivered, or sliced nuts (e.g. almonds, walnuts, pecans)
steps: In a quart-size mason jar or other 4-cup storage container, stir together the oats, milk, chia seeds, and cinnamon.
Add the fruit and nuts.
Cover with a lid and refrigerate overnight, or at least 8 hours.
Serve cold, or heat in the microwave for 1-2 minutes and serve warm.
notes: Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk if desired.
Try hemp seeds or ground flax seed (flax meal) instead of chia seeds.
Add ¼ cup dried fruit, such as raisins or dried cranberries, instead of fresh fruit.
For more crunch, add the nuts just before serving.

title: Fruit Salad with Honey-Yogurt Dressing
ingredientLines: 1 sweet or sweet-tart apple, cored and diced (e.g. Gala, Pink Lady, Delicious, Honeycrisp)
1 mango, pit and peel removed, diced
1 cup strawberries, greens removed and quartered
steps: Whisk together the yogurt and honey in a large bowl to make a dressing.
Add the banana, apple, mango, blueberries, and strawberries to the bowl with the honey-yogurt dressing.
Toss until the fruit is combined and coated with the dressing.
Serve immediately, or chill in the refrigerator until ready to serve. This fruit salad will keep in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
credit: Adapted from TheLemonBowl.com | Submitted by Dana Herring MS, RDN

title: Garden-Fresh Gazpacho
ingredientLines: 1½ pounds ripe medium tomatoes (about 6-10 tomatoes, depending on variety)
1 (5.5-ounce) can tomato juice, added as needed
1 medium cucumber, peeled, seeded, and finely chopped (about 1 cup)
1 medium red bell pepper, finely chopped (about 1 cup)
1 jalapeño, seeds and membranes removed, minced
¼ cup sliced fresh basil leaves
steps: Fill a large pot or saucepan halfway full with water. Set over high heat and bring to a boil.
Meanwhile, prepare a large bowl with ice water and make an X cut with a paring knife on the bottom of each tomato.
Carefully drop the tomatoes into the boiling water and cook for 15 seconds, then remove and transfer to the ice water.
Let tomatoes cool until able to handle, about 1 minute, then remove from the ice water and pat dry.
Peel and seed the tomatoes. To seed the tomatoes, place them in a fine mesh strainer set over a large mixing bowl. Press as much of the juice and pulp through as possible.
Transfer the collected juice and pulp to a liquid measuring cup. Add canned tomato juice to bring the total to 1 cup.
Transfer the tomatoes and juice back to the bowl. Add the cucumber, bell pepper, onion, jalapeño, garlic, lime juice, vinegar, soy sauce or tamari, cumin, salt, and black pepper. Stir to combine.
Transfer 1½ cups of the mixture to a blender and add the olive oil. Blend on high speed until smooth and creamy, about 20-30 seconds.
Return the pureed mixture to the bowl and stir to combine.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours, up to overnight.
Serve cold, garnishing with the basil.
notes: Try adding any leftover tomato pulp and seeds to other dishes such as rice, pasta, or soup.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Garlic Avocado Toast with Fried Egg
ingredientLines: 1 clove garlic, peeled and halved crosswise
steps: Place the bread slices in a toaster, under a broiler, or in a skillet over medium heat. Toast to the desired level of doneness.
Rub the cut side of one of the garlic clove halves on one side of each slice of toasted bread.

Use a spoon to scoop the flesh of the avocado out into a small bowl. Add the lime juice and mash together with a fork. Divide the mixture over the slices of toasted bread and spread to cover one side of each slice. Set aside.
Spray a small or medium skillet with cooking spray and place over medium heat. When the pan is hot, crack the eggs in the pan and cook to desired doneness.
Slide one of the eggs from the skillet onto the top of each slice of avocado toast.
Top each egg with half of the feta, parsley, and black pepper. Serve right away.
notes: Avocados are high in potassium. If you have been instructed to limit your potassium intake, limit the amount of mashed avocado used in this recipe to ¼ cup.
Eggs are an inexpensive source of high-quality protein and one of the lowest phosphorus protein sources.

title: Garlicky Mashed Potatoes
ingredientLines: 2 pounds potatoes, unpeeled (one type or a combination; e.g. Russet, red, Yukon gold)
Optional toppings: pesto, horseradish, caramelized onions, sundried tomatoes, bacon, chives, green onion, cheddar cheese, fried egg
steps: Cut the potatoes in half lengthwise, then cut each of the halves lengthwise again to create quarters. Cut the potatoes crosswise into ½-inch-thick slices.
Add the potatoes to a large pot. Add just enough cold water to cover them.
Cover the pot with a lid and bring the water to a boil over high heat. When the water begins to boil, remove the lid and bring the heat down to a simmer.
Cook the potatoes until they are easily crushed with tongs, about 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, add the half-and-half, garlic, lemon juice or vinegar, and salt to a small saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer over low heat.
Drain the potatoes, then return them to the pot and place the pot back over the heat.
Add the warm half-and-half mixture to the potatoes.
Mash the potatoes until you are happy with the texture. If you are using red potatoes, keep in mind that they will not get completely smooth with mashing.
Serve warm, topping as desired.

title: Gazpacho Dip with Garlic Pita Chips
servingSize: ½ cup dip with 6 pita chips
ingredientLines: 2 Roma tomatoes, finely chopped (about ¾ cup)
2 stalks celery, finely chopped (about ½ cup)
½ cucumber, peeled and finely chopped (about ½ cup)
½ bell pepper, finely chopped (about ½ cup)
½ small onion, finely chopped (about ¼ cup)
¼ cup chopped fresh herbs (e.g. basil, parsley)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Cut each pita round into 6 wedges.
Separate each wedge horizontally into 2 pieces.
Arrange the pita wedges in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Lightly coat the pita wedges with nonstick spray and sprinkle with garlic powder and salt.
Bake until the wedges curl at the edges and begin to brown, about 6-8 minutes. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool.
In a medium mixing bowl, combine the tomato, celery, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, garlic, red wine vinegar, black pepper, and fresh herbs. Stir to combine.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Serve the dip cold with the pita chips.
notes: Pita chips can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. The dip can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 7 days.

title: Ginger Blueberry Crisp
ingredientLines: 3 cups blueberries (fresh or frozen; thawed if frozen)
1-3 teaspoons grated fresh ginger, to taste (or ¼-½ teaspoon ground dried ginger)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Spray an 8x8-inch baking pan lightly with nonstick spray. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the blueberries and ginger. Spread the mixture into the bottom of the prepared baking pan.
In a separate small mixing bowl, add the oats, flour, sugar, butter, and cinnamon. Mix with a fork or pastry blender until the mixture is combined and crumbly.
Sprinkle the oat mixture over the blueberry mixture.
Place the baking dish in the preheated oven and cook until the oat topping is lightly browned and crispy, about 25-30 minutes.
Remove the pan from the oven and let cool at room temperature for at least 20 minutes before serving.
notes: This recipe will work well with other fruits such as apples, pears, cherries, peaches, or mixed berries.
Store any leftovers in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.
If using thawed frozen fruit, adding 1 tablespoon cornstarch to the fruit mixture can help thicken the texture.

title: Grape and Avocado Quinoa Salad
ingredientLines: Zest and juice of 1-2 limes, to taste
1½ cups diced cucumber (about 1 medium cucumber or ½ English cucumber)
4 scallions (green onions), white and light green parts, thinly sliced (about 1 cup)
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the lime zest, lime juice, and olive oil. Set aside.
Combine the rinsed quinoa with the water in a saucepan.
Bring the water to a boil, then cover with a lid and reduce to a simmer.
Cook until all liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Set the cooked quinoa aside to cool, about 10-15 minutes.
In a large bowl, toss the cooled quinoa, grapes, cucumbers, spinach, scallions, and mint together with the dressing.
Season with pepper to taste.
Gently fold in the avocado.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving.
notes: Substitute arugula or chopped kale for the spinach if desired.
This salad can be made 1-2 days before serving, if desired. Just wait to cut and add the avocado until ready to serve.

title: Greek Yogurt with Warm Berry Sauce
servingSize: ½ cup yogurt with a quarter of the sauce
steps: Combine the frozen berries and lime juice in a small saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to medium-low to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cook until a sauce forms and thickens, about 10-12 minutes.
Divide the yogurt into four serving bowls.
Top each serving of yogurt with a quarter of the sauce (about ⅓ cup).
Serve immediately, or chill before serving.
notes: Try swapping vanilla Greek yogurt for the plain Greek yogurt or adding ¼ teaspoon vanilla extract to the plain Greek yogurt.
If using fresh berries, add ½ cup water to saucepan in step 1.
Substitute lemon or orange juice for the lime juice for a different flavor combination if desired.
If more sweetness is desired, add up to 2 teaspoons of sweetener (e.g. honey, sugar, agave, stevia) to the berry sauce.
Garnish with slivered almonds or chopped nuts if desired.

title: Green Beans Almondine
ingredientLines: 1 teaspoon lemon juice or white wine vinegar
steps: Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the almonds and cook until toasted, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the butter and cook, stirring often, until melted and golden-brown, about 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the almond mixture to a small bowl.
Add the lemon juice and stir to combine, then set aside.
Return the pan to the stovetop over medium heat.
Add the green beans, water, and salt.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook until the green beans are almost tender, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook until the green beans are tender and the liquid is evaporated, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat and add the almond mixture. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
notes: Asparagus can be substituted for the green beans if desired. Reduce the cooking time to 4-6 minutes with the lid on and 3-5 minutes with the lid off.

title: Grilled Chicken Taco Salad Bowls
ingredientLines: 4 tablespoons (¼ cup) lime juice, divided (about 2 limes)
4 (4- to 6-ounce) boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 1 pound)
½ cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt (about one 5.3-ounce container)
1 cup fresh or frozen corn kernels, thawed if frozen
1 (15-ounce) no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
½ medium onion, thinly sliced (about 1 cup)
steps: In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the oil and 2 tablespoons of the lime juice.
Add the cumin, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and oregano. Stir to combine.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels, then add to the bowl and toss to coat. Set aside.
Preheat the grill to medium-high (about 400°F) or a grill pan on the stovetop over medium-high heat.
When the grill or grill pan is hot, add the chicken and cook through (internal temperature of 165°F), about 4-7 minutes on each side.
Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and let rest for 5-7 minutes, then cut into bite-sized strips or cubes.
While the chicken rests, in a small bowl, stir together the Greek yogurt, cilantro, salt, black pepper, and remaining 2 tablespoons of lime juice to make a dressing.
Gather four serving bowls and add 2 cups of the lettuce, ¼ cup of the tomato, and ¼ cup of the corn to each.
Top each bowl with a quarter of each of the following: black beans (~⅓ cup each), avocado (~¼ cup each), onion (~¼ cup each), and dressing (~2 tablespoons each).
Divide the chicken between the bowls
Serve right away.

title: Ground Turkey Sweet Potato Skillet
ingredientLines: 1 (15-ounce) can black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat a large pot medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the ground turkey, garlic, onion, and bell pepper.
Use a heat-resistant spoon to break up the turkey while it cooks. Stir occasionally and cook until the turkey is no longer pink.
Add the sweet potato, beans, black pepper, and crushed red pepper flakes.
Cover the skillet and cook until the potato is tender, stirring occasionally. If necessary, add a little bit of water to cook the sweet potato faster.
When the sweet potato is tender, sprinkle with the shredded mozzarella cheese.
Turn off the heat.
Cover the pot with a lid and let sit until the cheese is melted, about 5 minutes.
Serve warm.
credit: Adapted from Cooking Light | Submitted by JoAnna Hazard RD

title: Hearty Bell Pepper and Turkey Skillet
steps: Heat a large heavy skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and sauté until soft and transparent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the ground turkey and bell pepper. Continue to sauté until the bell peppers are soft and the turkey is fully cooked, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes and their juice, rice, basil, oregano, broth, tomato sauce, and Worcestershire sauce. Stir to combine.
Place the lid on the skillet. Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cook until the rice is tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed, about for 10-15 minutes. Add additional broth or water if needed to cook the rice.
Serve warm.
notes: Try substituting another quick-cooking grain product (e.g. quinoa, millet, whole-wheat orzo, bulgur) for the rice.
credit: Inspired by a recipe submitted by Jessica Long MS, RDN, CD

title: Hearty Pumpkin Chili
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher)
2 (14.5-ounce) cans no-salt-added diced tomatoes and their juice
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added garbanzo beans (chickpeas), drained and rinsed
Optional toppings: Shredded cheese, plain Greek yogurt, sliced scallion (green onion)
steps: Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the ground turkey and onion. Cook, stirring often, until the turkey is no longer pink and the onion is softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the chili powder, pumpkin pie spice, cumin, garlic powder, black pepper, and salt. Cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the broth, diced tomatoes with their juice, pumpkin puree, kidney beans, black beans, garbanzo beans, green chiles, and apple cider vinegar. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook uncovered for 35-45 minutes.

Serve warm, topping as desired. NOTE: To make the recipe in a slow cooker, add the ingredients and stir to combine. Cover the slow cooker with the lid, then set the slow cooker to cook on low for 8-12 hours (or on high for 4-6 hours).
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Hearty Pumpkin Muffins
ingredientLines: 1 tablespoon pumpkin pie spice or ground cinnamon
¾ cup packed dark brown sugar
⅓ cup canola oil or avocado oil
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Coat a 12-cup muffin pan with nonstick spray. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, whole-wheat flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and pumpkin pie spice or cinnamon.
In a separate large mixing bowl, whisk together the brown sugar, oil, and eggs. Add the pumpkin puree, milk, and vanilla extract. Whisk to combine.
Gradually add the flour mixture to the pumpkin mixture, stirring gently just until combined.
Pour the batter into the prepared muffin pan, filling each cup all the way to the top.
Bake until a toothpick comes out clean when inserted into the center of the muffins, about 18-22 minutes.
Let cool in the muffin pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a cooling rack. Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Try adding the extra pumpkin puree to oatmeal, yogurt, or smoothies.
If desired, add up to ½ cup of mix-ins such as walnuts, dried cranberries, or green pumpkin seeds (pepitas).

title: Hearty Red Lentil Soup
ingredientLines: 1 jalapeño pepper, seeds and ribs removed, minced
1 cup uncooked red lentils, picked through to remove any stones and rinsed
steps: Heat a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, celery, carrots, and jalapeño.
Sauté until the onions are softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Stir in the lentils, broth, tomatoes with their juice, cumin, and ground black pepper.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cover with a lid and simmer for 40 minutes.
Stir in the spinach. Cook until the spinach is thawed and the soup is warmed through.
Serve warm.
notes: To reduce the spiciness (heat), omit the jalapeno and substitute a bell pepper.
Substitute 6 cups fresh chopped spinach for the frozen spinach if desired.
otherCredits: Adapted from Diabetes.org | Submitted by Destiny Johnson MS, RD, LMNT
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Hearty Stir-Fry
ingredientLines: ¼ teaspoon ground dried ginger (or 1 teaspoon fresh grated ginger)
1 tablespoon peanut, canola, or avocado oil, divided
½ pound (8 ounces) raw animal or plant protein (e.g. tempeh, tofu, chicken, shrimp, meat, eggs)

4 cups fresh vegetables or frozen stir-fry vegetables (one type or a combination; e.g. asparagus, broccoli, carrots, mushrooms, onions, peppers, zucchini, snap peas, cabbage, green beans, cauliflower)
½ cup raw unsalted cashews or peanuts (optional)
2 cups cooked brown rice or quinoa
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, honey, lime juice, and ginger to make a sauce. Set aside.

Chop and slice the selected vegetables. Arrange in order of cooking time, from longest (hard/tough vegetables; onion, carrots, broccoli) to shortest (soft vegetables; snap peas, asparagus, zucchini). If using frozen vegetables, skip this step and add all the vegetables at the beginning of cooking.
Prepare the selected protein (small dice or thin slice, unless using shrimp or eggs).
Heat a large skillet, sauté pan, or wok over high heat.
Add the oil and the longest-cooking vegetables and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.
Add the protein and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.
Add the shortest-cooking vegetables and cook, stirring constantly, for 4 minutes.
Add the sauce and cashews or peanuts (if using). Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Divide the rice or quinoa between four bowls and divide the vegetable-protein mixture between the bowls. Serve warm.
categories: Main Dishes: Lamb, Goat, and Game Meat

title: Holiday Fruit Crostini
ingredientLines: ⅓ cup fresh fruit, sliced or chopped if needed (one type or a combination; e.g. apples, pears, figs, cranberries, raspberries)
1 teaspoon balsamic vinegar, white wine vinegar, or lemon juice
12 teaspoons (¼ cup) crumbled goat cheese or shaved parmesan, divided
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Slice the bread diagonally into 12 slices, about ½-inch-thick. Place the bread slices on a baking sheet and brush with the olive oil.
Bake until toasted, about 5 minutes, flipping about halfway through the cooking time.
Add the fruit, vinegar or lemon juice, honey, salt, and black pepper to a small mixing bowl. Toss to combine.
Divide the fruit mixture, between the bread slices (~1 tablespoon each). Top each slice 1 teaspoon of the cheese, then serve.
notes: Garnish with chopped fresh thyme leave for a savory twist.
Cubed brie can be used in place of the cheese. Bake until melted.

title: Home-Style Hummus
ingredientLines: 2 tablespoons lemon juice (about ½ lemon), plus more to taste if desired
steps: Drain the chickpeas. Reserve the canning liquid and set aside.
Put the chickpeas in a food processor or blender.
Add the garlic, lemon juice, tahini, oil, black pepper, salt, and half of the reserved chickpea canning liquid (about ⅓ cup).
Puree the until very smooth, about 2-3 minutes, adding additional canning liquid as necessary to produce a thick dip.
Add additional lemon juice to taste, if desired.
Transfer to a serving dish (or a storage container if you’re not eating it right away). Garnish with paprika.
Serve right away, or store in an air-tight container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Can be frozen if desired.
notes: Try substituting unsweetened peanut butter for the tahini, if desired.
For additional flavor, consider adding 2-3 tablespoons of diced olives, roasted red peppers, or caramelized onions in step 3 or as a garnish.
For a smoother dip, toss the chickpeas with the oil and microwave before blending, about 1-2 minutes.

title: Homemade Cranberry Sauce
ingredientLines: 12 ounces fresh cranberries, thawed if frozen
¾ cup fresh orange juice (about 2-3 oranges)
steps: Add the cranberries, orange zest, orange juice, honey, water, cinnamon, cloves, and salt to medium saucepan.
Set the saucepan over high heat and bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to medium.
Continue cooking, stirring often, until the cranberries break down. The sauce should thicken and reduce to about 2 cups.
If the sauce becomes too thick, add a little extra water to reach the desired consistency. Note that the sauce will continue to thicken as it cools.
Serve warm, or chill before serving.

title: Homemade Ricotta
ingredientLines: 3 tablespoons distilled white vinegar or lemon juice
steps: Add the milk, heavy cream, and salt to a large saucepan or stockpot. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn off the heat.
Add the vinegar or lemon juice and stir to combine.
Let sit until large curds separate from the liquid (whey), about 7-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, line a colander or strainer with two layers of damp paper towels and place over the mouth of a large bowl.
Carefully pour or ladle the milk mixture into the colander and strainer. Let drain to the desired consistency, about 30-40 minutes.
Use right away, or refrigerate for up to 7 days. Discard the liquid (whey) or use it in place of buttermilk in other recipes.
notes: This ricotta can be used in place of store-bought ricotta in a variety of dishes, including lasagna, pancakes, or as a spread on toast.
The nutrition facts below are based on store-bought ricotta, since some of the nutrition content is in the whey.

title: Homemade Tortilla Chips
ingredientLines: 5 (8-inch) whole-wheat tortillas or 10 corn tortillas *See Recipe Notes for a savory flavoring option
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Combine the sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. Set aside.
Brush both sides of each tortilla lightly with the oil.
Cut each tortilla into wedges; 8 wedges for whole-wheat tortillas, 4 wedges for corn tortillas.
Lightly sprinkle both sides of the tortilla wedges with the cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Place the tortilla wedges in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Place in the oven and cook until the tortilla wedges are golden-brown and crispy, about 7-10 minutes, flipping them over about halfway through the cooking time.
Serve immediately, or store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.
notes: To make a savory tortilla chip, substitute ¼ teaspoon salt for the sugar and cinnamon — reducing the total carbohydrate to 27.5 g and increasing the sodium to 380 mg. For a lower-sodium savory version, simply remove the sugar and cinnamon and leave them unsalted.
Use nonstick cooking spray in place of the oil in step 3 if desired.

title: Hummus and Veggie Wrap-Up
ingredientLines: 2 tablespoons hummus (store-bought or homemade; try the Home-Style Hummus recipe on page 16)
steps: Spread the hummus over the tortilla.
Layer the tortilla with the salad greens, onion, cucumber, tomato, and carrots.
Drizzle with the vinaigrette.
Fold the sides of the tortilla over towards the center, then roll up tightly.
Serve cold.
notes: Consider adding other non-starchy vegetables that you may have on hand, such as sliced bell peppers, cooked mushrooms, or zucchini.

title: Indian Spinach with Tofu
ingredientLines: 8 ounces extra firm tofu, cut into cubes
steps: Heat a medium skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ½ tablespoon olive oil and heat until shimmering.
Add tofu cubes and cook for 10 minutes, flipping every couple minutes. Remove from pan and set aside.
Return the pan to medium heat and add the remaining ½ tablespoon oil.
Add the onion, ginger, garlic. Cook 5 minutes.
Add the spinach, broth, turmeric, cumin, garam masala, sugar and salt.
Bring to a simmer. Cook for 8-10 minutes.
Remove from heat and puree with a immersion blender or transfer to a standing blender. Add more water if too thick.
Return puree back to the pan if removed. Stir in coconut milk and tofu cubes.
Serve warm over rice or with naan bread if desired.
notes: If you do not have fresh ginger, substitute ½ teaspoon ground ginger.
Substitute 8 ounces of fresh spinach for the frozen spinach if desired.
