credit: Adapted from connoisseurusveg.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Indian Stir-Fried Cauliflower
ingredientLines: 2 tablespoons peanut, avocado, or canola oil
½ teaspoon grated or minced fresh ginger
2 fresh green chile peppers (e.g. jalapeño, serrano), cut lengthwise, seeded, and minced
1 medium cauliflower head, cut into florets (about 2 pounds; 4-6 cups)
steps: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened and slightly brown, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, chile peppers, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and black pepper. Cook, stirring often, for 3-4 minutes.
Add the cauliflower florets. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes.
Add the water and cover the pan with a lid.
Cook until the cauliflower is fork-tender, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the peas and continue cooking until warmed through, about 1-2 minutes.
Serve warm, with a lime wedge to squeeze on juice as desired.

title: Indian-Style Simmered Chicken
servingSize: 4 ounces chicken with ½ cup rice and ⅙ of the spinach and sauce
ingredientLines: ¼-½ teaspoon cayenne pepper, to taste
1½ pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 6 breasts, 4 ounces each)
2 teaspoons fresh ginger, minced (or ½ teaspoon ground dried ginger)
steps: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, combine the garlic powder, coriander, cumin, salt, and cayenne with a fork. Toss the chicken breasts in the spice mixture.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken, sprinkling any of the remaining seasoning mixture on top, and sear until golden-brown, about 2-3 minutes on each side.
Add the ginger, coconut milk, and tomatoes with their juice. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover the pan with a lid.
Heat until the chicken is cooked through, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the spinach and cover the pan with the lid. Let cook until the spinach is wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in the lime juice.
Layer into six bowls with the rice on the bottom, then the spinach, sauce, and chicken. Serve warm.

title: Italian Meatloaf
ingredientLines: ½ medium onion, diced (about ½ cup)
1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground beef (90% lean or higher)
1 tablespoon yellow mustard (or 1 teaspoon dry mustard)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.
Heat a skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the bell pepper, onion, and salt. Cook until the bell pepper and onion are softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Transfer the pepper-onion mixture to a large mixing bowl.
Add the ground beef, carrot, ketchup, egg, breadcrumbs, tomato paste, mustard, basil, oregano, thyme, garlic powder, and black pepper and mix until well combined.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking sheet and shape the mixture into a loaf.
Bake until the meatloaf is firm and reaches an internal temperature of 160°F, about 35-45 minutes.
Cover the meatloaf loosely with foil and let it rest for 5-10 minutes, then cut it into six slices. Serve warm.
notes: You may mix with your hands if needed. Be sure to wash your hands with soap and water before and after mixing.

title: Italian Pasta Skillet
ingredientLines: 1 medium red bell pepper, diced (about 1½ cups)
1 cup shredded reduced-fat (2%) Italian cheese blend or cheddar cheese
Optional toppings: Chopped basil, grated Parmesan cheese
steps: Heat a large Dutch oven or saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add the ground beef and cook until no longer pink.
Drain any excess fat from the pan.
Add the oil, bell pepper, and mushrooms.
Cook, stirring frequently, until the bell pepper and mushrooms are tender.
Stir in the marinara pasta sauce and water.
Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil.
Add the pasta. Stir, then return to a low boil.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is tender, about 15 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low and add the spinach. Cook until the spinach is wilted.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the cheese until melted.
Serve warm, garnishing with chopped basil and/or grated parmesan cheese as desired.
credit: Adapted from accenthealth.com | Submitted by Jessica Long MS, RDN, CD

title: Italian Summer Soup
ingredientLines: 1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added white beans (e.g. cannellini beans, great northern beans)
steps: Heat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, garlic, Italian seasoning, cayenne, and salt.
Sauté until the onion is softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, bell pepper, zucchini, beans, corn, and broth.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook uncovered until the vegetables are tender, about 20-25 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: Substitute 1 (14.5-ounce) can no-salt-added diced tomatoes for the fresh tomatoes if desired.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Italian Wedding Soup
ingredientLines: ½ cup uncooked whole-wheat orzo pasta
2 links mild Italian turkey or chicken sausage (about 6.5 ounces)
steps: Warm a large saucepan or pot over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook until softened and starting to brown, about 7-10 minutes.
Add the Italian seasoning, garlic, black pepper, and red pepper flakes. Cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the broth and the orzo.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn the heat down to maintain a simmer.
Slice open the sausage casing and pinch off a small amount of the meat (about the size of a marble). Drop the pieces of meat directly into the simmering broth.
Continue simmering until the orzo is tender and the meatballs are cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Add the chopped spinach and lemon juice. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
notes: Feel free to substitute another type of short whole-wheat pasta (e.g. elbows, shells, rotini) or a quick-cooking whole grain (e.g. quinoa, millet) in place of the orzo.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Japanese Cucumber Salad
ingredientLines: 1 large or 2 medium English cucumbers (about 1-1½ pounds)
1 tablespoon sesame seeds, toasted if desired
steps: Trim the ends of the cucumber and cut each cucumber crosswise into thirds, then cut in half lengthwise.
Place the cucumbers in a large plastic zip-top bag and seal the bag. Place the bag on a hard, durable surface such as a clean cutting board.
Use a skillet or a sauté pan to smash the cucumbers in the bag until they start to split lengthwise.
Tear or cut the cucumbers into bite-sized pieces, then add them to a colander placed inside a bowl or over the sink.
Sprinkle the cucumbers with the salt and toss to combine.
Let the cucumbers sit to remove their excess liquid, at least 15 minutes and up to 30 minutes.

While the cucumbers sit, add the vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, and red pepper flakes (if using) to a medium mixing bowl. Stir together until the sugar has dissolved to make a dressing, about 1 minute.
Add the cucumbers to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine. Discard the liquid drained from the cucumber.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve immediately, or chill before serving if desired.

title: Kale and Shaved Fennel Salad
ingredientLines: 4 tablespoons (¼ cup) lemon juice (about 1 medium lemon), divided
1 large bunch or 2 medium bunches kale (about 14-16 ounces in total)
12 tablespoons (¾ cup) crumbled blue cheese, divided
12 tablespoons (¾ cup) chopped toasted walnuts, divided
steps: In a large mixing or serving bowl, add 2 tablespoons of lemon juice, oil, honey or maple syrup, mustard, salt, and black pepper and whisk well to create a dressing. Set aside.
Cut the fennel bulb into quarters lengthwise and remove the core from each piece. Cut each quarter into thin slices, with a knife or a slicing tool (e.g. box grater, mandoline).
In a medium mixing bowl, toss the shaved fennel with the remaining 2 tablespoons of lemon juice. Set aside.
Remove the large stems from the kale and cut or tear into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing. Using clean hands, toss and massage the kale with the dressing.
Cut the pear in half lengthwise and scrape out the core with the tip of a spoon. Cut each half lengthwise into thin slices.
Add the pear and fennel to the bowl with the kale and toss to combine.
Serve, topping each serving with 2 tablespoons of the blue cheese and 2 tablespoons of the walnuts.
notes: A different crumbly cheese such as feta, gorgonzola, or goat cheese can be substituted for the blue cheese.
Substitute apple for the pear if desired.

title: Kale Chips
ingredientLines: 1 teaspoon spice (one type or a combination; e.g. garlic powder, onion powder, chili powder, paprika)
steps: Preheat the oven to 300°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Set aside.
Wash the kale and pat dry. Remove the leaves from the stems, discarding the stems. Place the leaves in a large mixing bowl.
Add the oil and rub onto the surface of the kale leaves.
Add the nutritional yeast (if using), selected spice(s), and salt. Toss to combine.
Spread the kale into a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake until crispy, about 20-25 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through the cooking time.
Let cool, then serve at room temperature.
notes: If you do not have parchment paper, you can lightly coat the baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days.
otherCredits: Adapted from Ohsheglows.com | Submitted by Robin Adapted fromLaCroix, Rd, CSO Submitted by

title: Lamb-Vegetable Kabobs with Tzatziki
ingredientLines: ¼ cup peeled and finely chopped cucumber
½ cup (4 ounces) reduced-sodium beef broth
1 tablespoon minced fresh rosemary (or 1 teaspoon dried)
1 pound lamb, cut into 1- to 2-inch cubes
1 medium bell pepper, cut into 1- to 2-inch cubes
½ medium onion, cut into 1- to 2-inch cubes
steps: In a small bowl, stir together the Greek yogurt, cucumber, mint, and 1 teaspoon of the lemon juice. Set aside.
In a separate small mixing bowl, whisk together the broth, vinegar, oil, garlic, rosemary, salt, black pepper, and the remaining lemon juice to make a marinade.
Transfer the marinade mixture to a large plastic ziptop bag. Set the bag inside the bowl that held the marinade.
Add the cubed lamb to the marinade and toss to coat.
Seal the bag, squeezing out the excess air, and refrigerate in the bowl for at least 20 minutes, up to overnight.
Gather 12 skewers. If using wooden or bamboo skewers, soak them in warm water for at least 15 minutes to prevent the ends from burning and turning black.
While the skewers are soaking, heat up the grill to medium heat or the broiler to high heat. If the broiler is in the oven, set an oven rack to the middle position.
While the broiler or grill is heating, thread the marinated lamb cubes, zucchini, bell pepper, and onion onto the skewers.
Cook on the grill or under the broiler (on the middle rack if in the oven) for 15-20 minutes, turning every 4-5 minutes, until cooked through (internal temperature of 145°F).
Drizzle with yogurt mixture, then serve warm.
notes: Consider serving with whole-wheat pita or a cooked whole grain such as farro, barley, bulgur, or quinoa.
categories: Main Dishes: Lamb, Goat, and Game Meat

title: Lasagna Soup
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher)
8 ounces whole-grain lasagna noodles, broken into ½- to 1-inch pieces (about 6-10 noodles)
steps: Place a large pot over medium heat on the stovetop.
Add the oil and onion. Cook, stirring often, until the onion is translucent, about 5-8 minutes.
Add the ground turkey, oregano, and garlic. Cook until the turkey is almost completely cooked, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the broth, tomatoes, and tomato sauce.
Turn the heat up to high and bring to a boil.
Add the lasagna noodles and continue cooking at a boil until they are tender but still a little chewy (al dente), about 10-12 minutes.
Divide the soup between six serving bowls and top each with 2 tablespoons of the ricotta.
Serve warm.
notes: To make this in a slow cooker, simply add the ingredients and cook (low for 4-5 hours or high for 2-3 hours).
Leftovers can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 7 days or in the freezer for up to 6 months. The noodles may soak up more of the liquid as the soup sits in the refrigerator.
For a boost in vegetables, add a handful of fresh spinach leaves or puree some leftover vegetables in a blender a food processor to mix into the soup.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Leftover Cranberry Sauce Parfait
ingredientLines: ⅔ cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt, divided
4 tablespoons granola or muesli cereal, divided
2 teaspoons chia seeds or hemp hearts, divided
steps: In a parfait glass or bowl, layer the following ingredients in this order: ⅓ cup of the Greek yogurt, ½ tablespoon of the honey, all of the cranberry sauce, 2 tablespoons of the granola, 1 teaspoon of the chia seeds or hemp seeds, and 1 teaspoon of the ground flax.
Repeat with a second layer, with the remaining ⅓ cup Greek yogurt, ½ tablespoon honey, 2 tablespoons granola, 1 teaspoon chia seeds or hemp seeds, and 1 teaspoon ground flax.
Serve immediately.
notes: If you don’t have whole-berry cranberry sauce, try mashing up canned jellied cranberry sauce to use as a substitute.
For a different texture and flavor, try substituting 1-2 tablespoons pepitas (green pumpkin seeds) for the chia seeds or hemp hearts.

title: Leftover Roasted Turkey Wrap
ingredientLines: 3 ounces leftover roasted turkey breast, sliced or chopped (about ½ cup)
¼ avocado, pitted, peeled, and sliced
½ cup mixed salad greens or fresh spinach
steps: In a small bowl, add the Greek yogurt and cranberry sauce. Stir to combine, then set aside.
Lay the warmed tortilla on a clean flat surface, such as a cutting board. Spread the yogurt mixture evenly over the tortilla, leaving about a 1-inch border on all sides.
Layer the turkey, avocado, lettuce, carrot, tomato, green onion, and black pepper onto the bottom half of the tortilla, still leaving a 1-inch border.
Roll up the tortilla into a wrap by folding the sides in toward the center, then rolling the bottom up toward the top.
(Optional) Heat the wrap under the broiler until lightly toasted, about 2-3 minutes on each side.
Cut the wrap in half and serve.
notes: For a different flavor profile, try substituting Ranch dressing for the plain Greek yogurt and salsa for the leftover cranberry sauce.
Make this recipe any time of the year using leftover roasted chicken breast or rotisserie chicken.
Try replacing the shredded carrot with grated jicama or sweet potato.

title: Lemon Bars
ingredientLines: ¾ cup plus 1 tablespoon flour, divided
¼ cup plus 1 teaspoon powdered sugar, divided
2 lemons, zest and juice (about 2 teaspoons of zest and about ½ cup juice)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Spray a small (8 x 4-inch or 5 x 7-inch) baking dish.
In a medium bowl, combine ¾ cup flour and ¼ cup powdered sugar.
Add the melted butter and mix until it forms a crumbly dough. Press into the baking dish to cover the bottom.
Bake for 15 minutes, remove from oven and set aside.
While the crust is baking, zest the lemons to get 2 teaspoons of zest and then juice lemons into mixing bowl.
Add the granulated sugar to zest and juice, stir to combine.
Add the egg and egg white, remaining 1 tablespoon flour and salt. Whisk until well blended.
Pour the lemon mixture over the crust. Bake for 20 minutes or until the filling is set and no longer jiggly.
Cool completely and sprinkle with powdered sugar.
notes: Bars will stay fresh in the fridge for 4 days.
Bars can be frozen in a sealed container, with wax paper between the layers.
credit: Adapted from Sparkpeople.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Lemon Chicken Stir-Fry
ingredientLines: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 medium carrots, peeled and cut on the bias (diagonally-sliced)
2 cups snow peas, stems and strings removed
1 bunch scallions (green onions), cut into 1-inch pieces, white and green parts separated
steps: Grate 1 teaspoon lemon zest from the peel of the lemon and set aside.
Juice the entire lemon. Whisk the juice with the broth, soy sauce, ginger, and cornstarch in a small bowl. Set aside.
Heat a large nonstick skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, until partially cooked, about 1-2 minutes. Transfer the chicken to a plate.
Add the mushrooms and carrots to the now-empty pan and cook until the carrots are just tender, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the snow peas, white portion of the scallions, garlic, lemon zest, and the broth mixture. Stir to combine.
Bring to a rapid simmer and cook, stirring often, until the sauce is thickened, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the partially cooked chicken back to the pan, along with the green portion of the scallions.
Cook, stirring constantly, until the chicken is fully cooked.
notes: For a more potent flavor, try using 1 tablespoon minced fresh ginger root instead of dried.
If you are out of lemons, substitute 3 tablespoons lemon juice for the lemon (zest and juice).
credit: Adapted from www.eatingwell.com | Submitted by Jessica Long MS, RDN, CD

title: Lemon-Parmesan Broccoli
ingredientLines: 3 tablespoons grated or shredded parmesan cheese
¼-½ teaspoon ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Place the broccoli in the pan and sauté until bright green, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the water and sauté until fork-tender, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Remove the pan from the heat.
Add the lemon juice, parmesan, and black pepper to the broccoli. Toss to combine.
Serve warm.
notes: If you don’t have fresh garlic on hand, try using ¼ teaspoon garlic

title: Lemon-Thyme Orzo Primavera
ingredientLines: ½ cup uncooked whole-wheat orzo pasta (can substitute a different small whole-wheat pasta)
1 medium zucchini, grated or diced (about 1 cup)
1 medium carrot, grated or diced (about ½ cup)
1 cup (8 ounces) no-salt-added vegetable broth or chicken broth
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) grated parmesan cheese, divided
steps: Heat a medium or large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the uncooked orzo pasta. Cook, stirring often, until golden and fragrant, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the garlic, zucchini, and carrot. Cook, stirring often, for 2 minutes.
Add the broth and lemon zest. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cook until the liquid has been absorbed and orzo is al dente (tender, yet still a little chewy), about 10 minutes.
Stir in the thyme.
Serve warm, topping each serving with 1 tablespoon of parmesan cheese.
notes: Place the zested lemon in a zip-top plastic bag and store in the refrigerator for juicing later, within 5-7 days.
Consider serving with baked chicken or fish and a salad for a complete meal.
If you do not have fresh thyme, add ¼-1 teaspoon dried thyme (to taste) with the broth and lemon zest.

title: Lemony Pan-Seared Fish with Wilted Kale
servingSize: 1 fish fillet and the kale mixture
ingredientLines: 1 (4- to 6-ounce) fish fillet (e.g. flounder, whiting, tilapia, salmon, tuna)
1½ teaspoons chopped fresh dill (or ½ teaspoon dried)
2 cups chopped or shredded kale, stems removed
steps: Cut the lemon in half lengthwise. Juice one of the halves into a small bowl. Cut the other half into four wedges. Set the lemon juice and lemon wedges aside.
On a clean plate or other surface (e.g. cutting board), pat the fish dry with paper towels, then season it evenly on both sides with the seasoning blend and chopped dill.
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ½ tablespoon of the oil to the pan.
Add the fish and cook on the first side until browned, about 2-4 minutes.
Turn the fish over and heat until cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, about 4-6 minutes.
Transfer the fish to a clean plate and cover with foil.
Add the remaining ½ tablespoon of oil to the pan.
Add the kale and cook until wilted, about 2-4 minutes.
Add the lemon juice and stir to combine.
Transfer the kale to the plate with the fish and serve warm, squeezing on additional lemon juice as desired.

title: Light-and-Lemony Hollandaise Sauce
steps: Melt the butter in a small skillet over low heat. Keep it in the pan to stay warm.
Fill a medium saucepan three-quarters full with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Find a heat-resistant metal mixing bowl that fits in the mouth of the saucepan without touching the water. With the bowl off the heat, add and whisk together the eggs, lemon juice, and salt.
Add ⅓ cup water to a microwave-safe bowl or liquid measuring cup. Microwave until very hot, about 1 minute.

Place the heat-resistant metal bowl on the mouth of the saucepan over the simmering water to make a double boiler. The bowl shouldn’t touch the water. If it does, pour out small amounts of the water until it does not.
Whisk constantly, adding the ⅓ cup hot water in a slow but steady stream, until the eggs have thickened to a ribbony, lemon-yellow creamy, and uniform texture.
Turn off the heat and add the butter in a slow but steady stream, whisking constantly.
Add the cayenne and serve warm.
notes: This sauce goes well over eggs, cooked green vegetables (e.g. asparagus, green beans, broccoli), and seafood.
Store in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. To reheat, microwave at 50% power until warm, about 1-2 minutes.

title: Loaded Vegetable Omelet
ingredientLines: ⅓ cup finely diced bell pepper
steps: Crack the eggs into a small bowl. Add the milk and black pepper. Whisk with fork until combined, then set aside.
Heat a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, mushrooms, and bell pepper. Cook, stirring often, until tender and lightly browned, about 3-5 minutes.
Transfer the vegetable mixture to a plate and set aside.
Spray the pan with nonstick spray and return the pan to the stovetop. Reduce the heat to medium-low.
Add the egg mixture to the pan and cover the pan with a lid.
Allow the eggs to cook, without stirring, until firm but still moist, about 2-4 minutes.
Remove the lid and sprinkle the vegetable mixture and cheese over one half of the cooked eggs.
Fold the other half of eggs over the vegetables and cheese.
Turn off the heat and cover the pan with the lid until the cheese is melted, about 2-3 minutes, then serve warm.
notes: Substitute any of your favorite fresh or leftover vegetables, or add cooked lean meat and beans if desired.

title: Make-Ahead Burrito Bowls
ingredientLines: 2 cups cooked whole grain (e.g. quinoa, brown rice, bulgur)
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
4 cups diced or shredded cooked chicken
1 cup corn kernels (cooked from fresh, frozen, or canned; thawed if frozen)
4 cups lettuce or salad greens, shredded or chopped if needed
½ cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt
½ cup sliced scallions (green onions; about 3-4 stalks)
steps: Gather four microwave-safe food storage containers with lids.
Combine the cooked whole grain with the green chiles. Divide this mixture evenly among the four containers.
Divide the beans evenly among the four containers.
Add 1 cup of the chicken and ¼ of the cup corn to each of the four containers.
Add 1 cup of the lettuce or salad greens to each container.
Top each container with 2 tablespoons salsa, 2 tablespoons Greek yogurt, and 2 tablespoons scallions.
Cover the containers with lids and store in refrigerator until ready to eat, up to 3 days.
When ready to eat, microwave each container on high power (default setting) until hot, about 1-3 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: The lettuce or salad greens, salsa, Greek yogurt, and green onion can be added after reheating the bowl if desired. To save time and keep the bowls portable, you can pre-portion them out into their own container(s).
Substitute another cooked protein for the chicken such as pork, ground turkey, tofu, or steak if desired.

title: Maple-Pecan Granola
ingredientLines: ½ cup olive oil or avocado oil
½-1 teaspoon ground cinnamon, to taste
1½ cups unsalted pecans, chopped into ¼- to ½-inch pieces
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.
In large mixing bowl, whisk together the oil, maple syrup, vanilla, salt, and cinnamon.
Add the oats and pecans. Toss gently until completely coated with the oil-maple syrup mixture.
Transfer the mixture onto the prepared baking and spread into an even layer.
Bake until golden-brown and crispy, about 20-25 minutes, stirring the mixture every 7-10 minutes.
Remove from oven and place on a wire cooling rack or other heat-safe surface.
When completely cooled, use as desired or transfer to an airtight storage container for up to 2 months.
notes: Another type of nut or seed can be used in place of some or all of the pecans, if desired (e.g. walnuts, pepitas, pumpkin seeds, almonds). Honey can be used in place of the maple syrup.

Try adding ¼ cup of unsweetened coconut flakes. Once the granola is cooled, consider adding up to ½ cup of dried fruit (chopped if large; e.g. raisins, cranberries, papaya, pineapple) or mini chocolate chips.

title: Marinated Vegetables
ingredientLines: ¼ cup red wine vinegar or white wine vinegar
1-3 pinches crushed red pepper flakes, to taste

4 cups fresh vegetables, trimmed and cut into ½- to 1-inch pieces (one type or a combination; e.g. tomatoes, cucumber, broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, snap peas, yellow squash, mushrooms, zucchini, baby corn, red onion)
steps: To a medium mixing bowl or a jar with a lid, add the oil, vinegar, lemon juice, garlic powder, oregano, basil, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Whisk together the oil-vinegar mixture in the bowl or place the lid on the jar and shake, mixing until combined to make a marinade.
Place the selected vegetables in a large bowl.
Pour the marinade over the vegetables and toss until evenly coated.
Set the vegetables in the refrigerator to marinate, at least 30 minutes and up to overnight.
Serve cold, or cook as desired and serve warm.
notes: The marinade can be made ahead of time and stored in the refrigerator if desired.
These marinated veggies are best when prepared at least 2 hours before serving or cooking.

title: Mashed Potatoes and Cauliflower
ingredientLines: 2 medium Yukon gold or red potatoes, peeled and cubed
3 cups fresh or frozen cauliflower florets (about 2 pounds)
steps: Place the potatoes and fresh cauliflower (if using frozen, see step 2) in a medium saucepan. Add water to cover and bring to a boil.

Reduce the heat to low and simmer until the potatoes are fork-tender and the cauliflower is very soft (overcooked), about 15 minutes. (If using frozen cauliflower, add after the potatoes have been boiling for 5 minutes. Bring back to a boil and continue cooking for the additional 10 minutes.)
Drain the potatoes and cauliflower into a strainer.
Transfer the cauliflower to a blender or food processor, along with the garlic, milk, butter, salt, and pepper. Puree until smooth.
Add the potatoes and pureed cauliflower mixture back to the pan. Mash together until smooth and combined.
Stir in the parsley (if using) and serve warm.

title: Massaged Kale Salad
ingredientLines: 2 bunches kale, stems removed and chopped, or 1 (16-ounce) bag cut kale
1 pint cherry or grape tomatoes, halved (about 2-3 cups)
¼ cup unsalted shelled sunflower seeds (can substitute another seed or chopped nut)
steps: Add the kale to a large mixing or serving bowl.
Add 4 tablespoons (¼ cup) of the lemon juice, 2 tablespoons of the oil, and the salt.
Massage the kale until it wilts down in size by about half and it feels more tender, about 1-2 minutes, making sure each leaf is coated with the lemon juice-oil mixture. Set aside.
In a small bowl, make a dressing by whisking together the honey, salt, black pepper, the remaining 2 tablespoons lemon juice, and the remaining 1 tablespoon oil.
Pour the dressing over the kale, along with the sunflower seeds and tomatoes. Toss to combine.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving.
notes: Load this salad up with any of your other favorite vegetables, or even fruit.
If you’re watching the salt, you can reduce it, omit it, or substitute your favorite salt-free seasoning.
For a more lemony flavor, add ½ teaspoon lemon zest to the dressing.
This salad can be made 1-2 days before serving, if desired. Unlike salads made with lettuce or spinach, salads made with kale actually improve in flavor and texture with time.

title: Mediterranean Barley Salad
ingredientLines: 1 (15-ounce) can reduced-sodium garbanzo beans (chickpeas), drained and rinsed
6 large dates (e.g. Medjool), pitted and diced
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together the dressing ingredients and set aside.
Heat a small pan over medium-low heat.
Add the almonds to the pan and toast until light brown and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Transfer the almonds to a medium mixing bowl.
Add the cooked and chilled barley, chickpeas, roasted red peppers, and dates to the mixing bowl with the almonds. Stir to combine.
Pour the dressing over the barley mixture, whisking to recombine if needed. Toss to coat.
Gently fold in the feta cheese.
Serve right away, or chill before serving.
notes: Store in the refrigerator for 5-7 days.
credit: Submitted by Melanya Souza, RD, LD/N

title: Mediterranean Chicken and Bulgur Skillet
servingSize: ¾ cup of the bulgur mixture and ¼th of the chicken
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken and cook until browned on both sides, about 3 minutes per side. Transfer the chicken to a plate.
Add the onion and garlic to the now-empty pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the bulgur, black pepper, and oregano. Cook, stirring often, until fragrant and toasted, about 2 minutes.
Add the kale and bell pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, until kale begins to wilt, about 2 minutes.
Add the broth and bring to a boil. Remove the pan from the heat and place the chicken into the bulgur mixture.
Cover the pan with a lid and place in the oven. Bake until the chicken is fully cooked, about 12-15 minutes.
Serve, sprinkled with the feta and dill.
notes: For a bolder flavor, try using ½ cups sliced roasted red bell peppers in place of bell pepper.
credit: Adapted from Cooking Light | Submitted by Janelle Kramer MS, RD, LDN

title: Mediterranean Chickpea Salad
ingredientLines: 2 tablespoons lemon juice or red wine vinegar
½ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes
½ medium onion, diced (about ½ cup)
1 (15-ounce) cans no-salt-added chickpeas (garbanzo beans), drained and rinsed
½ medium cucumber, unpeeled and diced (about ½ cup)
½ medium bell pepper, diced (about ½ cup)
steps: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the lemon juice or vinegar, oil, oregano, and red pepper flakes to make a dressing.
Add the onion and garlic. Stir to combine, then let sit for at least 10 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, tomatoes, cucumber, and bell pepper. Toss to combine.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: Letting the onion and garlic sit in the acidic dressing in step 2 helps to cut down their harsh pungent flavors.
You can save some time by prepping the tomatoes, cucumber, and bell pepper while the onion and garlic sit with the dressing.
Cut up the remaining cucumber and bell pepper into slices and enjoy as a snack if desired.

title: Mediterranean Lamb Kabobs with Tzatziki
ingredientLines: ¼ cup cucumber, peeled if waxed and finely chopped
3 cloves garlic, crushed or minced (about 1 tablespoon)
1 tablespoon fresh minced rosemary (or 1 teaspoon dried)
1 pound lamb, cut into 1- to 2-inch cubes
½ cup zucchini, cut into 1-inch-thick slices
1 red onion, cut into cut into 1- to 2-inch cubes
1 large red pepper, cut into 1- to 2-inch cubes
steps: Combine the Greek yogurt, 1 teaspoon of the lemon juice, chopped mint leaves, and cucumber. Set aside.
Whisk together the olive oil, the remaining lemon juice, salt, pepper, garlic, beef broth, vinegar, and rosemary to make a marinade.
Transfer the marinade mixture to a large plastic ziptop bag set inside a bowl.
Add the cubed lamb and toss to coat with the marinade.
Seal the bag, squeezing out the excess air, and refrigerate in the bowl for at least 20 minutes, up to overnight.
If using wooden or bamboo skewers, soak them in warm water for at least 15 minutes to prevent the ends from burning and turning black.
While the skewers are soaking, heat up the grill to medium heat or the broiler to high heat. If broiling, place an oven rack on the middle position in the oven.
While the broiler or grill is heating, thread the marinated lamb cubes, red peppers, zucchini, and red onion onto the skewers.
Cook the kebabs on the grill or under the broiler (on the middle rack of the oven) for 15-20 minutes, turning every 4-5 minutes, until the lamb is done.
Drizzle the yogurt sauce over the cooked kebabs.
Serve warm with whole-wheat pita or a cooked whole grain such as farro, bulgur, or quinoa.
credit: Adapted from Recipes.SparkPeople.com | Submitted by Dana Herring MS, RDN
categories: Main Dishes: Lamb, Goat, and Game Meat

title: Mediterranean Quinoa Salad
ingredientLines: ½ medium cucumber, chopped (about ½ cup)
¼ cup chopped roasted red pepper or ½ cup halved cherry or grape tomatoes
¼ cup kalamata olives, pitted and chopped
1 teaspoon Dijon mustard or brown mustard
steps: Add the quinoa and water to a medium saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to maintain a simmer. Cook until the quinoa is tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and let sit to cool. You can speed up this process by spreading it on a baking sheet and putting it in the refrigerator.
In a medium mixing bowl, make the dressing by whisking together the olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, and mustard.
Add the cooked and cooled quinoa, along with the cucumber, red peppers or tomatoes, olives, parsley, and feta. Toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving if desired, up to 5 days.
notes: Consider substituting bulgur or barley for the quinoa, cooking it according to the package directions.
This salad is also good with the addition of rinsed canned white beans and/or chopped pitted dates.

title: Mediterranean Salmon Salad
ingredientLines: 1 (5-6 ounce) can salmon, no-salt added, drained and rinsed
Optional Garnishes: lettuce leaves, sliced tomato, sliced onions
steps: In a medium bowl, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, oregano, basil, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper until well combined.
Add salmon to bowl and mix well.
Divide salmon mixture evenly onto sandwich thins and top with desired garnishes.
notes: Substitute whole wheat pita bread or serve as a lettuce wrap without the sandwich thin if desired.
credit: Adapted from eatingwell.com | Submitted by Jessica Long, RDN, CD

title: Mexican Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
ingredientLines: ½ bell pepper, red, yellow or orange
½ cup corn, fresh or frozen
½ cup canned black beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Wash sweet potato well. Pierce 3-4 times with a fork.
Place on a microwave safe dish and microwave for 5 minutes, turning halfway through.
If the potato is not fork tender, cook an additional minute.
Once cool enough, slice in half lengthwise and scoop out ⅔ of the flesh, leaving ½-inch around the skin. Loosely chop the flesh that was removed.
Place a medium skillet over medium heat.
Add oil and heat until shimmering.
Add onion, garlic and bell pepper and cook 5 minutes.
Add corn and cook an additional 5 minutes.
Add the beans, chopped sweet potato, chili powder, cumin, salt, pepper and tomato paste. If mixture is too thick, add 1- 2 tablespoons of water.
Fill each sweet potato skin with half filling, top with yogurt.
notes: Substitute any type of bean for the black beans if desired.
To add more spice, add a dash of cayenne to the filling.
credit: Adapted from delish.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Microwave Berry Compote
ingredientLines: 2 cups frozen berries (mixed or a single variety)
1-2 tablespoons sugar or honey, to taste (optional)
steps: Add the berries, cornstarch, and salt to a microwave-safe bowl.
Toss to combine until the cornstarch is no longer white.
Microwave on high power (default setting) for 2 minutes.
Stir, then continue microwaving on high power (default setting) until slightly thickened and warmed through, about 2-3 minutes more.
Let cool until not too hot to taste, about 2-4 minutes, then add the sugar or honey (if using). Stir to combine.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: This compote will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days, or in an airtight container in the freezer for up to 6 months.
This compote works well as a topping for yogurt, oatmeal, ice cream, pancakes, French toast, or savory items like fish or chicken.
For a boost of flavor, add citrus zest, citrus juice, ground spices (e.g. cinnamon, ginger), and/or chopped fresh herbs (e.g. mint, basil).
Another fruit can be used in place of some or all of the berries. Add 1 tablespoon of water for every cup of chopped fresh fruit.

title: Microwave Breakfast Strata (Egg Casserole)
ingredientLines: 1 cup frozen pepper and onion blend
2 turkey breakfast sausage links, sliced or diced
1 whole-wheat English muffin, torn or cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Coat the inside of a large microwave-safe mug or bowl with nonstick cooking spray.
Add the pepper and onion blend and sausage. Microwave on high power (default setting) for 1 minute.
Use a paper towel to carefully soak up any liquid.
Add the English muffin pieces and cheese. Stir to combine, then set aside.
In a separate small bowl, use a fork to whisk together the eggs, milk, and black pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over English muffin mixture, then let sit for 1-2 minutes to soak.
Microwave on high power (default setting) until the eggs are no longer runny, about 2-3 minutes.
Let sit for 2 minutes, then serve warm.

title: Microwave Chicken Fajitas
ingredientLines: 2 medium bell peppers, sliced ¼-inch-thick (about 4 cups)
½ medium onion, sliced ¼-inch-thick (about 1 cup)
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) fajita seasoning, divided (store-bought or homemade; see Recipe Notes)
1 pound (16 ounces) fresh chicken tenders without breading
Optional toppings: Cheese, Pico de Gallo, guacamole or avocado, plain Greek yogurt, lettuce or cabbage, lime wedges, cilantro
steps: Add the bell peppers and onion to an 8x8-inch or 9x9-inch microwave-safe glass baking dish (or other 8-10 cup microwave-safe dish) that has a lid.
Add the oil and 2 tablespoons of the seasoning. Toss to coat the vegetables.
Coat the chicken with the remaining 2 tablespoons of seasoning, then place on top of the vegetables.
Cover dish with the lid and microwave on high power (default setting) until the chicken is cooked through (internal temperature of 165°F) and the vegetables are tender, about 7-10 minutes.
Let sit for 2 minutes, then slice the chicken and toss with the vegetable mixture.
Divide the chicken-vegetable mixture between the tortillas (~⅔ cup each). Serve warm, adding toppings as desired.
notes: Boneless skinless chicken breast or steak, cut into ½-inch strips, can be used in place of the chicken tenders.

To make reduced-sodium fajita seasoning (reduces sodium per serving to 515 mg), mix together: 4 teaspoons chili powder, 2 teaspoons sweet or smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1 teaspoon onion powder, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, 2 teaspoons packed brown sugar, ½ teaspoon salt, ¼-½ teaspoon cayenne (to taste).

title: Microwave Chocolate Mug Cake
ingredientLines: 1 tablespoon semi-sweet or dark chocolate chips
steps: Place the flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt in a 12-ounce microwave-safe ceramic mug. Whisk with a fork.
Add the milk, oil, and vanilla. Whisk again with the fork until smooth.
Stir in the chocolate chips.
Microwave on high power (default setting) for 1 minute.
Microwave for another 30 seconds if needed, but be careful not to overcook or the cake will be dry.
Let sit to cool slightly and firm up, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: This recipe works well as a quick single-serving dessert when you are craving something sweet.
For a chocolate -peanut butter flavor, swap out the chocolate chips for one tablespoon of peanut butter.
Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk if desired.

title: Microwave French Toast
servingSize: 1 mug or bowl without optional toppings
ingredientLines: Optional toppings: Powdered sugar, fruit compote, fresh fruit, maple syrup, Greek yogurt, sliced almonds, chocolate-hazelnut spread
steps: Add the butter to a microwave-safe mug or bowl.
Place in the microwave and cook on high (default power) until melted, about 15-30 seconds. Set aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, tear the bread into bite-sized pieces. Set aside.
When the butter has cooled, add the milk, egg, brown sugar, cinnamon, and vanilla to the mug or bowl. Whisk with a fork to combine.
Add the pieces of bread, stirring to coat and pressing them down into the milk-egg mixture. Let sit for 1-2 minutes to soak.
Place in the microwave on top of a plate or paper towel. Cook on high (default power) until the liquid is fully set, about 1½-2 minutes.
Let sit for 2 minutes, then serve warm, topping as desired.

title: Microwave Turkey and Vegetable Omelet
ingredientLines: 2 slices deli turkey, chopped or torn into small pieces
½ medium bell pepper, diced (about ½ cup)
¼ cup chopped fresh spinach or broccoli
steps: Spray the inside of a microwave-safe mug or bowl with nonstick cooking spray.
Add the eggs, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper. Whisk with a fork to combine.
Add the turkey, bell pepper, and spinach or broccoli. Stir to combine.
Microwave on high power (default setting) in 1-minute increments until the eggs are fully set. This will take about 2-3 minutes in total.
Let sit for 2 minutes, then serve warm.
notes: Consider using a different fresh or cooked vegetable(s) and/or a different cooked protein. This is a great way to use up leftovers.

title: Microwave Vegetable Omelet in a Mug
ingredientLines: 1 cup chopped fresh or frozen vegetables (one type or a combination; e.g. onion, bell pepper, mushrooms, spinach, tomato, asparagus)
¼ cup shredded cheese (e.g. cheddar, mozzarella, feta)
steps: Spray the inside of a microwave-safe mug with nonstick cooking spray. Add the selected vegetable(s) and water.
Microwave on high power (default setting) until the vegetables are tender, about ½-3 minutes depending on the type of vegetable(s).
Use a paper towel to carefully soak up any liquid in the mug.
Add the eggs and cheese, whisking with a fork to combine. Microwave on high power (default setting) for 1 minute.
Stir gently with the fork, then continue microwaving until the eggs are just set but still moist, about 15-45 seconds.
Let cool slightly, then serve warm.
notes: The handle of the mug may get hot. Be careful when removing the mug from the microwave, using hot pads or oven mitts if needed.
This can be made with pre-cooked or leftover cooked vegetables. Reduce the amount to ½ cup, omit the water, and skip steps 2-3.
This recipe can be made in a microwave-safe bowl instead of a mug.

title: Mini Pumpkin Muffins
ingredientLines: 1½ cups flour (try using 1 cup whole-wheat flour and ½ cup white all-purpose flour)
⅓ cup mini dark chocolate chips
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
In a mixing bowl, add the pureed pumpkin, oil, yogurt, eggs, sugar, and vanilla. Stir to combine.
In a separate mixing bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and pumpkin pie spice. Whisk to combine.
Combine the wet and dry ingredients. Stir until combined.
Add the chocolate chips. Stir to combine.
Spoon the batter into a greased mini muffin tin, filling each cup about ¾ of the way full.
Bake for 15 minutes. To check if they are done, press lightly on each muffin. The muffin should spring back up when pressed.
notes: The recipes makes 12 regular sized muffins. Regular sized muffins will take about 22-25 minutes to cook.
If you do not have pumpkin pie spice, a mix of any of the following spices will work: cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, allspice.
credit: Submitted by Robin LaCroix RD, White River Junction VA

title: Mini Turkey Meatloaves
ingredientLines: ½ cup shredded or grated carrots
¼ cup frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed to remove liquid
⅓ cup shredded or grated parmesan cheese
½ teaspoon Italian seasoning or oregano
6 tablespoons tomato sauce or ketchup, divided
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.

In a medium mixing bowl, add the ground turkey, oats, carrots, spinach, parmesan cheese, egg, garlic powder, Italian seasoning or oregano, salt, pepper, Worcestershire sauce, and 3 tablespoons of the tomato sauce or ketchup. Gently knead the mixture together until well-combined.
Spray 8 regular-sized muffin tin cups with nonstick spray.
Fill each prepared muffin tin cup with the meatloaf mixture. If needed, prepare an additional 1-2 cups for any extra meatloaf mixture.
In a small bowl, stir together the remaining 3 tablespoons of tomato sauce or ketchup with the brown sugar. Spread ½ tablespoon of this mixture over each meatloaf.
Bake until the center reaches 165°F, about 25-30 minutes.

Cool slightly, then remove from the muffin tins and serve warm. Refrigerate for up to 4 days, freeze for up to 3 months. To serve, thaw in the refrigerator and heat in the microwave or oven to an internal temperature of 165°F.
notes: For a fun and tasty topping, “frost” the mini meatloaves with mashed potatoes or mashed sweet potatoes.
credit: Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Naan Vegetable Pizza
ingredientLines: 3 tablespoons pizza sauce or marinara sauce (store-bought or homemade)
½ cup chopped vegetables (one type or a combination; e.g. mushrooms, broccoli, onion, bell peppers, tomatoes)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Place the naan bread on a cutting board.
Add the sauce and spread evenly over the bread.
Sprinkle evenly with the cheese and vegetables.
Transfer the naan bread with toppings to the oven, placing it directly on the oven rack.
Bake until the cheese is melted, about 7-9 minutes.
Carefully remove the pizza from the oven and transfer to the cutting board. Let cool for 5 minutes.
Cut in half with a pizza cutter or large knife.
Serve warm.
notes: Consider adding lean meat such as ham, turkey pepperoni, or cooked chicken sausage.

title: No-Bake Energy Balls
ingredientLines: ⅔ cup toasted unsweetened coconut flakes
½ cup flax meal (ground flax seed)
½ cup toasted unsalted pepitas (green pumpkin seeds) or shelled sunflower seeds
½ cup unsweetened nut or seed butter (e.g. peanut butter, almond butter, sunflower butter)
1 tablespoon chia seeds or hemp hearts (hulled hemp seeds)
steps: In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the oats, coconut, flax meal, pepitas, nut or seed butter, honey, chia seeds or hemp hearts, vanilla, and cinnamon.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator to chill for 30 minutes.
Roll the mixture into 1-inch balls. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks, or freeze for up to 3 months.
notes: Substitute mini dark chocolate chips for some or all of the pepitas, if desired.

title: No-Bake Gingerbread Energy Bites
ingredientLines: ½ cup almond meal or almond flour
1½ cups roughly chopped pitted dates, packed
steps: Add the oats, almond meal, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and clove to a food processor. Pulse until the mixture is a fine texture like flour.
Add the dates, honey, and vanilla. Pulse until the mixture comes together.
Use a small scoop or spoon (about a tablespoon) to portion the mixture out, then roll the mixture into balls.
Serve right away, or chill before serving.
notes: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks, or freeze for up to 1 year.
Nuts or seeds can be substituted for the almond meal, if desired. Add to the food processor first and pulse until finely ground.
Try new flavors by changing the flavor of extract used (e.g. almond extract, orange extract) or the spices used (e.g. pumpkin pie spice, apple pie spice).

title: No-Bake Mini Cheesecakes
ingredientLines: ¼ cup finely ground graham cracker crumbs (about 1 full graham cracker sheet)
¾ cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt
4 ounces reduced-fat cream cheese (Neufchatel), softened at room temperature
steps: In a small bowl, stir together the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and cinnamon to form a crumbly mixture.
Gather four small jars or other serving containers and divide the mixture between them, about 1 tablespoon in each. Press down to form a crust.

In a medium mixing bowl, use an electric mixer to beat together the Greek yogurt, cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla. Continue to beat until the mixture is completely smooth and resembles a very thick whipped cream.
Divide the yogurt-cream cheese mixture between the jars.
Place in the refrigerator to chill, at least 1 hour.
Serve cold.

title: No-Bake Mini Pumpkin Cheesecakes
ingredientLines: ½ cup uncooked old fashioned (rolled) oats
1 (8-ounce) package cream cheese, softened at room temperature
¾ cup pumpkin puree (about half of a 15-ounce can)
½ cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt (about one 5.3-ounce container)
steps: Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oats and pecans. Cook until lightly browned and fragrant, about 6-8 minutes, stirring often.
Transfer the oats and pecans to a food processor, along with the brown sugar, butter, and ½ teaspoon of the cinnamon.
Pulse to chop, then continue blending until the mixture looks like wet sand, about 2-3 minutes. Transfer the mixture to a bowl or plate and set aside.

In the food processor, add the cream cheese, pumpkin puree, yogurt, sugar, and remaining 1½ teaspoons cinnamon. Blend until completely smooth and airy, about 3-5 minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.

Gather eight small (~½-cup) jars, drinking glasses, bowls, or storage containers. Add 1 tablespoon of the oat mixture to each and press down firmly to make a crust. Divide the cream cheese mixture over the crusts (~⅓ cup each), followed by the remaining oat mixture (~½ teaspoon each).
Cover the containers with lids or plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, then serve cold.

title: Okra with Tomatoes
ingredientLines: 1½ pounds (24 ounces) fresh or frozen okra, trimmed and cut into bite-sized pieces
1 teaspoon chopped fresh oregano (or ¼ teaspoon dried)
steps: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the okra and cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, water, oregano, Cajun seasoning, and lemon juice.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to low.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook until the okra is tender, about 15-20 minutes.
notes: This recipe goes well with rice and fish.
If you don’t like okra, try substituting chopped collard greens or mustard greens (leaves and stems).

title: Olive Oil Granola
ingredientLines: ½ cup maple syrup or packed brown sugar
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon or pumpkin pie spice
½ cup dried fruit (one type or a combination; e.g. raisins, dried cranberries, dried cherries, dried apricots), chopped if large (optional)
steps: Preheat oven to 300°F
In a large bowl, combine the oats, walnuts, pumpkin seeds, shredded coconut, maple syrup or brown sugar, olive oil, cinnamon or pumpkin pie spice, and salt.
Divide the mixture between 2 rimmed baking sheets and spread in an even layer.
Bake until golden-brown and crispy, about 30-45 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
Transfer the granola to a large bowl.
Add the dried fruit (if using). Stir to combine.
Once cool, transfer to an air-tight container and store for up to 1 month.
notes: This granola can be eaten on it’s own as a snack, or on top of another food item such as yogurt or fruit.
Any chopped nut can be substituted for the walnuts.
An additional cup of nuts or another large seed, such as sunflower seeds, can be substituted for the pumpkin seeds.

title: One-Pot Chicken Barley Stew
ingredientLines: 6 cups (48 ounces) low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
1 (10-ounce) package frozen mixed vegetables (e.g. green beans, carrots, corn, peas)
steps: Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion. Cook, stirring often, until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the garlic, thyme, black pepper, and salt. Cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the broth and barley.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook until the barley is tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the mixed vegetables and cooked chicken.
Cook until warmed through, about 4-6 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: This recipe works well with leftover chicken, rotisserie chicken, or canned chicken.
If using raw chicken, add it at the beginning of cooking with the onion.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Orange Beef and Vegetable Stir-Fry
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) lean beef steak (e.g. round, sirloin), sliced against the grain into thin strips
1 tablespoon peanut, canola, or avocado oil
3-4 scallions (green onions), thinly sliced (about ½ cup)
1 tablespoon minced or grated fresh ginger (or about 1 teaspoon dried ginger)
steps: Add the egg to a medium bowl and beat lightly.
Add the steak to the bowl with the egg and toss to coat.
Sprinkle the cornstarch over the steak and toss to coat.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together the orange juice, soy sauce, vinegar, and honey to make a sauce. Set aside.
Heat a large wok or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the scallions, garlic, and ginger. Cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the steak to the pan and continue cooking, stirring often, until lightly browned, about 4-8 minutes.
Add the sauce and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.
Add the stir-fry vegetables and cook until the vegetables are heated through, about 4-6 minutes.
Serve warm, on its own or over a cooked grain if desired.
notes: Substitute another protein – such as chicken, pork, or shrimp – for the steak if desired.

title: Oven-Baked Buffalo Chicken Quesadilla
ingredientLines: ⅔ cup reduced-fat shredded cheese, divided
⅓ cup broccoli or cauliflower florets
¼ cup no-salt-added white beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Evenly coat a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Place one of the tortillas on the baking sheet.
Sprinkle ⅓ cup of the cheese over the tortilla, in an even layer.
Add the bell pepper, broccoli, chicken, tomato, onion, beans, and hot sauce.
Top with the remaining ⅓ cup cheese.
Place the second tortilla on top.
Place the baking sheet in the oven.
Cook until the tortillas are crisp and the cheese is melted, about 10-15 minutes.
notes: No chicken on hand? Substitute ground turkey or use your favorite bean for great protein and fiber.
Garnishes well with guacamole, light sour cream, plain Greek yogurt, or salsa.
credit: Submitted by Katie Kirzoncic RD, LDN, Lebanon VAMC

title: Oven-Baked Fish Sticks
ingredientLines: 2 (4- to 6-ounce) white fish fillets (e.g. flounder, cod, tilapia), cut lengthwise into four strips each
½ cup whole-wheat or Panko breadcrumbs
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Cover a 9x13-inch baking sheet with foil and spray the foil with nonstick spray. Set aside.
Set up a breading station by placing three bowls, pie dishes, or other shallow dishes in a row.
In the first dish, add the flour. In the second dish, add the milk. In the third dish, add and stir together the breadcrumbs, parmesan, and seasoning blend.
Dip one strip of fish into the flour (first dish) to coat it evenly on all sides. Shake off any excess flour.
Add the strip of fish to the milk (second dish) to coat evenly on all sides. Shake to remove any excess milk.
Add the strip of fish to the breadcrumb mixture (third dish) to coat it evenly on all sides.
Place the strip of fish onto the prepared baking sheet.
Repeat steps 4-7 with the remaining strips of fish, then discard any leftover breading ingredients.
Bake the breaded fish strips for 10 minutes, then flip each strip over and continue baking until golden-brown and cooked through, about 5-10 minutes. Serve immediately.

title: Oven-Roasted Cauliflower
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Meanwhile, remove the outer leaves from the cauliflower head, then cut the florets away from the stalk. Discard the stalk and leaves.
Cut the cauliflower florets into bite-sized (about 1-inch) pieces.
Add the cauliflower, oil, salt, and black pepper to a large bowl. Toss to combine and coat the cauliflower.
Transfer the cauliflower to a baking sheet and spread into an even layer.
Bake until fork-tender and starting to brown, about 20-25 minutes, stirring about halfway through the cooking time.
Serve warm.
notes: Any other vegetable (e.g. broccoli, Brussels sprouts, carrots), can be roasted using this recipe. Note that the preparation and cooking time will likely vary.
For a boost of flavor, try adding another spice or herb such as coriander, cumin, dried dill, garlic powder, or ground ginger.

title: Parmesan Zucchini Noodles (Zoodles)
ingredientLines: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh basil (or 1 teaspoon dried basil)
steps: Using a spiralizer, cut the zucchini into noodles.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the zucchini noodles and cook, tossing occasionally, until slightly wilted and tender, about 5 minutes. Be careful to not overcook or they will get mushy.
Remove from the heat.
Add the parmesan, black pepper, and basil. Toss to combine.
Serve warm.
notes: If you do not have a spiralizer, slice the zucchini lengthwise into thin strips, then slice them again to resemble long thin noodles.
Substitute yellow summer squash for the zucchini, if desired.

title: Pasta Primavera
ingredientLines: 1 pound fresh or frozen broccoli florets (about 6 cups)
1 pound fresh or frozen asparagus, ends snapped off and cut into 2-inch pieces
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes
steps: Add the oil, broth, linguine, onion, broccoli, asparagus, mushrooms, garlic, red pepper flakes, and black pepper to a large pot.
Set the pot over high heat and bring to a boil.
As soon as the liquid comes to a boil, set a timer for 7 minutes.
Toss the ingredients in the pot constantly with long-handled tongs.
Once the 7 minutes is up, add the peas, heavy whipping cream, Parmesan cheese, and lemon zest.
Continue cooking, tossing frequently, until the pasta and veggies are tender.
Remove the pot from heat. Note that much of the liquid will have evaporated, but not all.
Let the pasta sit for a couple minutes to cool slightly. The sauce will continue to thicken during this time.
Serve warm.
credit: Inspired by a recipe submitted by Christina Corkern RD, LD/N

title: Pasta Skillet with Sausage and Vegetables
ingredientLines: 8 ounces uncooked whole-grain rotini pasta (half of a 16-ounce box)
2 cups fresh vegetables, chopped as needed (one type or a combination; e.g. zucchini, mushrooms, broccoli, peppers, onion) or 1 (16-ounce) bag frozen vegetables
2 pre -cooked Italian chicken sausage links, cut into ¼- to ½-inch pieces (about 6 ounces)
½ cup grated or shredded parmesan cheese
steps: Cook the pasta according to the box directions. Before draining the pasta, measure off ½ cup of the pasta cooking water. Drain the pasta into a colander and set aside.
Place the empty pasta pot back on the stove over medium heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the selected vegetables. Cook, stirring often, until tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the sausage and cook, stirring often, for 3-5 minutes.
Add the marinara sauce and Italian seasoning. Add the reserved pasta water, as needed, to thin out the sauce if it gets too thick and evaporated as you cook.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until simmering, about 4-5 minutes. Then add the cooked pasta and stir to combine.
Remove from heat and add the parmesan. Serve warm.
notes: This dish can be made with any shape of whole-grain pasta you prefer, such as penne, bowties, or rotini. Cooked spaghetti squash or zucchini noodles could be used in place of the pasta, for lower carbohydrates and more fiber.
Chicken sausage usually comes fully cooked with options for sweet or spicy versions. Any leftover sausage links can be placed in a plastic zip-top bag and frozen for later use.

title: Pasta with Chickpeas
ingredientLines: 1 (15.5-ounce) can no-salt-added garbanzo beans, drained and rinsed
1 cup whole-wheat short pasta (e.g. elbows, orzo, small shells, rotini), uncooked
Crushed red pepper flakes, to taste, optional
steps: Heat a large sauté pan or saucepan (pot) over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring frequently, until it becomes lightly browned, about 1-2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, scraping up any browned bits on the bottom of the pan.
Add the chickpeas, zucchini, pasta, diced tomatoes with their juice, and water.
Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cook until the pasta is tender and much of the liquid has been absorbed, about 15-20 minutes.
Serve warm, adding the crushed red pepper flakes as desired for additional spice.
notes: Pairs well with a garnish of grated parmesan and/or fresh chopped basil on top.
credit: Adapted from dinnerwithjulie.com | Submitted by Brandi Kozlowski DTR

title: Peanut Butter and Banana Milkshake
ingredientLines: 4 frozen medium bananas, peeled and sliced before freezing
¾ cup lowfat (1%) milk, plus more as needed to adjust the consistency
steps: Add the bananas, milk, and peanut butter to a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth and thick (milkshake consistency), add more milk as needed to adjust the consistency.
Serve immediately.
notes: Any time you have overripe bananas, peel them and cut them into chunks. Then, toss them into a zip-top plastic bag or a freezer-safe container with a lid and freeze until needed.
Look for peanut butter without added honey or sugar.
Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk if desired.
Add 2 tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder for a chocolate-peanut butter flavor.
Portion any leftovers into a popsicle tray or small paper cups with a popsicle stick for a frozen sweet treat.

title: Peanut Butter Energy Bars
ingredientLines: ½ cup dried tart cherries, chopped
steps: Coat the inside of a 9x13-inch baking dish with nonstick spray.
In a large mixing bowl, stir together the peanut butter, vanilla, honey, and ground flaxseed.
Stir in the oats, dried cherries and sliced almonds.
Press the mixture firmly into prepared pan, the cover with a lid or plastic wrap. Place in the refrigerator to chill for at least 1 hour.
Remove from the refrigerator and cut into 24 bars.
Wrap each bar and store in refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.
notes: Substitute your favorite nuts, nut butter, or dried fruit as desired.
Substitute ½ cup mini semi-sweet chocolate chips for the dried fruit, if desired.

title: Peanut Slaw with Noodles
ingredientLines: 4 ounces whole-wheat spaghetti (¼th of a 16-ounce package)
1 small purple (red) or green cabbage (about 2 pounds), cut into quarters and core removed
1 bunch green onions, trimmed and sliced into thin rounds
3 tablespoons white wine vinegar or rice vinegar
steps: Bring 6 cups of water to a boil in a large saucepan (pot).
Break the spaghetti noodles in half and add to the boiling water.
Cook the spaghetti for the amount of time listed on the package instructions, then drain into a colander (strainer).
Rinse the cooked spaghetti under cold water and set aside.
Thinly slice the cabbage crosswise.
Grate the carrots, or slice into thin ribbons using a peeler.

In a 2-cup liquid measuring cup or medium bowl, whisk together the peanut dressing ingredients until smooth. If the mixture is too thick, add warm water to thin a bit. A mason jar with lid also works well to shake the dressing.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked spaghetti noodles, cabbage, carrots, and green onions.
Pour dressing over the vegetables and toss to coat.
For best flavor, set aside to marinate for 20 minutes before serving.
Serve at room temperature, or the dish can be chilled or warmed if desired.
notes: Save time by using 2 (14-ounce) bags of coleslaw mix in place of the cabbage.
Add cooked chicken or tofu cubes to make a complete meal.
This slaw keeps very well for a few days (covered and refrigerated) and makes great leftovers for lunch
credit: Adapted from Cookie and Kate Blog | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Pesto and Chickpea Pita Pizzas
ingredientLines: 4 tablespoons (¼ cup) pesto, divided (store-bought or homemade)
½ cup chopped bell pepper (about ½ medium bell pepper), divided
½ cup cooked or canned chickpeas (garbanzo beans), drained and rinsed, divided
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the pita bread rounds on the baking sheet and bake for 5 minutes
Remove from the oven and spread 2 tablespoons of the pesto on each pita round, leaving about a ½-inch area around the edges.
Top each pita round with ¼ cup of the bell pepper and ¼ cup of the chickpeas.
Sprinkle each pita round with 2 tablespoons of the mozzarella.
Place back in the oven and bake until the cheese has melted and the bell peppers are soft, about 9-11 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: You can make these pizzas in the microwave if you do not mind a softer crust. Simply add the toppings and microwave, one at a time, on high (default power) for 1-3 minutes.
Another vegetable (e.g. mushrooms, onion, spinach) can be substituted for the bell peppers, if desired.

title: Pesto Quinoa Bowl
ingredientLines: 1 (5-ounce) bag fresh baby spinach (or ½ cup frozen chopped spinach)
1 cup cherry tomatoes, cut in half
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added canned white beans (e.g. Cannellini, Great Northern), drained and rinsed
¼-½ teaspoon ground black pepper, to taste
5 tablespoons shredded or grated fresh parmesan cheese (optional)
steps: Add the quinoa and water to a medium saucepan.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cover the saucepan with a lid and cook until the quinoa is tender and the water is absorbed, about 10-15 minutes. Remove the saucepan from the heat and set aside.
While the quinoa cooks, heat the oil and garlic in a medium skillet over medium heat just until fragrant, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the green beans and cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes.
Add the spinach. Cook, stirring often, until the spinach is wilted and the green beans are tender. Turn off the heat.
Add the cooked quinoa, tomatoes, beans, pesto, and pepper. Toss until well combined.
Divide into five serving bowls.
Serve warm, topping each bowl with 1 tablespoon parmesan cheese if desired.
notes: Consider substituting mushrooms, zucchini, or onion for the green beans, or use a combination of vegetables.
credit: Submitted by VHA Healthy Teaching Kitchen Program

title: Pico de Gallo (Salsa Fresca)
ingredientLines: 1 jalapeño or 2 serrano chiles, ribs and seeds removed, minced
¼ cup minced fresh cilantro leaves
½ cup finely chopped onion (about ½ medium onion)
steps: In a medium mixing bowl, add the tomatoes, jalapeno or serrano chiles, cilantro, lime juice, onion, and salt.
Stir to combine.
Set in the refrigerator to chill for at least 15 minutes before serving.
Serve cold or at room temperature, as a dip or a condiment.
notes: To make the salsa hotter, add a quarter to half of the chile seeds to the salsa.
To cut down on the raw onion flavor, let the chopped onion sit in the bowl with the lime juice while you prepare the other ingredients or rinse it under cold water for 30 seconds.

title: Plant-Powered Chocolate Muffins
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Prepare muffin tin by coating with nonstick cooking spray. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, add hummus, eggs, and mashed bananas. Blend well using a hand mixer.
Add sugar and oil into hummus mixture and blend well.
In a small bowl, combine the flour and baking soda. Add to the wet ingredients and blend just until combined.
Gently fold the chocolate chips into the mixture.
Scoop batter into muffin tins, filling each ~¾ full.
Bake mini muffins for 15-16 minutes and regular sized muffins for 20-24 minutes, or until an inserted toothpick comes out clean.
Allow to cool and enjoy.
notes: If you cannot find chocolate hummus, you may substitute ¼ cup cocoa powder, 3 tablespoons of sugar and 1 cup white beans, pureed.
Muffins will store well in the refrigerator for one week or freezer for up to 3 months.
credit: Adapted from Sarahremmer.com| Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Pomegranate-Poached Pears
ingredientLines: 4 ripe firm pears (Bosc pears work best, but can also use Bartlett or Anjou)
1 cup nonfat plain or vanilla Greek yogurt
steps: Peel the pears and cut them in half. Remove the cores with a spoon or melon baller.
Place the pears flat-side-down in a large saucepan.
Pour the pomegranate juice over the pears and add the cinnamon stick to the pan.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Cover the pan with a lid and reduce the heat to low.
Simmer gently until the pears are tender when pierced with a fork, about 25-30 minutes, turning them over gently once or twice while they cook so they color evenly.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer the pears to a serving dish.
Garnish each pear half with 2 tablespoons of the yogurt and ½ tablespoon of the toasted almonds.
Serve warm.
notes: To toast the almonds, cook them in a dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, about 3 -5 minutes.
Any leftover pomegranate juice can be saved for putting in a smoothie, adding to beef stew, or reducing and used as a sauce over pork or chicken.
Another juice (e.g. cranberry, cherry, apple) can be used in place of the pomegranate juice if desired.

title: Pork and Rice Skillet
ingredientLines: 1 pound boneless pork chops, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the pork, onion, and garlic.
Sauté until the pork is browned and the onions are tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the rice, Italian seasoning, frozen peas and carrots, and broth.
Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to a simmer and cover the pan with a lid.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the rice is tender and the pork is fully cooked, about 30-45 minutes.
Stir in the yogurt and cheese until combined and the cheese is melted.
Serve warm.
notes: To reduce carbohydrate content further, try substituting non-starchy vegetables (e.g. green beans, broccoli, cauliflower, peppers, asparagus, mushrooms) for the peas and carrots.
To reduce cooking time, try using 10-minute brown rice.
credit: Adapted from www.iwashyoudry.com | Submitted by Kristen Bertram RDN, CD

title: Pork and Vegetable Fried Rice
ingredientLines: 1 (8.8-ounce) package microwavable brown rice, cooked according to the package directions
½ pound boneless pork loin, cut into ½-inch pieces
½ pound pea pods, cut into 1-inch pieces
½ pound asparagus, cut into 1-inch pieces
steps: Coat a large nonstick wok or skillet with cooking spray and place over medium heat.
Once the pan is hot, add the eggs and cook, stirring gently, until they are just set, about 30-60 seconds. Transfer to a small bowl and set aside.
Heat 1 teaspoon of the canola oil in the same now-empty pan over medium-high heat.
Sprinkle the salt evenly over the pork.
Add the pork to the pan. Cook, stirring constantly, until browned on all sides, about 2 minutes. Transfer to the bowl with the cooked eggs and set aside.
Heat the remaining 1 teaspoon of oil in the same pan.
Add the pea pods and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.
Add the bell pepper, scallions, garlic, and ginger. Cook, stirring constantly, until just tender, about 2 minutes.
Add the cooked rice, soy sauce, and vinegar. Cook until the liquid is absorbed, about 30-60 seconds.
Fold in the cooked eggs and pork.
Remove from the heat, stirring in the sesame oil and/or hot sauce if desired.
Serve warm.
notes: Substitute any vegetables of your choice for the pea pods and bell peppers, or try chicken breast instead of pork.
credit: Adapted from www.smittenkitchen.com | Submitted by Jessica Long, MS, RDN

title: Pork Egg Roll in a Bowl
ingredientLines: 5 scallions (green onions), sliced, white and green parts separated
1 tablespoon Sriracha or garlic chili sauce
2 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds, if desired
steps: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the sesame oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the garlic, onion, and the white portion of the scallions.
Sauté until the onions are soft and the garlic is fragrant, about 4-5 minutes.
Add the ground pork, ground ginger, and Sriracha or garlic chili sauce.
Sauté until the pork is cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the coleslaw mix, soy sauce, and rice wine vinegar.
Sauté until the cabbage is tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Serve, topped with the green portion of the scallions and the sesame seeds, if using.
notes: For more cost savings, shred your own cabbage. You will need about 4-6 cups shredded cabbage.
credit: Adapted from nomnompaleo.com | Submitted by JoAnna Hazard RD

title: Pork Tenderloin Kebabs
ingredientLines: 2 bell peppers, diced (any color, or a variety)
1 red onion, cut into 1- to 2-inch chunks
10 ounces mushrooms, cut in half if wider than about 1 inch
steps: If roasting in the oven, preheat the oven to 400°F. If grilling, preheat the grill to medium-high heat (350-400°F).
Place 12 wooden skewers in warm water to soak for 10-15 minutes. If using metal skewers, soaking is not needed.
Cut the pork tenderloin into 1-inch cubes. Try to keep the cubes small and consistent in size, so they cook quickly and evenly.
In a large bowl, combine the bell peppers, zucchini, onion, mushrooms, pineapple, peach, oil, salt, and pepper.
Assemble the kebabs by alternating between the cubed pork and the various vegetable and fruit pieces.
Roast or grill the kebabs until the pork is cooked to an internal temperature of 145°F, about 10-15 minutes, turning every 3-5 minutes if grilling.
Serve warm.
notes: Can’t find a 1-pound pork tenderloin? Substitute with 1 pound of boneless pork chops.
credit: Adapted from America’s Test Kitchen | Submitted by Dana Herring MS, RDN

title: Powered-Up Microwave Oatmeal
ingredientLines: 1 tablespoon flax meal (ground flaxseed) or chia seeds
1 tablespoon maple syrup or packed brown sugar
steps: In a microwave-safe bowl, stir together the oats, milk, hemp hearts, flax meal or chia seeds, maple syrup or brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt.
Microwave on high power (default setting) for 2 minutes.
Remove from the microwave and let sit to thicken and cool slightly, about 1-2 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: For a quick make-ahead option, add all the ingredients except the milk to a plastic ziptop bag. When ready to eat, pour into a microwave-safe bowl along with the milk and cook as directed.
Add toppings such as fruit, shredded coconut, nuts, or seeds as desired.

title: Pressure Cooker-Braised Chicken Thighs
servingSize: 1 chicken thigh with a quarter of the sauce
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) baby portabella or button mushrooms, sliced ½-inch thick
½ cup low-sodium chicken or beef broth
1½ pounds bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed (4 thighs, about 5 to 7 ounces each)
steps: Heat the pot of a pressure cooker over medium-high heat or heat an electric pressure cooker on high heat sauté.
Add the oil, mushrooms, onion, salt, and black pepper. Cook, stirring often, until the onions soften and the mushrooms have released their liquid, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, flour, and sage. Cook, stirring often, until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the diced tomatoes with their juice, broth, and vinegar, scraping up any browned bits with a spoon or spatula.
Place the chicken thighs in the pot and spoon some of the liquid-vegetable mixture over the tops.

Lock the lid in place and close the pressure valve. For a stovetop cooker, bring to pressure over high heat and then reduce to low heat. Set an electric pressure cooker to high pressure. Cook for 15 minutes, with the time starting after the pressure has built up.
Turn off the heat and turn the pressure valve to vent to release the pressure. Once the pressure is completely released, carefully open the lid, allowing the steam to escape away from you.
Remove the chicken, cover with foil, and set aside.
Return the pot to medium-high heat or high heat sauté. Bring the liquid to a simmer and cook until thickened into a sauce, about 5 minutes.
Stir the parsley into the sauce, then divide the sauce over the chicken thighs and serve warm.
credit: Adapted from America’s Test Kitchen | Submitted by Dana Herring MS, RDN

title: Pumpkin Cheesecake Dip
ingredientLines: ¾ cup pumpkin puree (about half of a 15-ounce can)
steps: Add the cream cheese and Greek yogurt to the bowl of a food processor. Blend until smooth, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the pumpkin puree, pumpkin pie spice, maple syrup or honey, and salt. Blend until completely combined, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed, about 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to a medium serving bowl or storage container.
Cover with a lid or plastic wrap. Place in the refrigerator to chill for at least 30 minutes.
Serve cold.
notes: If you don’t have pumpkin pie spice, you can substitute ground cinnamon.
This dip goes well with apple slices, graham crackers, and pretzels.
This dip will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Freezing is not recommended.

title: Pumpkin Mousse
ingredientLines: ½ cup 100% pure pumpkin puree (canned or cooked from fresh)
steps: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the milk and pudding mix for 2 minutes. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the pumpkin, cinnamon, ginger, and allspice.
Add the pumpkin mixture to the prepared pudding. Stir to combine.
Gently fold ½ cup of the whipped topping into the pumpkin-pudding mixture until combined.
Divide the mixture between four serving bowls.
Refrigerate until set, about 1 hour.
Serve cold, garnishing each serving with 2 tablespoons of the remaining whipped topping.
notes: To reduce the sugar content, substitute sugar-free instant butterscotch pudding.
Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk if desired.
Try adding any leftover pumpkin puree to smoothies, oatmeal, soup, chili, or yogurt.

title: Quick-Pickled Onions
ingredientLines: 3 tablespoons vinegar (any flavor; e.g. white vinegar, red wine vinegar, apple cider vinegar)
½ medium onion, thinly sliced (about 1 cup)
steps: In a small to medium mixing bowl, whisk together the vinegar, oil, sugar or honey, salt, and black pepper.
Add the onion and toss to coat.
Let sit at room temperature for 1 hour or in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Serve as desired. Quick-pickled onions will keep in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.
notes: For best flavor, slice the onion vertically along the grain (long stripes going towards the root).
