Pickled onions are a great topping for tacos, salads, burgers, and barbecue-flavored sandwiches.
For an even quicker pickle, double the brine (everything except the

title: Quinoa and Black Bean Burrito Bowls
ingredientLines: ¼ cup minced onion (about ½ medium onion)
2 (15-ounce) cans no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) chopped fresh cilantro, divided
8 tablespoons (½ cup) lime juice (about 4 limes), divided
1 cup shredded or chopped lettuce, divided
8 tablespoons (½ cup) chopped bell pepper (about ½ medium bell pepper), divided
8 tablespoons (½ cup) frozen or no-salt-added canned corn (thawed if frozen, drained and rinsed if canned), divided
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) plain nonfat Greek yogurt, divided
Optional toppings: Salsa, sliced avocado, chopped fresh tomato, shredded cheese, hot sauce
steps: Add the quinoa and 2 cups of water to a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer. Cover the pan with a lid and cook until the quinoa is tender, about 10-15 minutes. Remove from the heat and fluff with a fork, then set aside.
While the quinoa is cooking, heat a separate medium saucepan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook until softened and starting to brown, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the black beans, ½ cup of water, 2 tablespoons of the cilantro, the chili powder, and the cayenne. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook until the liquid is mostly evaporated, about 10-15 minutes.
Add 2 tablespoons of the lime juice to the black bean mixture, then remove from the heat.
Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of cilantro and remaining 6 tablespoons (¼ cup plus 2 tablespoons) of lime juice to the quinoa.

Divide the quinoa mixture between four serving bowls. Top each with ¼ cup of the lettuce, ½ cup of the black bean mixture, 2 tablespoons of the bell pepper, 2 tablespoons of the corn, and 1 tablespoon of the Greek yogurt.
Serve, adding other toppings as desired.
credit: Adapted from toriavey.com | Submitted by Janelle Kramer

title: Quinoa-Crust Pizza
ingredientLines: ½ cup pizza sauce or marinara sauce (store-bought or homemade)
1 cup shredded cheese (e.g. mozzarella, Italian blend)
Optional toppings: Chopped or sliced mushrooms, diced bell peppers, pepperoni, diced onion, sliced or crumbled cooked sausage, sliced olives, chopped fresh herbs, red pepper flakes
steps: Add the quinoa to a small mixing bowl. Add enough water to cover the quinoa by at least 1 inch. Let sit overnight, or at least 6 hours.
When the quinoa is done soaking, preheat the oven to 425°F.

Line a 9-inch round cake pan with a cut circle of parchment paper. Add 1 tablespoon of the oil to the pan. Spread the oil around with your hands or a pastry brush until the pan is evenly coated. Set aside.
Drain and rinse the soaked quinoa under running water.
Add the quinoa and ¼ cup water to a blender or food processor.
Add the baking powder, salt, and the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Blend until smooth and creamy. The mixture will look like a thick pancake batter.
Pour the quinoa crust batter into the prepared cake pan and spread into an even layer, then bake for 15 minutes.
Remove the pan from the oven, flip the quinoa crust over in the pan, then return it to oven. Bake until the crust is browned and the edges are crispy, about 10-15 minutes.

Top the crust with the sauce, cheese, and any other toppings you would like. Continue baking until the cheese has melted and started to brown and any vegetable toppings are tender, about 12-15 minutes.
Let the pizza cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a cutting board and cut into eight slices. Serve warm.

title: Quinoa Enchilada Bake
ingredientLines: ½ medium onion, diced (about ½ cup)
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
1 cup shredded Mexican blend cheese, divided
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Spray an 8x8-inch baking dish with cooking spray and set aside.
Add the quinoa and water to a small saucepan and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer. Cook until tender, about 10-15 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Meanwhile, heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add the oil, bell pepper, and onion. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes
Add the chili powder, cumin, and garlic powder. Cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds, then remove from the heat.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the beans, corn, enchilada sauce, green chiles, and ¼ cup of the cheese. Stir in the cooked quinoa and the vegetable mixture.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish. Top with remaining ¾ cup of cheese.
Spray one side of a sheet of foil with cooking spray and place over the baking dish. Wrap around the edges to seal.
Bake for 20 minutes, then remove foil and continue baking until the cheese is melted and the edges are bubbling, about 10 minutes. Let cool for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with the cilantro, then cut into four pieces and serve warm with the lime wedges.
notes: This recipe freezes well, before or after baking. Freeze for up to 3 months. When ready to cook, cover with the foil and place in the preheated oven. Add 10 minutes to the initial cooking time, for a total cooking time of about 40 minutes.

title: Quinoa, Shrimp, and Black Bean Casserole
ingredientLines: 1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
2½ tablespoons dried cilantro (or ½ cup fresh)
1 pound frozen shrimp, thawed and cooked
steps: Heat a medium or large saucepan (pot) over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and garlic.
Cook, stirring often, until the onion is lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the quinoa, broth, cumin, cayenne pepper, and black pepper.
Increase the heat to high and bring mixture to a boil.
Cover the pot with a lid and reduce the heat to simmer.
Cook until the quinoa is tender and most of the broth has been absorbed, about 15-20 minutes.
Stir in the frozen corn, cooked shrimp, black beans and cilantro.
Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until heated through.
notes: To reduce sodium further, try using fresh shrimp, ensuring it is fully cooked prior to serving.
To cook the shrimp with the quinoa, add it during the last 5 minutes of the total cooking time for the quinoa.
credit: Inspired by a recipe submitted by Megan Gundy RD, Hines VAMC

title: Quinoa Tabbouleh
ingredientLines: 1 (15-ounce) can no-salt added chickpeas (garbanzo beans), drained and rinsed
½ cup reduced fat feta, crumbled
steps: Add quinoa and water to a medium saucepan.
Bring water to boil, then turn down the heat to simmer.
Cover and cook until the quinoa is fluffy and chewy, about 15-20 minutes.
Move the saucepan off the heat and keep covered with a lid for 1-2 minutes.

Empty the cooked quinoa into a large bowl and allow it to cool almost to room temperature. You can speed this process up by spreading the quinoa into a thin layer on a baking sheet and stirring it occasionally.
Stir the onion, tomatoes, chickpeas, parsley, mint, garlic and black pepper into the bowl with quinoa.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar and lemon juice.
Pour the dressing over the salad and stir to combine.
Fold in the feta. Serve room temperature or chilled.
notes: For a more traditional tabbouleh, substitute ¾ cup dry bulgur for quinoa, cooked according to package directions.
credit: Adapted from Thekitchn.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Ranch Seasoning Mix (for Dip or Dressing)
ingredientLines: Plain Greek yogurt or low-fat (1%) milk (if making dressing)
steps: Whisk all the dry seasoning mix ingredients together until blended. If you want a more finely-ground seasoning mix, pulse the mixture in a food processor until it reaches your desired consistency.
Store the dry seasoning mix in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 3 months. Three (3) tablespoons of the mix is equal to one packet of store-bought ranch seasoning mix.
To make ranch dip, add 1 tablespoon of the prepared mix to ⅔ cup plain Greek yogurt. To make ranch dressing, add 1 tablespoon of the mix to ⅓ cup milk and ⅓ cup plain Greek yogurt. Stir well.
categories: Dressings, Sauces, and Seasonings: Salad Dressings
Dressings, Sauces, and Seasonings: Seasoning Blends

title: Red Enchilada Sauce
steps: In a medium saucepan, whisk together the oil, flour, chili powder, oregano, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, and salt.
Place the saucepan over medium heat. Heat until bubbling and fragrant, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, water, and brown sugar. Whisk to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer. Cook until slightly thickened, about 8-10 minutes.
Use in recipes as desired. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 14 days or in the freezer up to 6 months.

title: Red Pizza Sauce
steps: Add the tomatoes, garlic, oil, vinegar, oregano, salt, sugar, black pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using) to a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth, about 1-2 minutes.
Use right away, or keep in the refrigerator until needed.
notes: This sauce will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months.
Add other cooked chopped vegetables if desired, either blending them into the sauce or leaving them whole for a chunky sauce. Ideas include bell peppers, onions, carrots, and mushrooms.

title: Rice and Vegetable Medley
ingredientLines: ¼ cup chopped onion (about ¼ medium onion)
½ cup chopped carrots (about 1 medium carrot)
½ cup chopped celery (about 1 stalk celery)
½ cup sliced fresh mushrooms (about 2 ounces)
½ cup green peas, fresh or frozen
steps: Prepare rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Heat medium skillet over medium-high heat.
Add olive oil and heat until shimmering.
Add onions, carrots, and celery to skillet and sauté about 2- 4 minutes.
Add mushrooms to skillet and sauté about 4-5 minutes more.
Stir peas into vegetable mixture until warmed through.
Remove vegetable mixture from skillet and stir into prepared rice.
Add dried fruit to rice and vegetable mixture and mix well.
Serve warm.
notes: Add a protein such as shrimp, chicken, or tofu to make this meal complete.
Swap other dried fruit (e.g. chopped apricots, dates, or cherries, raisins) for the dried cranberries if desired.

title: Roasted Beet Borscht
ingredientLines: 1 pound beets (about 2-3 medium beets), cut into 1-inch chunks
½ teaspoon ground black pepper, divided
2 tablespoons chopped fresh dill (about ½ ounce)
½ cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt
1 medium tart-flavored apple (e.g. Granny Smith), cored and finely chopped (about 1 cup)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
On a baking sheet, toss the beets with 2 tablespoons of the oil, ¼ teaspoon of the salt, and ¼ teaspoon of the black pepper. Roast until tender, about 30-40 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat a large pot over medium heat. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the carrots, onion, the remaining ¼ teaspoon salt, and the remaining ¼ teaspoon black pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until beginning to soften, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and thyme. Cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the broth and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook until the carrots are tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Transfer the beets to a blender, along with the carrots, onion, and enough broth to fill the blender about halfway.
Remove the plastic piece from the center of the blender lid and place a towel over the hole. Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes.
Return the pureed mixture to the pot and stir in the vinegar and sugar or honey. Reheat over the stovetop if needed.
In a small mixing bowl, stir together the yogurt and dill.
Serve warm or chill before serving, topping each serving with 1 tablespoon of the yogurt-dill mixture and 2 tablespoons of the chopped apple.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Roasted Beet Hummus
ingredientLines: 1 medium beet, cut into 1-inch chunks (about 1½ cups)
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added white beans (e.g. great northern, cannellini), drained and rinsed
2 tablespoons tahini (sesame seed paste; can substitute creamy peanut butter)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Place the beet pieces on a baking sheet and toss with ½ tablespoon of the oil. Place in the oven and roast until fork-tender, about 30-40 minutes.
Meanwhile add the garlic and 2 tablespoons of the lemon juice to a small bowl and stir to combine. Set aside.
Add ¼ cup of the roasted beet to a food processor. Pulse until broken down into small pieces.

Add the garlic-lemon juice mixture, ½ teaspoon lemon zest, beans, tahini, salt, and black pepper. Puree the mixture until very smooth, while slowly drizzling in the remaining 3½ tablespoons of oil, about 3-4 minutes.
Finely chop the remaining roasted beet. Add to a small bowl and toss with any remaining lemon zest and 1 tablespoon lemon juice. Set aside.
Transfer the pureed mixture to a serving dish and garnish with the chopped beet and lemon mixture.
Serve right away, or store in an air-tight container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. May be frozen if desired.

title: Roasted Beets with Feta
ingredientLines: 4 small beets, peeled and diced (about 2 cups)
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a medium bowl, toss together the beets, oil, and salt.
Transfer the beets to a baking sheet and spread into a single layer.
Roast for until fork tender, about 25-30 minutes, tossing halfway through the cooking time.
Remove from the oven and set aside to cool slightly, about 8-10 minutes.
Return the beets to the bowl.
Add the parsley, balsamic vinegar, and red wine vinegar. Toss to combine.
Serve right away, or chill before serving. Top each serving with 1 tablespoon of the feta just before serving.

title: Roasted Broccoli, Fennel, and Chickpeas
ingredientLines: ½ jalapeno, membranes and seeds removed, minced
1 medium head broccoli, cut into florets (about 3 cups)
1 medium fennel bulb, cored and sliced about
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added chickpeas (garbanzo beans), drained and rinsed
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the yogurt, parsley, jalapeño, lemon juice, and black pepper. Set aside.
In a separate large mixing bowl, stir together the oil, garlic, coriander, cumin, paprika, and salt.
Add the broccoli, fennel, and chickpeas. Toss to combine and coat with the oil-seasoning mixture
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking sheet, spreading it into a single layer.
Roast for 12 minutes, then remove from the oven and stir the mixture on the baking sheet.
Spread the mixture back out into a single layer, then place back in the oven.
Continue cooking until browned and the vegetables are fork-tender, about 10-12 minutes.
Transfer the roasted vegetable-chickpea mixture to the bowl with the yogurt mixture. Toss to combine.
Serve warm.

title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Carrots
ingredientLines: ½ pound carrots, peeled and sliced into matchsticks (julienne cut)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Prepare the Brussels sprouts by removing the outer leaves if dry or discolored, trimming the stems off, and cutting each sprout in half lengthwise.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the oil, maple syrup, mustard, thyme, salt, and black pepper.
Add the Brussels sprouts and carrots. Toss to combine.
Transfer the Brussels sprouts and carrots to a baking sheet and spread into a single layer.
Roast in the oven for 15 minutes, then remove from the oven and toss the Brussels sprouts and carrots on the baking sheet.
Spread the Brussels sprouts and carrots back into a single layer, then continue cooking in the oven until fork-tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: This recipe will work with a variety of vegetables, such as cauliflower, onions, asparagus, eggplant, mushrooms, or peppers. Cook time may need adjusting, up or down, based on the vegetable you are using.

title: Roasted Eggplant Spread
ingredientLines: 1 medium eggplant, peeled and cut into 1- to 2-inch chunks (about 12 ounces or 4 cups)
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a medium mixing bowl, toss together the eggplant, onion, oil, salt, and black pepper.
Transfer the mixture to a baking sheet and spread into a single layer.
Roast in preheated oven until caramelized and tender, about 25-30 minutes.
Remove from oven and set aside to cool slightly, about 10 minutes.
Transfer the roasted vegetable mixture to a food processor or high-powered blender and add the tomato paste.
Pulse to chop up and mix in the tomato paste. The spread will remain chunky.
Serve right away.
notes: Try this spread on toasted crusty bread, pita chips, crackers, or sandwiches.
This spread may be stored in the refrigerator for up to 7 days.

title: Roasted Fresh Tomato Soup
ingredientLines: 3 pounds ripe tomatoes (about 12-20 tomatoes, depending on variety)
1 medium onion, cut into large chunks (about 2 cups)
½ cup chopped fresh basil (about one 2-ounce container; can substitute 2 tablespoons dried basil)
1-2 teaspoons sugar or honey, to taste
steps: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Remove the cores from the tomatoes. Cut about three-quarters of the tomatoes into wedges. Cut the tomatoes into a dice.
Peel the garlic cloves. Mince 1 clove, leaving the rest whole.
On a baking sheet, toss together the tomato wedges, onion, whole garlic cloves, oil, and salt.
Roast until the tomatoes are soft and spotty-brown, about 30-45 minutes. Set aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, in a medium mixing bowl, stir together the diced tomatoes, minced garlic, and basil. Set aside to marinate for 30 minutes.
Working in batches if needed, transfer the roasted vegetables to a food processor or high-powered blender and blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the pureed mixture to a medium saucepan.
Add the marinated tomatoes and sugar or honey. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve warm.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Roasted Jalapeño Sriracha
ingredientLines: ½ pound (8 ounces) jalapenos, left whole (about 4-6 jalapenos)
½ medium onion, cut into large chunks or thick wedges
1 tablespoon avocado oil or canola oil
4 garlic cloves, peeled and left whole
steps: Preheat oven broiler to high.
Line a baking sheet with a large piece of aluminum foil.
Place the jalapenos and onion on the baking sheet and toss with oil.
Place under the broiler, on the middle rack if your broiler is inside the oven and broil for 5 minutes.
Turn the jalapenos and onion pieces over, then add the garlic cloves to the baking sheet. Continue broiling until the vegetable are spotty-brown and charred in places, about 5 minutes.
Wrap the vegetables tightly with the foil and set aside for 20 minutes.
Open the foil carefully. One at a time, run the jalapenos under cool water while rubbing to remove the skins. Split the jalapenos lengthwise and scrape out the seeds.
Place the jalapenos, onion, garlic, lime juice, water, sugar, and salt in a blender. Blend until smooth, about 2 minutes.
Serve right away or chill before serving. Store in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 7 days.

title: Roasted Kohlrabi, Beets, and Fennel
ingredientLines: 2 kohlrabi bulbs, peel and chopped into ¾- to 1-inch cubes
2 medium beets, peeled and sliced about ½-inch-thick
1 medium fennel bulb, cored and sliced about ½-inch-thick
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley (or ½ teaspoon dried parsley)
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Add the kohlrabi, beets, and fennel to a baking sheet.
Add the oil, salt, and black pepper. Toss to combine.
Roast in the oven until fork-tender, about 25-30 minutes, stirring about halfway through the cooking time.
Remove from oven.
Add the parmesan and parsley. Toss to combine.
Serve warm.
notes: This recipe works well with a variety of root vegetables.

title: Roasted Red Pepper Romesco
ingredientLines: 1 large red bell pepper, stem and seeds removed, quartered
2 tablespoons red wine vinegar or sherry vinegar
2 garlic gloves, peeled and left whole
steps: Move an oven rack to be about 10 inches from the broiler. Preheat the oven broiler to high.

Place the bell pepper and tomatoes on a baking sheet, skin-side-up. Place under the broiler until the skins are blistered and slightly blackened, about 10-15 minutes. Keep a close watch and rotate halfway through for even cooking.
Remove from the oven. Transfer the bell pepper and tomatoes to a heatproof bowl. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and set aside for 10-15 minutes.
Remove the skins from the bell pepper and tomatoes.
Add the bell pepper, tomatoes, oil, almonds, vinegar, parsley, garlic, paprika, salt, black pepper, and cayenne (if using) to a food processor or blender.
Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed.
Serve right away, or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Freeze for up to 3 months.
notes: Serve on top of fish, chicken, or roasted vegetables, or use as a dipping sauce for bread.

title: Roasted Vegetables
ingredientLines: 4 cups (about 1 pound) fresh vegetables, cut into bite-sized pieces (one type or a combination; e.g. green beans, cauliflower, carrots, broccoli, sweet potato, Brussels sprouts, beets, bell peppers)
¼ cup grated or shredded parmesan cheese (optional)
steps: Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Line a baking sheet or casserole dish with parchment paper.
Place the selected vegetables in a large bowl.
Add the oil, garlic, black pepper, and salt. Toss to coat the vegetables.
Spread the vegetables out onto the prepared baking sheet or casserole dish in a single layer.
Bake until fork-tender, about 20-25 minutes, tossing about halfway through cooking for more even browning if desired.
(Optional) Top with the parmesan and parsley, and return to oven to broil until golden-brown, about 3-5 minutes, watching closely so they do not burn.
Serve warm.
notes: Actual cooking time may be shorter or longer, depending on the vegetables selected.
Roasted vegetables will keep in the refrigerator for 5-7 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months.
Feel free to change up the seasonings to suit your flavor preferences.
Substitute 1 teaspoon garlic powder for the fresh garlic if desired.

title: Rosemary Chicken Salad Sandwiches
ingredientLines: 1½ cups chopped or shredded cooked chicken breast
¼ cup nonfat plain Greek yogurt
steps: Combine all ingredients, except the bread, in a large mixing bowl. Stir well.
Spread ½ of the mixture (about 1 cup) over one bread slice, top with second bread slice to form a sandwich.
Cut sandwiches in half and serve.
notes: Instead of whole grain bread, try with a pita, wrap, or on a bed of mixed greens.
A great way to use leftover chicken or substitute leftover turkey if desired.
credit: Adapted from MyRecipes

title: Rosemary Tuna Salad Sandwiches
steps: In a small bowl, combine the tuna, almonds, yogurt, mayonnaise, rosemary, onion powder, mustard, and black pepper.
Set the mixture in the refrigerator for 10 minutes to chill and to allow the flavors to blend.
Place down two slices of bread.
Divide the tuna mixture, spinach, tomato, and onion over the two bread slices.
Top with the remaining bread slices to make two sandwiches.
Cut the sandwiches diagonally in half and serve.
credit: Adapted from www.myrecipes.com | Submitted by Dana Herring MS, RDN

title: Sautéed Swiss Chard
ingredientLines: 1 bunch chard, stems chopped and leaves torn into 2- to 3-inch pieces
2 garlic scapes, finely chopped (or 1 clove minced garlic)
steps: Heat a large sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chard stems, scallions, and garlic scapes. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the stems are tender, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the chard leaves and water. Cover the pan with a lid and cook for 3 minutes.
Remove the lid. Add the salt, black pepper, and nutmeg. Continue cooking uncovered for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and drizzle with balsamic vinegar. Serve warm.

title: Savory Avocado Toast
steps: Toast the slice of bread to your desired level of doneness.
Cut the egg and avocado into slices.
Layer the toast with the following ingredients, in this order: egg, avocado, and salsa.
Serve immediately.
notes: Try other toast topping combinations to change it up. Here are some ideas to get you started: 2 tablespoons nut butter (e.g. peanut, almond) + ½ small banana, sliced + ½ tablespoon honey or 2 tablespoons lowfat cottage cheese + 1 tablespoon fresh fruit or fruit preserves

title: Sheet Pan Chicken and Vegetables
ingredientLines: 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and diced into ½-inch pieces
¼ teaspoon ground black pepper, divided
8 ounces (½ pound) boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-size chunks or strips
3-4 cups of fresh vegetables cut into bite-size pieces (red bell pepper, zucchini, yellow squash, onion, broccoli or cauliflower)
½ teaspoon garlic powder (or 1 clove garlic minced)
steps: Pre-heat the oven to 400°F.
Prepare a baking sheet with parchment paper or coat with nonstick cooking spray.
In a medium bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon olive oil and half of the salt and pepper.
Spread on prepared baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes.
Using the same bowl, add the chicken and fresh vegetables. Coat with 1 tablespoon oil and the remaining salt and pepper, lemon juice and zest, Italian seasoning, and garlic powder. Toss to coat.
Once the sweet potatoes have cooked for 10 minutes, add the chicken and vegetables to the pan with the potatoes. Toss and spread evenly.
Bake for 20 more minutes, tossing halfway through, until the chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender.
Sprinkle with parmesan. Serve warm.
notes: Try using pork or tofu for the chicken if desired.
Substitute onion powder for the garlic powder if desired.

title: Sheet Pan Sausage and Veggie Bake
servingSize: 1 sausage link and ½ of vegetables
ingredientLines: 1 bag (16 ounces) frozen bell pepper and onion mix, or 3-4 cups sliced or diced fresh vegetables
2 links (~3 ounces each) pre-cooked chicken sausage, sliced
1 bag (10 ounces) frozen diced butternut squash, or ~2 cups fresh diced butternut squash or sweet potato
steps: Pre-heat the oven to 425°F.
Prepare a baking sheet with parchment paper or coat with nonstick cooking spray.
Spread the bell peppers and onions, or fresh vegetables, in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Add the slices of chicken sausage over the vegetables.
Add the diced butternut squash or sweet potato over the chicken sausage and vegetables.
Coat vegetables and chicken with nonstick cooking spray.
Sprinkle the pepper, garlic powder and Italian seasoning over top.
Bake until the vegetables are cooked through and slightly crisped along the edges, about 35 minutes. Serve warm.
notes: Change the flavor of this dish by swapping out a different salt-free seasoning and chicken sausage. Consider par- ing Cajun seasoning with andouille chicken sausage or taco seasoning with jalapeno chicken sausage.
Sodium content of sausage will vary so choose lower sodium options whenever possible.
You can use frozen vegetables, fresh vegetables, or a combination of both for this recipe.

title: Sheet Pan Tilapia and Vegetable Medley
servingSize: 1 tilapia filet, 1 potato, and ¾ cup of the vegetables
ingredientLines: 2 medium Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into wedges
1 cup sugar snap peas, cut in half
steps: Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil. Spray the foil with cooking spray.
In a large bowl, add the potatoes, Brussels sprouts, radishes, sugar snap peas, carrot, oil, garlic powder, and black pepper. Toss to combine.
Transfer the vegetable mixture to the prepared baking sheet in a single layer
Bake until the potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes.
Remove the baking sheet from the oven, then preheat the broiler.
Push the vegetables to one side of the baking sheet, then add the tilapia to the other side.
Sprinkle the fish with the tarragon and salt, then dot with the softened butter.
Broil 4-5 inches from the heat until the fish flakes easily with a fork or until a thermometer placed in center of the thickest part reads 145°F, about 5 minutes.
Serve warm, with lemon wedges if desired.
credit: Adapted from www.tasteofhome.com | Submitted by Jessica Long, MS, RDN, CD

title: Shrimp and Broccoli Pasta
ingredientLines: 10 ounces uncooked whole-wheat short pasta (e.g. rotini, penne, macaroni elbows)
1 pound (16 ounces) shrimp, deveined and peeled, thawed if frozen
steps: Cook pasta according to directions on box. Do not add salt to the water. Before draining, remove 1 cup of the pasta cooking water and set aside.
While the pasta is cooking, heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil, garlic, and pepper and sauté until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add frozen broccoli and lemon juice, cover with a lid and cook for 2-3 minutes or until broccoli is thawed.
Add the shrimp. Cook, stirring often, until the shrimp is cooked and broccoli is heated through, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the cooked pasta, along with the reserved pasta water.
Stir in shredded Parmesan cheese and red pepper flakes.
Serve warm.
notes: Store leftovers in refrigerator up to 4 days. Leftovers can be reheated in the microwave or served cold.
Another protein can be substituted for the shrimp if desired (e.g. cooked leftover chicken, chicken sausage, white beans, or chickpeas).

title: Silken Chocolate Mousse
ingredientLines: 1 (16-ounce) block tofu, excess liquid drained and discarded
¾ cup semi-sweet mini chocolate chips (about 6 ounces)
steps: Place the tofu in a blender or food processor. Blend until smooth and creamy. Set aside.
In a microwave-safe glass bowl, add the chocolate chips, water, and cocoa powder.

Microwave for 30 seconds at a time, stirring in between each, until the chocolate is just finished melting, about 1½-2 minutes total. Stirring in between cooking bursts is important to keep the chocolate from burning.
Add the melted chocolate mixture to the tofu in the blender, along with the powdered sugar, vanilla, and cinnamon. Blend until smooth and small air bubbles form, about 1-2 minutes.
Divide the mixture between eight serving cups and chill until the mousse firms up, about 1 hour in the refrigerator (or 20 minutes in the freezer).
Top with raspberries if desired. Serve cold.
notes: Tofu is a plant-based protein that takes on the flavor of whatever you pair it with– in this case, chocolate!
If you don’t have mini chocolate chips, you can use regular chocolate chips. They may just take longer to melt.
To save time, consider serving this dish warm as a pudding.

title: Simple Pumpkin Pudding
ingredientLines: ½ cup 100% pure pumpkin puree (canned or cooked from fresh)
steps: Add the milk, pumpkin, sugar, cornstarch, pumpkin pie spice to a medium saucepan. Whisk to combine.
Place the pan over medium heat.
Cook, whisking often, until the mixture thickens, about 7-10 minutes.
Once thickened, remove from the heat and let sit to cool for 3-5 minutes.
Divide the pudding into four serving bowls.
Serve warm, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: This pudding will keep in the refrigerator for 3 days.
Substitute your favorite non-dairy milk if desired. If the milk is sweetened, reduce the sugar in the recipe to 2 tablespoons.
If you don’t have pumpkin pie spice, you can use the same amount of ground cinnamon.

title: Simple Skillet Fish with French Dressing
ingredientLines: 2 (4- to 6-ounce) white fish fillets (e.g. flounder, cod, tilapia)
steps: Pat both sides of the fish dry with a paper towel.
Sprinkle fish with pepper and seasoning blend.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil, and heat until shimmering.
Place fish in skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Once you see the edges touching the pan turn white and start to lift from the pan, flip the fish and cook an additional 2-3 minutes or until fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Remove from heat and drizzle with French dressing.
Serve warm.
notes: If using frozen fish, thaw in the refrigerator before cooking.
credit: Submitted by Andrea Goergen, MHS, RDN, LDN

title: Simple Tomato Marinara Sauce
ingredientLines: 1 teaspoon garlic powder (or 6-8 garlic cloves, minced)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh basil (can substitute the same amount of basil paste or 1 teaspoon dried basil)
¼-½ teaspoon ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Add the oil, onion powder, garlic powder, and oregano to a medium saucepan or a sauté pan.
Set the pan over medium heat, heating until fragrant, about 2-5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, basil, vinegar, sugar, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook, stirring often, until the flavors have blended, about 5-10 minutes.
Serve warm as desired, such as over your choice of pasta or as a dipping sauce.
notes: Consider adding any leftover veggies you have to this sauce. Simply mince or puree them prior to adding to the sauce.
Try making tomato soup out of this sauce by adding 1 cup of unsalted chicken broth or milk.

title: Skillet Shepherd’s Pie
ingredientLines: ½ pound yellow or red potatoes (about 2 medium potatoes or 4 small potatoes), cut into 1- to 2-inch chunks
¼-½ teaspoon ground black pepper, to taste
¼-⅓ cup lowfat (1%) milk, based on desired consistency
½ cup diced onion (about ½ medium onion)
½ pound (8 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher)
⅔ cup (6 ounces) reduced-sodium beef broth
steps: Add the potatoes and 1 teaspoon of the salt to a medium saucepan. Add enough water to cover the potatoes. Bring to a boil, then cook until tender, about 15 minutes.

Drain the water, returning the potatoes to the pot. Add the remaining ¼ teaspoon of salt, black pepper, and ¼ cup of the milk. Mash with a potato masher, adding more milk as needed to adjust the consistency. Set aside.
Heat a broiler-safe medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, then add the frozen vegetables and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add the ground turkey and cook until no longer pink, about 5-7 minutes, breaking it into crumbles as it cooks.
Add the flour, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, and thyme. Stir to combine and cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the broth and stir to combine. Cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the mashed potatoes on the top and spread to cover.
Broil on high until golden-brown, about 4-5 minutes, then serve warm.
credit: Adapted from Cullyskitchen.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Slow Cooker Chicken Fajitas
servingSize: ½ cup of the chicken mixture and 1 tortilla
ingredientLines: 1 (16-ounce) can low-sodium diced tomatoes with green chili peppers
1 packet low-sodium or no-salt-added taco seasoning
1 (16-ounce) can black beans, low sodium, drained and rinsed
1 (14– to 16-ounce) bag frozen bell peppers and onion mix
Optional toppings: Shredded cheese, plain Greek yogurt or light sour cream, guacamole
steps: Add the diced tomato and green chili peppers to a slow cooker.
Place the chicken breasts on top of the vegetable mixture.
Sprinkle everything in the slow cooker with the taco seasoning.
Cover the slow cooker with a lid.
Cook on low for 4-6 hours or until chicken breasts are fully cooked, adding the beans and frozen vegetables during the last 60 minutes of the total cooking time.
Shred the chicken using two forks.
Stir the shredded chicken back into the slow cooker.
Spoon about ½ cup of the shredded chicken mixture onto each tortilla.
Serve, garnished with toppings as desired.
notes: Try this on top of a salad or on top of rice for a more complete meal.
Instead of using frozen vegetables, try using fresh shredded cabbage to make cabbage chicken tacos.
credit: Submitted by Jessica Kovarik MS, RD, CSSD, Roseburg VAHCS

title: Slow Cooker Moroccan Chickpea-Lentil Stew
ingredientLines: 1 (15-ounce) can garbanzo beans (chickpeas), drained and rinsed
1 medium butternut squash, peeled and cubed (about 2½ cups, or one 15-ounce package)
½ cup red lentils, picked through and rinsed
steps: Add the broth, garbanzo beans, tomato sauce, butternut squash, bell pepper, onion, and lentils to the pot of a slow cooker.
Add the ginger, garlic, turmeric, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, black pepper, and salt.
Stir all the ingredients together to combine.
Cover the slow cooker with the lid and set to cook on low for 6-8 hours or high for 3-4 hours.
Serve warm.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Slow Cooker Mulled Cider
ingredientLines: 4 cups (32 ounces) apple cider or apple juice
½ cup fresh or frozen cranberries
steps: Add the apple cider or juice, cranberries cinnamon sticks, and star anise to the pot of a slow cooker.
Cook on low for 3 hours.
Add the orange slices.
Switch the slow cooker to the keep warm setting.
Serve warm, straining off the solids before serving if desired.
notes: Feel free to add or substitute other warm spices, such as sliced fresh ginger or whole cloves.
This cider could also be served chilled, if desired.
Store this cider in the refrigerator for up to 7 days.

If you don’t have whole spices, substitute 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon for the cinnamon sticks. Substitute 1 teaspoon ground star anise or ½ teaspoon Chinese five spice for the whole star anise. For best results, use a spice sachet or strain the cider through cheesecloth before serving.

title: Slow Cooker-Poached Eggs and Salmon
servingSize: 1 salmon fillet with an egg and half the spinach
ingredientLines: 4 cups fresh spinach (about 4 ounces, or 1 cup frozen spinach)
2 pinches (about ⅛ teaspoon) ground black pepper, divided
steps: Fill a medium saucepan about halfway full with water and bring to a boil.
Meanwhile, coat the inside of two oven-safe ramekins or other small dishes with nonstick cooking spray. Crack an egg into each dish and top each with 1 tablespoon of the chives.
Set the egg dishes in the bottom of a slow cooker, then add the salmon fillets on either side.
Pour the boiling water into the slow cooker until it comes about halfway up the sides of the egg dishes – be careful not to get any water in the egg cups.
Cover the slow cooker with the lid and cook on high for 1 hour. Check for doneness and, if needed, cook for an additional 10-15 minutes.
Use oven mitts to carefully remove the egg dishes. Then lift the salmon out with a slotted spatula or spoon. Set aside.
Add the spinach to the slow cooker and stir into the water until wilted, about 3-4 minutes. Drain or lift out of the slow cooker with tongs and divide between two plates.
Add ½ tablespoon of the melted butter to each portion of spinach. Toss to combine. Top each portion with one of the salmon fillets.
Use a butter knife to loosen the eggs from the dishes and place each on top of the salmon.
Sprinkle each plate with 1 teaspoon of the lemon juice, 1 pinch of the salt, and 1 pinch of the black pepper. Serve warm.
notes: The salmon is done when it reaches an internal temperature of 145°F or flakes easily with a fork. The eggs are done when the whites and yolk do not jiggle when the dishes are shaken.
For best results, serve right away. If needed, this recipe will keep in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. To reheat, cook in the microwave at 50% power until warm, about 1½-3 minutes.

title: Slow-Cooker Roasted Chicken
servingSize: 4 ounces chicken meat (without skin and bones)
ingredientLines: 1 (5-pound) whole chicken, insides removed and skin pat dry with paper towels
steps: In a small bowl, mix together the seasoning blend, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper
Rub the seasoning mixture over the entire chicken (including the inside).
Place 4 loosely crumpled up balls of foil in the bottom of the crock of a slow cooker. This will act as a stand to prevent the chicken from overcooking or drying out.
Place the chicken on top of the balls of foil, without pressing the chicken down on the foil.
Cover the slow cooker tightly with the lid and cook on High for 4-5 hours or Low for 6-8 hours.
Carve the chicken and serve warm.
notes: If you use a seasoning blend that contains salt, skip adding the salt in step 1.
If the lid of your slow cooker does not close tightly, place a sheet of foil over the mouth of the slow cooker, then place the lid on top of that.

Instead of the balls of foil, you can use large (2-inch) chunks of root vegetables (e.g. potatoes, carrots, onions, turnips) for your chicken stand or if your crock-pot comes with a wire rack you could use that as well.
credit: Adapted from FamilyFreshMeals.com | Submitted by Dana Herring MS, RDN

title: Slow Cooker Stuffed Peppers
servingSize: 1 bell pepper with ⅙th of the filling
ingredientLines: 1 (14-ounce) can black beans, drained and rinsed
1½ cups red enchilada sauce or low-sodium salsa
1½ cups shredded reduced-fat Mexican cheese blend, divided
steps: Pour the water into the bottom of a slow cooker.
Cut the tops off the bell peppers and scrape out the ribs and seeds. Discard the tops, ribs, and seeds.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, quinoa, beans, enchilada sauce or salsa, cumin, chili powder, onion powder, garlic powder, and 1 cup of the cheese.
Fill each bell pepper with the ground beef mixture.
Place the stuffed bell peppers upright in the slow cooker so their bottoms are sitting in the water.
Cover the slow cooker with the lid. Cook on Low for 6 hours or on High for 3 hours.
Remove the lid, sprinkle the remaining ½ cup cheese over the tops of the peppers.
Cover the slow cooker again with the lid and let sit for a few minutes to melt the cheese.
Serve warm.
notes: To make this a vegetarian meal, substitute 1 can of refried beans for the lean ground beef.
credit: Adapted from www.pinchofyum.com | Submitted by Jessica Long, MS, RDN, CD

title: Smokey Ham and Bean Soup
ingredientLines: ¼-1 teaspoon smoked paprika or liquid smoke, to taste
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added great northern beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat a large saucepan or pot over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, celery, and carrots. Cook, stirring often, until softened, about 7-10 minutes.
Add the garlic, smoked paprika or liquid smoke, and red pepper flakes. Cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the tomatoes with their juice and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes.
Add the broth, beans, and ham.
Bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook until warmed through, about 7-10 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: For a creamier texture, mash ¼-½ cup of the beans before adding them to the soup.
If desired, you can substitute chili powder or cumin for the smoked paprika or liquid smoke.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Soothing Spice-Infused Golden Milk
ingredientLines: 2 teaspoons sugar-based sweetener (e.g. sugar, honey, maple syrup)
steps: In a microwave-safe mug or a small saucepan, add the milk, cinnamon, ginger, turmeric, and sweetener. Stir to combine.

Microwave in the mug on high power (default setting) or simmer in the saucepan on the stovetop over medium heat until warmed and the flavors have infused, about 2-3 minutes in the microwave or 7-10 minutes on the stovetop.
Serve warm, or chill in the refrigerator and serve cold.
notes: Another milk or plant-based milk alternative (e.g. almond milk, soy milk, coconut milk) can be used, if desired. If you need extra calories, use reduced fat (2%) or whole cow’s milk or a higher-fat milk alternative (e.g. full-fat coconut milk).
This drink will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Consider making a bigger batch to enjoy throughout the week. To reheat, simply microwave for 1-2 minutes.

title: Southwest Chicken Soup
ingredientLines: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cubed
1 (15.5-ounce) can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat a large stockpot over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken. Cook, turning occasionally, until lightly browned and about halfway cooked.
Once the chicken is about halfway cooked, add the onion, bell pepper, green beans, and garlic.
Cook until the chicken is fully cooked and the vegetables begin to soften.
Stir in the broth, beans, corn, diced tomatoes and their juice, chili powder, cumin, black pepper, cayenne pepper, oregano, and basil.
Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to a simmer and add the spinach.
Stir in the spinach.
Continue to cook until the spinach has thawed and the flavors have blended.
Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.
Serve warm.
notes: Garnish with cheese, avocado, and plain Greek yogurt or light sour cream as desired.
To adjust the spiciness, use more or less of the cayenne pepper as desired.
credit: Adapted from eatingwell.com | Submitted by Neal Kurmas MS, RD, LD, CDE
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Spaghetti Squash with Turkey Ragu
servingSize: 1 cup squash with ¾ cup sauce
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher)
6 tablespoons grated or shredded parmesan cheese, divided (optional)
steps: Wash the spaghetti squash and prick multiple times with a paring knife. Microwave on high power for 2-3 minutes.
Place the squash on a large cutting board and slice the squash in half crosswise. Scoop out and discard the seeds.

Place one squash half, cut side down, on a microwave-safe dish. Microwave until easily pierced and the spaghetti strands peel away, about 6-8 minutes. Repeat with the second squash half. Cool each squash half about 5 minutes.
Use a fork to scrape out the strands. Place the squash in a strainer for about 5 minutes to let any excess water drain.
While the squash cooks, heat large sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, for 4-5 minutes.
Add the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the ground turkey. Cook, breaking up any large pieces, until no longer pink, about 6-8 minutes.
Stir in the pasta sauce and heat until warmed through, then add to the squash and garnish with parmesan cheese.

title: Spice-Crusted Chicken with Fruit Salsa
servingSize: 4 ounces chicken with ½ cup fruit salsa
ingredientLines: 1½ pounds (24 ounces) boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 6 breasts, 4 ounces each)
3 cups fruit salsa, divided (store-bought or homemade)
steps: Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Do not add any oil or cooking spray.
Add the coriander, cumin, and black pepper. Toast the spices, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30-45 seconds.
Transfer the toasted spices to a plate or shallow dish such as a pie plate. Stir in the salt and set aside.
Pat the chicken breasts dry with paper towels.
Place the now-empty skillet over medium-high heat.

Working with one chicken breast at a time, set the chicken breasts in the spice mixture on one side and then flip to the other side, until both sides of each chicken breast are coated with the spice mixture.
Add the oil to the hot pan and heat until shimmering.
Place the chicken breasts in the pan and cook until the internal temperature reaches 165°F, about 4-5 minutes per side.
Top each chicken breast with ½ cup of the salsa.
Serve warm.

title: Spiced Mango-Raisin Chutney
ingredientLines: ½ cup minced onion (about ½ medium onion)
3 ripe mangos, peeled, pitted, and cut into cubes about ½-inch in size (about 3 cups)
steps: Combine 2 tablespoons of the water with the onion and salt in a large saucepan.
Set over medium heat, cover the pan with a lid, and cook until the onion is softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the ginger, dry mustard, cinnamon, black pepper, garlic powder, cayenne, and cloves. Stir to combine and cook uncovered until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the mangos, raisins, sugar, lime juice, and the remaining 1 cup water. Stir to combine.
Increase the heat to high, and bring to simmer, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.

Cook until the mango has softened and almost all of the liquid has evaporated, about 25-30 minutes. For a saucier consistency, mash up some of the cooked mango pieces with a potato masher or a rubber spatula.
Serve warm, or chill before serving. Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 1 month, or frozen for up to 6 months.
notes: Try serving this over a cooked protein (e.g. tofu, chicken, pork, seafood), whole-grain toast, or brown rice.

title: Spicy Chicken Creole
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into thin strips
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) chopped fresh basil, divided
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) chopped fresh parsley, divided
steps: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken and cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring often.
Reduce the heat to medium.
Add the bell pepper, celery, and onion. Cook until softened, stirring often, about 4-6 minutes.
Add the chili powder, allspice, garlic powder, and red pepper flakes. Cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes with their juice, tomato paste, brown sugar, and vinegar.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to maintain a simmer.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook for 10-15 minutes.
Serve warm, topping each portion with 1 tablespoon of the basil and 1 tablespoon of the parsley.

title: Spinach and Red Pepper Frittata
ingredientLines: ½ red bell pepper, diced small
½ small yellow onion, diced small
½ cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Heat a large, oven-safe frying pan (e.g. cast-iron) over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the bell pepper and onion. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 4-5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach. Remove the pan from the heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, skim milk, and Italian seasoning.
Add the egg mixture to the pan with the vegetables.
Bake in the oven until golden brown and fully cooked, about 20-25 minutes.
Sprinkle the cheese on top and let sit until melted.
Serve warm.
notes: If you don’t have frozen spinach on hand, use 16 ounces fresh spinach, roughly chopped. Cook until wilted before removing the pan from the heat.
credit: Submitted by Katie Kirzoncic RD, LDN, Lebanon VAMC

title: Spinach Artichoke Dip
ingredientLines: ¾ cup plain reduced-fat or nonfat Greek yogurt
1 (14-ounce) can or jar artichoke hearts, drained and chopped, removing any hard pieces
1 (10-ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed to drain excess liquid
1/4 cup shredded or grated parmesan cheese
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
In a large bowl, stir together the cream cheese, yogurt, garlic, salt, pepper, pepper flakes (if using), and onion powder until combined.
Add the artichoke hearts, spinach, ½ cup mozzarella, and green chilies. Stir well.
Transfer the mixture to a 1½- to 2-quart baking dish.
Sprinkle the mixture with the parmesan and the remaining ½ cup mozzarella.
Bake until hot and bubbly, about 25 minutes.
Serve with whole-grain chips, whole-wheat crackers, crusty bread, or firm vegetables such as carrots or celery.
notes: Can also be used as a topping for pizza or on a sandwich.
This recipe is best when freshly prepared, but can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 5 days and reheated for serving again
credit: Adapted from House of Nash Eats Blog| Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Spinach-Mozzarella Egg Bake
ingredientLines: ½ medium onion, chopped (about ½ cup)
5 ounces spinach, roughly chopped (about 5 cups fresh or 1¼ cups frozen)
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Spray a 13x9-inch baking dish with nonstick spray. Set aside.
Heat a nonstick skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.

Spray the pan with nonstick spray, then add the onion, tomato, and spinach. Cook, stirring often, just until the spinach is wilted (or thawed if frozen), about 2-5 minutes. Remove the pan from the heat and set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, gently whisk together the eggs, milk, and Italian seasoning.
Add the cooked vegetable mixture, beans, and cheese to the egg mixture. Stir to combine.
Pour the egg mixture into the prepared baking dish, spreading it evenly over the bottom of the dish.
Place in the oven and bake until the mixture is completely set and just starting to brown, about 25-35 minutes.
Let cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then cut and serve warm.
notes: Change out the vegetables, cheese, or seasoning for different flavor combinations if desired.
Store any leftovers in the refrigerator for up to 4 days, reheating each portion in the microwave.

title: Steamed Vegetables with Tahini Sauce
ingredientLines: 4 cups fresh or frozen vegetables, trimmed and cut into ½- to 1-inch pieces (one type or a combination; e.g. bell peppers, broccoli, carrots, mushrooms, green beans, cauliflower, zucchini)
2 tablespoons tahini (sesame seed paste; can substitute creamy peanut butter)
1 tablespoon warm or room-temperature water, plus more to adjust consistency
steps: Place a steamer basket inside a large saucepan or stockpot and add just enough water fill the area under the steamer.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-high to maintain a rapid simmer.

Add the selected vegetables to the steamer basket, cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid, and cook until the vegetables are fork-tender. This will take about 5-15 minutes, depending on which type(s) of vegetable is being steamed.

While the vegetables are cooking, add the tahini and water to a large mixing bowl. Whisk together until smooth, then whisk in the lemon juice, garlic, and salt. If a thinner consistency is desired, whisk in additional water.
Remove the vegetables from the steamer basket and add to the bowl with the tahini mixture.
Serve warm, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: To cut down on the raw garlic flavor, let the garlic sit in the bowl with the lemon juice while you cut up the vegetables.
The vegetables can be stored in the refrigerator for 5-7 days. They can be served cold or reheated in the microwave before serving.

title: Stir-Fried Eggplant
ingredientLines: 1 medium eggplant, cut into bite-sized cubes (about 3 cups)
2 teaspoons grated fresh ginger (or ½ teaspoon ground dried ginger)
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, sugar, ginger, and garlic to make a sauce. Set aside.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the eggplant and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes.
Add the sauce. Continue to cook, stirring often, until the eggplant is tender and glazed with the sauce, about 3-5 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: Add a protein, such as cooked chicken, fish, or tofu and/or serve over cooked brown rice, if desired.

title: Stove-to-Oven Vegetable Frittata
ingredientLines: 2 cups frozen shredded hash brown potatoes
½ cup shredded cheese (e.g. cheddar, mozzarella, Mexican blend)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Spray the inside of a medium to large oven-safe skillet (e.g. cast-iron, stainless steel) with nonstick cooking spray, then place on the stovetop over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the bell pepper, onion, and salt. Cook until softened and lightly browned, about 6-8 minutes, stirring often.
Add the spinach and cook until thawed, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the potatoes. Stir to combine, then remove the pan from the heat and set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, and black pepper.
Add the egg mixture to the pan with the vegetables, then sprinkle the cheese over the top.
Bake until fully set and golden-brown, about 25-35 minutes.
Let cool for 5-10 minutes, then cut into four wedges and serve warm.
notes: If you don’t have an oven-safe skillet, assemble the ingredients in step 8 in a greased 8x8-inch baking dish.

title: Stovetop Chicken Divan
ingredientLines: 8 ounces whole-wheat egg noodles, uncooked (about 5 cups)
1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into ¾-inch pieces
1½ cups shredded reduced-fat Colby-jack or cheddar cheese
steps: Add the noodles and broth to a large nonstick skillet.
Add the chicken and then the broccoli.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the milk, mayonnaise, flour, dry mustard, garlic powder, onion powder, celery seed, thyme, and black pepper.
Add the milk mixture to the skillet.
Set the skillet over medium heat and bring to a simmer.
Cover the skillet with a lid. Cook, stirring every 4-5 minutes, until the noodles and broccoli are tender and the chicken is fully cooked, about 10-12 minutes.
Sprinkle with the cheese and let sit until melted.
Serve warm.
notes: Feel free to substitute your favorite meat for the chicken.
Try substituting another frozen non-starchy vegetable (e.g. carrots, cauliflower, green beans) for the broccoli.
credit: Adapted from www.eatingwell.com | Submitted by Jessica Long MS, RDN, CD

title: Stovetop Peach Blueberry Crisp
ingredientLines: 3 peaches, diced (can substitute another fruit, such as apples or plums)
2 tablespoons maple syrup or honey, divided
¼ teaspoon plus a pinch cinnamon, divided
1 tablespoon canola oil or avocado oil, divided
steps: In a bowl, mix together the peaches, blueberries, lemon juice, cornstarch, 1 tablespoon of the maple syrup or honey, and 1/4 teaspoon of the cinnamon. Set aside.
In a separate bowl, mix together the rolled oats, sliced almonds, 1 tablespoon of the maple syrup or honey, the vanilla extract, a pinch of the cinnamon, and the salt.
Heat a skillet over medium heat. Add ½ tablespoon of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the oat mixture and reduce the heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, until golden brown and toasted, about 4-6 minutes. Transfer mixture to a plate and set aside.
Add ½ tablespoon of the oil to the now-empty skillet and increase the heat to medium.
Add the fruit mixture. Cover the skillet with a lid and cook until the peaches are softened, about 8-10 minutes, removing the lid to stir occasionally.
Remove the lid and cook until the mixture has thickened, about 3-5 more minutes, stirring occasionally.
Top the fruit mixture with the oat mixture and serve warm.
credit: Submitted by Audrey Ferguson RDN

title: Strawberries with Walnut Crumble
steps: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the walnuts and cook, stirring or shaking often, until fragrant and toasted, about 2-3 minutes. Remove the walnuts from the pan and set aside.
Place the pan back over medium-high heat. Add the sugar, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Cook, stirring constantly, until the sugar melts and the mixture begins to bubble, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the strawberries and stir until the mixture is juicy and heated through, about 1-2 minutes. Remove from the heat and set aside.
In a small mixing bowl, stir together the oats, brown sugar, flour, and cinnamon.
Add the oat mixture to the berry mixture, and stir gently until partially combined. Let sit until the flour soaks up the liquid from the strawberries, about 1-2 minutes.
Divide the strawberry mixture into four serving bowls and top each with 1 tablespoon of the walnuts. Serve warm.
notes: Substitute other fresh berries (e.g. blueberries, raspberries, blackberries) if desired.

title: Strawberry-Balsamic Vinaigrette
ingredientLines: ⅔ cup sliced fresh or frozen strawberries, thawed if frozen
½ medium shallot, chopped (about ¼ cup)
2 teaspoons fresh thyme leaves (or ½ teaspoon dried thyme)
steps: Add the strawberries, vinegar, shallot, thyme, mustard, black pepper, and salt to a blender or food processor.
Pulse or blend on low until broken down and starting to become smooth, about 1-2 minutes.
With the blender or food processor running on low speed, slowly drizzle the oil in a steady stream through the opening in the blender or food processor lid. This should take about 1-2 minutes.
Continue blending until completely smooth and creamy.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: This vinaigrette will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days.
If you don’t have fresh or frozen strawberries, you can substitute 2-4 tablespoons strawberry jam or preserves, to taste.
categories: Dressings, Sauces, and Seasonings: Salad Dressings

title: Strawberry-Banana Oatmeal Smoothie
ingredientLines: ¼ cup uncooked old fashioned (rolled) oats
2 teaspoons chia seeds or ground flax seed (optional)
¼ cup nonfat Greek yogurt (plain or any flavor)
1 small banana (or ½ large), as ripe as possible
steps: Add the oats and chia seeds or ground flax seed (if using) to the pitcher of a blender.
Blend on high until the texture looks like flour.
Add the milk and use a spoon or rubber spatula to combine it with the oat mixture.
Add the yogurt, strawberries, banana, and vanilla.
Blend until smooth and fully combined, about 2-3 minutes.
Transfer to a pint-size mason jar or other 2-cup storage container with a tightly fitting lid.
Cover and refrigerate overnight (or at least 4 hours) to soften the oats and chia seeds or ground flax seed.
Shake well and divide into two serving glasses.
Serve cold.
notes: To change the flavor, substitute ¼ cup orange or other fruit juice for up to ¼ cup of the milk.
Substitute frozen berries if fresh berries are unavailable.
This smoothie will keep in the refrigerator for 2-3 days.
Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk if desired.

title: Strawberry-Basil Salsa
steps: In a large bowl, combine the strawberries, apples, and pineapple.
Add the lime juice, basil, salt (if using), and black pepper (if using).
Toss to combine.
Serve immediately, or chill until ready to use.
notes: Serve with tortilla chips (homemade or store-bought) or as a topping for grilled fish or chicken.
To add a little heat, stir in half of a seeded and minced jalapeño or serrano pepper.
Substitute your favorite fruit combinations as desired.

title: Stuffed Bell Peppers
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher)
1 (10-ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed to remove moisture
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Cut the bell peppers in half lengthwise, slicing from the stem to the bottom, leaving the stems intact.
Remove and discard the white ribs and seeds near the stem and along the length of the inside of the bell peppers.
Place the prepared bell peppers in an 9x13-inch baking dish. Drizzle the peppers with ½ tablespoon of oil and rub all over to coat the peppers with oil.
Place in the oven and cook for 10 minutes.
While the peppers are cooking, heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the remaining ½ tablespoon of oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the turkey, onion, garlic, black pepper, chili powder, and cumin. Cook until the turkey is no longer pink, about 6-8 minutes, breaking it up into crumbles as it cooks.
Stir in the spinach, salsa, and corn. Remove pan from heat.
Spoon the turkey mixture into the bell pepper halves. Cover the baking dish with foil and bake until the filling is hot and the peppers are tender, about 15-20 minutes. Serve warm.

title: Stuffing Meatloaf with Cranberry Glaze
ingredientLines: ⅓ cup cranberry sauce (store-bought or homemade)
⅔ cup cubed whole-wheat bread (about 2 bread slices, or ½ cup panko breadcrumbs)
¾ cup finely diced apple (about 1 medium apple)
½ cup finely diced celery (about 2 stalks celery)
½ cup diced onion (about ½ medium onion)
1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.
Whisk together the cranberry sauce, ketchup, and mustard in a small bowl. Set aside.
Add the bread cubes and egg to a medium mixing bowl. Stir to combine and set aside.
Preheat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the butter and oil. Heat until melted and shimmering.
Add the apple, celery, and onion. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the garlic, thyme, sage, salt, and black pepper. Cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat and set aside to cool slightly.
Add the ground turkey and apple-vegetable mixture to the bowl with the bread mixture. Gently knead to combine.
Transfer the turkey mixture to the prepared baking sheet and form into a loaf about 3-4 inches wide and 1½-2 inches tall.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Brush the cranberry mixture over the meatloaf.
Continue baking until cooked through (internal temperature of 165°F), about 15-20 minutes.
Cut into six slices and serve warm.

title: Summer Fruit Salad with Lime Yogurt Sauce
ingredientLines: 1 (6 ounce) container plain nonfat Greek yogurt
steps: Rinse all fruit under cool running water.
Remove stems from strawberries and grapes and cut in half.
Gently toss all fruit into a large bowl, set aside.
In a small bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, honey, lime juice and zest.
Combine yogurt sauce with fruit just before serving.
notes: Substitute any of your favorite seasonal fruits.
Vary the flavor by using flavored yogurt such as vanilla or key lime (omit the honey if using flavored yogurt)
Try different juice and zest (i.e. lemon or orange) instead of lime.
credit: Adapted from Jessica Long, RDN | Submitted by Kristen Adapted from Bertram, RDN Submitted by

title: Summer Vegetable Chowder
ingredientLines: 1 cup fresh or frozen corn kernels
1 medium red bell pepper, diced (about 1 cup)
1 small zucchini, quartered lengthwise and sliced (about 1 cup)
steps: Place a large saucepan or other pot over medium heat.
Add the butter and oil. Heat until melted.
Add the onion and mushrooms. Cook until golden brown, about 7-10 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over onions and mushrooms. Cook and stir until flour mixture is golden brown, about 5-6 minutes.
Whisk in broth until smooth.
Add corn, bell pepper, garlic, black pepper, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in milk and heat through.
Serve warm.
notes: If you can’t find no-added-salt chicken broth, you may use low-sodium broth, but omit salt.
Consider adding cooked chicken breast or turkey sausage to increase the protein.

title: Summer Vegetable Crustless Quiche
ingredientLines: ½ medium onion, diced (about ½ cup)
½ medium zucchini, chopped (about ½ cup)
2 cups chopped or torn leafy greens (e.g. kale, chard, spinach)
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Grease a pie plate or 8x8-inch baking dish with cooking spray. Set aside.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes.
Add the zucchini and continue cooking for 5 minutes.
Add the greens and continue cooking for 5 minutes.
Transfer the vegetables to the prepared pie plate or baking dish.
In a medium bowl, beat the eggs. Add the milk, flour, baking powder, paprika, thyme, salt, and black pepper. Whisk to combine, then gently stir in feta.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables and stir gently.
Bake until the center is set, about 25-30 minutes.
Let cool slightly, then cut into six pieces and serve warm.
notes: Try other vegetables such as peppers, mushrooms, and thinly sliced potatoes. Add a different cheese, if desired.

title: Summer Vegetable Ratatouille
ingredientLines: 1 medium bell pepper, cut into bite-sized pieces (about 1½ cups)
1 medium eggplant, peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces (about 3 cups)
1 medium zucchini, cut into bite-sized pieces (about 2 cups)
1 medium yellow squash, cut into bite-sized pieces (about 2 cups)
1 medium onion, cut into bite-sized pieces (about 1½ cups)
⅛-¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, to taste
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Using a box grater, grate the tomatoes over a medium mixing bowl. Pour off excess juice, as desired. Set aside.
Place the bell pepper, eggplant, zucchini, squash, and onion on a baking sheet. Add 1½ tablespoons of the oil and the salt. Toss to combine, then spread into a single layer.
Roast in the oven until well-browned and fork tender, about 20-25 minutes., tossing halfway through the cooking time.
While the vegetables are roasting, heat a large saucepan or stockpot over medium heat.
Add the remaining ½ tablespoon of oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the grated tomatoes, oregano, black pepper, and crushed red pepper.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a low simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.
Add the roasted vegetables. Continue cooking for 7-10 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the basil.
Serve warm.
notes: Serve over rice, pasta, or crusty bread.
Top with a sprinkle of parmesan or feta, if desired.

title: Sweet-and-Savory Sweet Potato Hummus
ingredientLines: 1 (15-ounce) can garbanzo beans (chickpeas), drained and rinsed
2 tablespoons lemon juice (about ½ medium lemon)
steps: Prick the sweet potato all over with the prongs of a fork, then wrap in a paper towel and microwave on high (default setting) until fork-tender, about 3-4 minutes on each side.

While the sweet potato is cooking, add the beans, olive oil, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, coriander, salt, black pepper, and nutmeg to a food processor. Pulse to combine, then blend until mostly smooth, about 1-2 minutes.
Cut the cooked sweet potato in half lengthwise and let cool slightly, about 2-3 minutes.
Scoop the sweet potato flesh (about ⅔ cup) out of the skin and into the food processor. Discard the skin.
Continue blending until the mixture is very smooth, about 2-3 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving. Store in the refrigerator for 5-7 days.
notes: This dip goes well with whole-grain crackers, pita, or raw vegetables.
For a pop of flavor and texture, try adding pomegranate seeds and/or toasted pepitas (green pumpkin seeds).
Peanut butter can be used in place of the tahini, if desired.

title: Sweet-and-Sour Cabbage
ingredientLines: 4 cups thinly sliced red cabbage, thinly sliced (about ½ medium head of cabbage)
steps: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the butter and oil. Heat until the butter is melted and the oil is shimmering.
Add the cabbage and toss to coat. Cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes.
Add the vinegar, sugar, black pepper and salt. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to maintain a low simmer.
Simmer until the cabbage is wilted and tender, about 25-30 minutes, stirring often.
Serve warm.
notes: Any sweetener can be used as an alternative to brown sugar.

title: Sweet-and-Sour Chicken
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced into 1-inch strips
¼ teaspoon ground dried ginger (or 1 teaspoon fresh grated ginger)
1 tablespoon peanut, canola, or avocado oil
¼ cup white vinegar or rice vinegar
1 (20-ounce) can pineapple chunks, drained with ¼ cup juice reserved and set aside
steps: Sprinkle the chicken with the garlic powder and ginger. Toss to coat.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken to the pan and cook, stirring often, until no longer pink, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the cooked chicken from the pan and cover with foil. Set aside.
Return the pan back to the stovetop and increase the heat to medium-high.
While the pan is heating, add the vinegar, soy sauce, cornstarch, and the reserved ¼ cup of pineapple juice to a small bowl and whisk together with a fork to make a sauce.
Add the pineapple chunks, stir-fry vegetables, water chestnuts, and sauce mixture to the pan.
Cook, stirring often, until warmed through and the sauce is thickened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the chicken back to the pan and toss to coat with the sauce.
Serve warm, on its own or over a cooked grain, if desired.

title: Sweet and Tangy Kale Salad
ingredientLines: 4 cups kale leaves without stems, torn into bite-sized pieces
½ medium apple, chopped (about ½ cup)
¼ cup dried cranberries or dried cherries
¼ cup toasted nuts, chopped (e.g. pecans, walnuts, almonds)
Pinch-¼ teaspoon ground black pepper, to taste
steps: In a medium bowl, whisk together the oil, vinegar, mustard. and honey.
Add the kale and toss to combine, then use clean hands to massage the kale with the dressing for 2-3 minutes.
Add the apple, dried cranberries or cherries, and nuts. Toss to combine.
Add the salt and black pepper. Toss to combine.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: Consider adding 2 tablespoons crumbled feta cheese or blue cheese.
This salad is best when eaten within 2 days.
credit: Adapted from CookieAndKate.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Sweet n’ Sour Pork Roast
ingredientLines: 2 pounds (32 ounces) frozen mixed vegetables, oriental or stir-fry style
1 (8-ounce) package ready microwavable whole-grain rice (e.g. brown rice)
steps: Place the pork loin into the bottom of a slow cooker.
In a mixing bowl, make a glaze by combining the brown sugar, apple juice, vinegar, and soy sauce.
Pour the glaze mixture over the pork loin.
Cover the slow cooker with a lid.
Cook on low for 4-5 hours or until fully cooked, adding the vegetables and rice when there is 30 minutes left in the total cooking time.
Serve warm.
notes: Can’t find a 2-pound pork loin? Substitute with a 2-pound tenderloin or 2 pounds of boneless pork chops.
credit: Inspired by a recipe submitted by Georgia Janssen RDN, Iowa City VAMC

title: Sweet Potato Hash
ingredientLines: Nonstick cooking spray (or use parchment paper)
1 medium sweet potato, peeled and cut into ½-inch cubes (about 4-6 ounces)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Coat a baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray (or line it with parchment paper). Set aside.
In a medium bowl, add the sweet potato cubes, oil, oregano, garlic powder, and salt. Toss to evenly coat.
Transfer the sweet potato cubes to the prepared baking sheet and spread into a single layer. Bake until fork-tender, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over low heat. Add the butter and onion and sauté until tender.
Add the cooked sweet potatoes to the pan with the onion. Continue to cook for 5 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Stir spinach into the potato and onion mixture.
Serve warm.
notes: This recipe is best when eaten right away. Leftovers will soften, though the flavor will still be good.
Leftovers will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days or the freezer for 3 months.
credit: Submitted by Melanya Souza, RD, LD/N

title: Sweet Potato-Pumpkin Seed Casserole
ingredientLines: 3 pounds sweet potatoes (about 6 large sweet potatoes, or 9 medium sweet potatoes), peeled if desired and cut into ½-inch cubes
2 green onions, thinly sliced (about ¼ cup)
steps: Cut three sheets of aluminum foil and loosely crumple each into a large ball. Place the foil balls at the bottom of a large saucepan or stockpot.
Place a steamer basket on top of the foil balls. Fill the pot with water until it reaches just below the steamer basket.
Add the sweet potatoes to the pot, pressing down if needed to fit.
Place the pot over high heat and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to maintain a rapid simmer (steam coming up).
Place the lid on the pot and cook until the sweet potatoes are tender enough to be mashed, about 18-22 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 400°F. Spray a a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray and set aside.
Transfer the sweet potatoes to a large mixing bowl. Gently mash with a potato masher until smooth yet slightly lumpy.
Add the apricots, 3 tablespoons of the orange juice, ½ teaspoon of the orange zest, oil, maple syrup, cinnamon, ginger, allspice, and salt. Stir until combined.
Transfer the sweet potato mixture to the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle the top with the pepitas.
Bake until golden-brown, about 15-20 minutes.
Sprinkle with the green onions, then serve warm.
notes: The sweet potatoes can be cooked in any way, if a steamer basket is not available or convenient. Examples include microwaving, boiling, and baking. Cooking time will vary depending on the method used.

title: Sweet Potato Swirl Pie Bars
ingredientLines: ⅓ cup plus 1 tablespoon brown sugar, divided
2 ounces reduced-fat cream cheese (Neufchatel), softened at room temperature
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.

Pierce the sweet potato with a fork several times, then microwave on high (default setting) for 4 minutes. Flip it over and continue cooking until soft, about 2 minutes. Scoop out the inside and set aside. Discard the skin.
Place the graham crackers in a bag and crush into crumbs with a wooden spoon, rolling pin, or mallet. Transfer the crumbs to a small mixing bowl.
Add the butter and 1 tablespoon of the brown sugar to the graham cracker crumbs. Stir to combine. Press the mixture into a 4x8-inch glass baking dish. Bake for 10 minutes.
In a food processor, add the cooked sweet potato, milk, eggs, pumpkin pie spice, and the remaining ⅓ cup brown sugar. Process until smooth. Pour over the cooked crust.
In a separate small mixing bowl, beat the cream cheese with the powdered sugar. Drop the mixture onto the sweet potato filling, one teaspoon at a time, then swirl gently.
Bake for 40 minutes. Cool completely, then cut and serve.
notes: Crushed ginger cookies can be used in place of the graham crackers (omit the sugar in the crust).
credit: Adapted from Eating Well | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Sweet Vanilla Acorn Squash
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Slice the acorn squash in half lengthwise and scoop out the seeds.
Lay the squash flat-side-down and slice into half-moon shaped pieces, about ½-inch in thickness.
In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil and vanilla extract. Place the sliced squash in the bowl and toss to coat.
Sprinkle the squash with the brown sugar, salt, and black pepper. Toss to combine.
Spread the squash on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Roast until tender, about 30 minutes, flipping the squash pieces over after 15 minutes.
Remove and discard the skin. Serve warm.
notes: Substitute any winter squash for the acorn squash if desired.
credit: Adapted from Dessert for Two | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Taco Seasoning
steps: Mix all the spices together in a small bowl.
Transfer the spice mixture to a small container with a lid for ease of use when adding to recipes.
notes: Use 1½-2 tablespoons of the mixture per 1 pound of ground meat or other protein for tacos.
This recipe is salt-free. When seasoning your dishes, add salt separately, to taste.
Store the spice mixture at room temperature in the sealed container for up to 1 year
This seasoning also goes well in burritos, sprinkled onto kale chips, in a dip, in a soup, or in any dish you want to give a twist of Tex-Mex flavor to.
categories: Dressings, Sauces, and Seasonings: Seasoning Blends

title: Three-Bean Chili
ingredientLines: 1 (15.5-ounce) can red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15-ounce) can black beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15.5-ounce) can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
Drops of tabasco sauce, to taste, optional
Water, as needed to adjust consistency
steps: Heat a large saucepan (pot) over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and peppers.
Sauté until the onion and peppers soft, about 4-5 minutes.
Add the kidney beans, black beans, pinto beans, crushed tomatoes, and diced tomatoes with their liquid. Stir to combine.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, tabasco sauce (if desired), and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 20 minutes until flavors have blended.
