If more liquid is needed add small amounts of water until it reaches the desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve warm.
credit: Inspired by a recipe submitted by Georgina Hignell RD, Northport VAMC
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Tiramisu Parfaits
ingredientLines: 4 ounces reduced-fat cream cheese (Neufchatel; about ½ cup), softened
¼ cup sweetener (e.g. sugar, honey, maple syrup, agave)
1 cup (8 ounces) brewed espresso or strong coffee
steps: Add the tofu, cream cheese, and selected sweetener to a food processor and blend until completely smooth, about 2-3 minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.
Stir together the espresso or coffee and the cinnamon. If the coffee or espresso has cooled, heat this mixture briefly in the microwave, about 2-3 minutes. Set aside.
Break each graham cracker sheet into four rectangular sections, following the perforations.
Gather four serving dishes (e.g. glasses, jars, bowls).

Add ¼ cup of the tofu mixture to the bottom of each dish. Working one graham cracker section at a time, briefly dip the graham crackers in the coffee and then place a layer of four in each of the serving dishes. Add ¼ cup of the tofu mixture to each dish, then top each with a second layer of four soaked graham cracker sections.
Dust each serving with 1 teaspoon of the cocoa powder.
Set in the refrigerator to chill, at least 2 hours, then serve.
notes: If you cannot find silken tofu, you can substitute 1½ cups soft tofu, ricotta, or plain Greek yogurt.
These parfaits will keep in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.

title: Tofu Breakfast Burritos
ingredientLines: 8 ounces firm unseasoned tofu, drained and cubed
½ bell pepper, any color, diced
4 tablespoons reduced-fat cream cheese (Neufchatel), softened, divided
steps: Spread the cubed tofu over layers of paper towels. Set aside to dry slightly.
While the tofu is drying, heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the olive oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the mushrooms, onion, tomato, and bell pepper. Cook, stirring often, until tender, about 5-10 minutes.
Crumble the tofu into small pieces and add it to the pan with the vegetables, along with the salt.
Stir and cook until well-combined and soft, about 5 minutes. Turn off the heat and stir in the shredded cheese.
Spread 1 tablespoon of the cream cheese down the center of each tortilla, then top with a quarter of the tofu mixture. Top with 1 tablespoon of the salsa.
Fold the sides of the tortilla toward the center, then roll up like a burrito. Repeat Step 7-8 with the remaining tortillas.
Serve warm.
notes: Tofu provides a great alternative to a typical breakfast burrito that will give you the same flavor as an egg burrito.

title: Tomato and Sausage Bean Stew
ingredientLines: 6 ounces (2 links) Italian chicken sausage, sliced
1 (15.5-ounce) can great northern beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat a large Dutch oven or stockpot over medium-high heat.
Add the sausage and cook until browned, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the onion and sauté until soft and tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes, garlic, basil, oregano, black pepper, and crushed red pepper flakes (if using).
Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil, scraping the bottom of the pan with a heat-resistant rubber spatula to release the browned bits on the bottom.
Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the beans and frozen spinach.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until heated through. If a thicker texture is desired, simmer longer, uncovered, until the sauce has reduced.
Serve warm.
notes: Since most chicken sausage comes in a 12- to 16-ounce package, try freezing the rest for making the recipe again.
credit: Adapted from www.budgetbytes.com | Submitted by Jessica Long MS, RDN, CD

title: Tomato, Spinach, and Cannellini Bean Pasta
ingredientLines: 4 cups (32 ounces) no-salt-added or low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth
12 ounces whole-wheat strand pasta (e.g. linguine, spaghetti), uncooked
1 (15.5-ounce) can no-salt-added cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat a large saucepan (pot) over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and garlic.
Sauté until the onion is soft, about 4-5 minutes.
Add the broth, pasta, diced tomatoes with their liquid, spinach, cannellini beans, oregano, and black pepper. Stir to combine.
Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to a low simmer and cover the pot with a lid.
Cook, stirring frequently, until almost all the liquid has been absorbed and the pasta is tender, about 10 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve warm.
credit: Inspired by a recipe submitted by Georgina Hignell RD, Northport VAMC

title: Tropical Fruit Salsa
ingredientLines: 1 mango (about 1 cup; can substitute frozen mango, chopping as needed)
½ pineapple (about 2 cups; can substitute frozen or canned pineapple, chopping as needed)
steps: Cut a thin slice off the top and bottom of the mango. Place the mango up on one of the cut sides. Cut along the wide sides of the pit, cutting the flesh away on both sides.
Use a paring knife to score the flesh into a grid pattern, going all the way down to the skin without cutting through. Use a large spoon to scoop the flesh away from the peel and into a large bowl.
Cut the top and the base off the pineapple. Place the pineapple upright on one of the cut sides. Slicing downward and working in sections, cut the skin away from the flesh.
Quarter the pineapple vertically. Then, using the same downward slicing motion, cut the core away from the flesh.
Cut half of the pineapple flesh into a small dice and add to the bowl with the mango. Reserve the remaining pineapple for another use.
Remove the seeds and ribs from the red bell pepper and the jalapeño. Mince and add to the bowl.
Mix in the lime juice, cilantro, and salt.
Serve at room temperature or chilled, with whole-grain tortilla chips or as a topping for tacos, chicken, or fish..

title: Tropical Smoothie
ingredientLines: 1 cup diced frozen mango or pineapple
steps: Pour the milk into the pitcher of a blender.
Add the mango or pineapple, banana, and spinach.
Blend until smooth and fully combined, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve immediately.
notes: For a boost of flavor, consider adding 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger (or ¼ teaspoon ground dried ginger) and/or ¼ teaspoon ground cinnamon.
For additional protein, try adding 1-2 scoops protein powder, 1-2 teaspoons chia seeds or hemp hearts, 1 teaspoon ground flax seed (flax meal), ¼-½ cup Greek yogurt, or ¼-½ cup cottage cheese.
Substitute your favorite unsweetened non-dairy milk if desired.
If you don’t have fresh spinach on hand, substitute any leafy green or ¼ cup loose frozen spinach.
Substitute any other frozen fruit for the mango or pineapple if desired.

title: Tropical Tex-Mex Shrimp Fajitas
servingSize: 2 tortillas with ~1 cup of the fajita mixture
ingredientLines: 1 pound frozen shrimp, peeled and deveined, thawed
1 bell pepper (any color), cut into strips
Optional toppings: Fresh cilantro, avocado slices, Pico de Gallo, plain Greek yogurt or nonfat sour cream
steps: In a small bowl, mix together the cornstarch, chili powder, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, cayenne, and cumin.
In a separate large bowl, add 1 tablespoon of the seasoning mixture and the shrimp. Mix until coated, then set aside.
Heat 1 teaspoon of the oil in a large skillet over high heat.

Add the pineapple to the skillet in a single layer. Let the pieces get a little charred before moving them around, then stir and cook again until browned in spots. Transfer to an empty bowl and set aside.
Add 1 teaspoon of the oil to the same now-empty skillet.
Add the bell peppers. Once the pieces are browned in spots, add the onion and remaining seasoning mixture. Cook, stirring often. until tender. Transfer to the bowl with the pineapple and set aside.
Heat the remaining 1 teaspoon of oil in the same skillet.
Add the shrimp, spreading them out into a single layer. Cook until they just turn pink, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the pineapple, bell peppers, onion back into the skillet with the shrimp.
Cook, stirring constantly, until everything is sizzling, about 2 more minutes.
Meanwhile, wrap the tortillas in a damp paper towel and microwave until warm, about 30 seconds.
Serve ½ cup of the fajita mixture onto the warmed tortillas.
Serve warm, topping as desired.
credit: Adapted from www.smittenkitchen.com | Submitted by Jessica Long, MS, RDN, CD

title: Tuna Sushi Bowl
ingredientLines: ½ cup cooked white or brown rice, warm or cold
1 medium carrot, thinly sliced (about ½ cup)
¼ cup shelled edamame (mukimame), cooked and cooled
1 (2.6-ounce) pouch reduced-sodium chunk light tuna in water
1 teaspoon fresh grated ginger (or ¼ teaspoon ground dried ginger)
steps: Add the cooked rice to a medium serving bowl or storage container.
Working in small piles around the inside of the bowl, add the carrot, edamame, cucumber, and tuna.
Sprinkle with the seaweed.
Add the vinegar, soy sauce, oil, honey and ginger to a small jar with a lid. Seal the jar. Shake to combine and make a sauce.
Drizzle the sauce mixture over the ingredients in the bowl.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
notes: Consider doubling the recipe for leftovers or for more servings.
Diced avocado is a nice addition to this bowl.
credit: Adapted from EatingWell.com | Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO

title: Turkey Breakfast Sausage
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher)
¼ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes (add more or less to adjust the heat level as desired)
steps: Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the turkey, sage, oregano, salt, garlic powder, black pepper, red pepper flakes, and maple syrup to a large mixing bowl.
Gently knead the ingredients together with your freshly-washed hands.
Divide the mixture into eight equal portions, then form each portion into a patty about ¼- to ½-inch thick. Press your thumb into the center of each patty to create a dimple.
Working in batches, add the patties to the skillet and cook until browned and cooked through, about 3-5 minutes on each side.
Serve warm.
notes: Both the cooked and uncooked patties will freeze well, up to 3 months.

If the patties are too dry for your taste, use ½ pound ground pork and ½ pound lean ground turkey. It will still have about half the fat as traditional pork breakfast sausage, but the slightly higher fat content will prevent a dry texture. Alternatively, you can add 1 egg or 1-2 tablespoons olive oil to the turkey mixture.

title: Turkey Chili with Beans and Corn
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher)
2 (15-ounce) cans no-salt-added beans (one type or a combination; e.g. kidney beans, black beans, pinto beans), drained and rinsed
steps: Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onions and bell pepper. Cook, stirring often, for 2 minutes.
Add the ground turkey. Cook until the turkey is no longer pink, about 7-10 minutes, breaking it up into crumbles as it cooks.
Add the garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes with their juice.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 25-30 minutes.
Add the beans and corn. Stir to combine and cook until the corn is thawed, about 2-4 minutes.
Serve warm.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Turkey Joes
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% lean or higher)
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added kidney beans, drained and rinsed
8 whole-wheat burger buns or sandwich thins
steps: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the turkey and onion. Cook until the turkey is no longer pink and the onion is softened, about 6-8 minutes, breaking the turkey into crumbles as it cooks.
Add the garlic and bell pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the beans, tomato sauce, red wine vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, and dry mustard. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook uncovered for 10 minutes.
Place ½ cup of the turkey joe mixture onto the bottom half each bun, then add the top bun.
Serve warm.
notes: If desired, you may substitute ¼ cup barbecue sauce for the red wine vinegar, Worcestershire, and dry mustard.
If you don’t have dry mustard, you can substitute 1 tablespoon prepared mustard.

title: Tuscan Bean Soup
ingredientLines: ½ medium onion, chopped (about ½ cup)
¼-½ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, to taste
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added white beans (e.g. cannellini beans, great northern beans), drained and rinsed
6 tablespoons shredded or grated parmesan cheese, divided
steps: Heat a large saucepan or pot over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, celery, and garlic. Sauté until the onion and celery are soft, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the oregano, thyme, and red pepper flakes. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir in the broth, beans, and the tomatoes with their juice.
Increase the heat to high and bring the soup to a simmer. Reduce the heat to maintain simmer.
Cover the saucepan with a lid and cook for 20-25 minutes, allowing the flavors combine.
Remove the lid and stir in the spinach.
Cover the pot with the lid and cook until the spinach is just wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Divide the soup between six serving bowls and top each with 1 tablespoon of the parmesan cheese. Serve warm.
notes: If you don’t have fresh spinach on hand substitute 1 cup loose frozen spinach.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Tuscan Tuna Salad Wrap
ingredientLines: 1 tablespoon dried parsley (or ¼ cup fresh)
¾ cup (about half 15-ounce can) no-salt-added great northern beans, drained and rinsed
½ cup halved cherry or grape tomatoes
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) olive oil mayonnaise, divided
steps: Whisk together the vinegar, oil, onion (if using), garlic, and parsley in a medium mixing bowl.
Add the beans, tuna, tomatoes, bell pepper, and celery. Toss to combine.
Set the mixture in the refrigerator to chill and to allow the flavors to blend, about for 10 minutes.
Spread 1 tablespoon of the mayonnaise on each wrap or tortilla and top each with about ¾ cup of the tuna mixture.
Roll each wrap or tortilla tightly, sealing the ends, like a burrito.
Serve cold.
notes: In place of a wrap, try adding over a bed of lettuce or salad greens or as a pita bread filling.
Keep the salad separate from the wrap if you are not eating it right away. Store in the fridge for 3 days.

title: Un-Stuffed Pepper Skillet
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground turkey or chicken (90% lean or higher)
½ cup uncooked quick-cooking brown rice
1 medium yellow or orange bell pepper, diced (about 1 cup)
1 medium red bell pepper, diced (about 1 cup)
¾ cup shredded Italian or cheddar cheese
steps: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the ground turkey or chicken. Cook until no longer pink, about 6-8 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the rice and cook, stirring often, for about 2 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes with their juice, tomato sauce, broth, bell peppers, onion, brown sugar, Italian seasoning, black pepper, and cayenne (if using). Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook for the amount of time listed on the rice package. Stir every 5-10 minutes while the rice cooks.
When the rice is tender, turn off the heat and sprinkle the cheese over the top.
Cover the pan with the lid and let sit until the cheese melts, about 5 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: For a Tex-Mex flavor, try substituting salsa for the tomato sauce and taco seasoning for the Italian seasoning.

title: Unstuffed Cabbage Roll Soup
ingredientLines: 1 pound (16 ounces) lean ground turkey (90% or leaner)
1 bag coleslaw mix (or 4 cups of shredded cabbage and carrots)
steps: Place a large pot over medium heat and add the ground turkey. Break it up as it starts to cook. Add the onion and cook until the onion is softened and the meat is no longer pink, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the coleslaw mix, beef broth, tomato sauce, rice, brown sugar, garlic, bay leaf, oregano and pepper.
Bring to a boil and reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook until the rice is tender; about 25 minutes for white or quick-cooking brown rice and 45 minutes for regular brown rice.
Remove from heat and let rest for 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf. Serve warm.
notes: Store in the refrigerator for 4 days or freeze for up to 3 months.
Substitute no-added-salt broth to reduce the sodium content.
credit: Adapted from the Wholesome Dish| Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Unstuffed Cabbage Rolls
ingredientLines: 1 pound lean ground beef, turkey, or chicken
1 cup whole-grain rice (e.g. brown rice), uncooked
steps: Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the ground meat, onion, and garlic.
Continue cooking, stirring frequently, until the onion is tender and the ground meat is fully cooked, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the cabbage, rice, diced tomatoes with their liquid, tomato sauce, water, and pepper.
Cover and simmer until the rice and cabbage are tender, about 20-30 minutes.
Serve warm.
notes: Is the final dish too thick? Add some extra water until you reach the desired consistency.
credit: Submitted by Heather Klan RDN, LD, Erie VAMC

title: Vegetable Egg Scramble
ingredientLines: ⅓ cup diced tomato (about ½ small tomato, such as a Roma tomato)
¼ cup finely chopped onion (about ¼ medium onion)
1 cup loosely packed spinach, chopped if large (or ¼ cup frozen chopped spinach)
2 ounces Oaxaca cheese, cut into small cubes (about ½ cup; can use another cheese such as mozzarella, cheddar, or Monterrey jack)
steps: In small bowl, use a fork to whisk together the eggs and water. Set aside.
Heat nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the tomato and onion. Cook until the onion is softened, about 4-6 minutes.
Add the spinach, salt-free seasoning, and black pepper. Cook and stir until the spinach wilts, about 2 minutes.
Add the egg mixture. Let sit for a few seconds without stirring then, using a rubber spatula (scraper), push the egg mixture away from the edges and bottom of the pan.
Continue to cook, gently folding with the spatula, until soft curds form, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the cheese and continue cooking, folding gently, until the eggs are just finished cooking, about 1-2 minutes.
Divide between two plates and serve warm.
notes: Another finely chopped vegetable can be used in place of spinach, if desired (e.g. bell pepper, broccoli, carrots).
For a little kick, try adding hot sauce or salsa at the end of cooking or as a topping when serving.

title: Vegetable Quesadilla
ingredientLines: ¼ cup tomato, diced (about ½ small tomato)
¼ cup onion, diced (about ¼ medium onion)
½ cup fresh vegetables, chopped or sliced (one type or a combination; e.g. bell peppers, mushrooms, spinach)
steps: Heat a medium or large nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Spray the pan with nonstick spray.
Add the tomato, onion, selected vegetables, salt-free seasoning, cumin, garlic powder, and cayenne or chili powder (if using).
Sauté until the vegetables are tender, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the vegetable mixture from the pan and set aside.
Carefully wipe out the pan with a paper towel, then coat the inside of the pan with more cooking spray.
Place the tortilla in the pan.
Spread the vegetable mixture over one half of the tortilla and cover the vegetables with the cheese.
Fold the tortilla in half and cook each side until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Cut the quesadilla into quarters and serve warm, with the Greek yogurt for dipping.
notes: In place of the cheese, consider spreading one side of the tortilla with hummus before adding the vegetables. For a cheesy flavor, try mixing 1-2 tablespoons nutritional yeast seasoning into the hummus before spreading it on.

title: Vegetable Thai Curry
ingredientLines: 1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger (or 1 teaspoon ground dried ginger)
4 cups fresh or frozen vegetables, trimmed and cut into ½- to 1-inch pieces (one type or a combination; e.g. bell peppers, broccoli, carrots, mushrooms, green beans, cauliflower, zucchini)
steps: Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook, stirring often, until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add the selected vegetables and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the curry paste. Cook, stirring often, for 2 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, broth, and sugar. Stir to combine.
Gently fold in the tofu cubes and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cook until the vegetables have softened, about 5-10 minutes, depending on the vegetables used.
Remove from the heat and stir in the lime juice, then serve warm over the cooked brown rice.
notes: Cooked chicken, fish, beef, or pork can be substituted for the tofu.

title: Vegetable Tortilla Pizzas
ingredientLines: 1 (8-ounce) bag shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese (about 2 cups)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Heat a medium skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the bell pepper, onion, and mushrooms. Sauté until tender, about 4-5 minutes.
Spray two baking sheets lightly with nonstick cooking spray and place 2 of the tortillas on each baking sheet.
In a small bowl, stir together the tomato sauce, garlic powder, basil, and oregano.
Divide the tomato sauce mixture over the tortillas, spreading evenly to cover each tortilla, leaving a ½- to 1-inch border without sauce around the edge.
Divide the cheese and sprinkle evenly over the tortillas.
Top each tortilla with a quarter of the vegetable mixture.
Bake until the cheese is melted and the tortillas are lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes. Serve warm.
notes: Try using other vegetables (or fruit) as pizza toppings. Some ideas are zucchini, eggplant, pineapple, or broccoli.
Substitute 2 teaspoons Italian seasoning for the dried basil and oregano if desired.

title: Walnut Chili Mac
ingredientLines: 1 (15.5-ounce) can great northern beans, drained and rinsed
1½ cups whole-wheat elbow macaroni pasta, uncooked
Optional toppings: Shredded cheese and sliced scallions (green onions)
steps: Heat a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, ground beef, and walnuts.
Cook for 5 minutes until brown, stirring frequently.
Stir in the water, salsa, tomatoes, and beans.
Increase the heat to high and bring to a rolling boil.
Add the uncooked pasta.
Reduce the heat to low and cover the pot with a lid.
Simmer over low heat until the pasta is tender, about 25-30 minutes.
Serve warm, topped with shredded cheese and scallions if desired.
notes: Use ground turkey or substitute additional beans to make the dish more lean or vegetarian.
Add additional vegetables such as bell peppers, mushrooms, carrots, etc. to increase fiber and nutrient density of this dish.
credit: Submitted by Emily Richters, MS, RDN, LDN, Wilkes-Barre VAMC

title: White Bean and Egg Shakshuka
ingredientLines: ¼ cup no-salt-added white beans (e.g. Cannellini, Great Northern), drained and rinsed
¼ teaspoon sweet or smoked paprika
steps: Coat the inside of a microwave-safe bowl with cooking spray.
Add the tomato sauce, beans, rosemary, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Make a well in the center of the sauce, and crack the eggs into it.
Microwave on high power (default setting) for 1 minute.
Continue cooking in 20-second bursts at 80% power until the egg yolk and white are set. Depending on your microwave, this will take about 2-4 minutes in total.
Serve warm.
notes: If you like heat, try adding a pinch of cayenne or crushed red pepper flakes.

Transfer any leftover beans and tomato sauce to airtight storage containers and refrigerate for up to 5 days. The leftover tomato sauce could also be frozen in an ice cube tray, then transferred to a plastic storage zip -top bag and stored in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: White Bean, Kale, and Tomato Stew
ingredientLines: 2 large carrots, peeled and diced (about 1 cup)
2 (15.5-ounce) cans no-added salt cannellini beans, with liquid
1 (8-ounce) package ready microwavable whole-grain rice (e.g. brown rice) or 2 cups cooked whole-grain rice
steps: Heat a heavy stockpot over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, carrots, and garlic.
Sauté until the onion and carrots are tender, stirring frequently, about 7-8 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low.
Add the chopped kale and broth.
Cover the pot with a lid.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes and their juice, cannellini beans, rice, Italian seasoning, and black pepper.
Cook until heated through.
Serve warm.
credit: Submitted by Ross M. Kennedy MPH, MSNW, RDN, Southeast Louisiana VAHCS
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: White Chili
ingredientLines: 3 medium poblano or bell peppers, finely diced
1 pound lean ground turkey or chicken
2 (15.5-ounce) cans no-salt-added white cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper, plus more to taste
2 tablespoons fresh cilantro, chopped (or 2 teaspoons dried)
steps: Heat a large saucepan (pot) over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, celery, and peppers.
Sauté until the vegetables are soft, about 4-5 minutes.
Add the ground turkey or chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Add the cannellini beans, broth, cumin, coriander, oregano, and cayenne pepper.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the cilantro.
Taste, adding more cayenne if desired.
Serve warm, with lime wedges to squeeze on juice to taste.
notes: To reduce the heat, choose bell peppers over poblano peppers.
credit: Inspired by a recipe submitted by Christina Corkern RD, LD/N

title: Whole-Wheat French Toast
ingredientLines: Optional toppings: Chopped or sliced fresh fruit, sliced or chopped nuts, maple syrup, powdered sugar
steps: In a liquid measuring cup or small mixing bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, sugar, cinnamon, vanilla, nutmeg, and salt.
Pour the egg mixture into a shallow dish that is wide enough to fit a slice of bread lying flat (e.g. shallow bowl, edged plate, pie plate, storage container).
Heat a medium skillet over medium-low heat or an electric skillet/griddle to 300-350°F.
Coat the pan or electric skillet/griddle with nonstick spray.
Working with one slice at a time, dip the bread in the egg mixture with clean hands or tongs, making sure to soak both sides for a few seconds, then place on the pan, skillet or griddle.
Cook until golden-brown, about 2-3 minutes on each side.
Serve warm with desired toppings.
notes: For a twist on traditional French toast, try substituting different flavors of extract for the vanilla extract. Some ideas include maple extract, almond extract, orange extract, or butter extract
A non-dairy milk alternative can be used in place of the milk, if desired.

title: Whole-Wheat Pumpkin Pancakes
ingredientLines: 1 teaspoon pumpkin pie spice (can substitute cinnamon)
1 cup white whole-wheat flour or regular whole-wheat flour
1 tablespoon maple syrup or brown sugar
steps: Place the butter in a microwave-safe dish and cook in the microwave until melted, about 30 seconds.
Add the pumpkin pie spice and stir to combine. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate medium mixing bowl, whisk together the milk, pumpkin, egg, maple syrup or brown sugar, vanilla, and oil.
Add the milk mixture and the butter mixture to the flour mixture. Stir gently until just combined.
Spray a nonstick skillet with cooking spray and set over medium heat.
Using a ¼-cup measure, scoop the batter onto the warm skillet. Cook until small bubbles form on the surface of the pancakes and the edges are dry, about 2-3 minutes.
Flip each pancake and cook for 1-2 minutes, then remove from the pan
Repeat the process with the remaining batter, spraying with more cooking spray as needed.
Serve warm, topping as desired.

title: Winter Vegetable Soup
ingredientLines: 1 medium acorn squash or butternut squash, peeled and cut in ¾-inch cubes (about 2 cups)
1 (15-ounce) can no-salt-added white beans (e.g. navy beans, cannellini beans), drained
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the bacon and cook, stirring often, for 3 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring often, for 3 minutes.
Add the squash, potato, celery, carrot, basil, cinnamon, and thyme. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes with their juice and stir to combine. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the broth and stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer. Cook for 8 minutes.
Add the kale and beans.
Continue cooking at a simmer until the potatoes, squash, and kale are tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Serve warm.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Zesty Black Bean Soup
ingredientLines: 3 (15-ounce) cans no-salt-added black beans, drained and rinsed
1 (10-ounce) can no-salt-added diced tomatoes with green chiles, drained
1-2 tablespoons lime juice, to taste (about ½-1 lime)
6 tablespoons nonfat plain Greek yogurt, divided
steps: In a food processor or blender, add the beans, broth, tomatoes with green chiles, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, and oregano. Blend until fairly smooth.
Transfer the mixture to a medium saucepan and place over medium heat.
Bring the mixture up to a gentle simmer and let it cook until it is warmed through and the flavors have combined, about 5-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the lime juice and stir to combine.
Divide the soup between six serving bowls and top each with 1 tablespoon of the Greek yogurt and ½ tablespoon of the scallions.
Serve warm, adjusting the flavor with additional lime juice as desired.
notes: For a chunkier texture, set some of the canned beans aside and keep them whole, then stir them in at the end of cooking.
categories: Main Dishes: Soups and Stews Recipes

title: Zesty Glazed Carrots
ingredientLines: 3 medium carrots, peeled and sliced (about 1½ cups)
1 tablespoon minced fresh parsley, minced (or 1 teaspoon dried parsley)
steps: Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the carrots, water, honey, butter, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a low simmer.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook for 7 minutes.
Remove the lid and continue cooking until carrots are fork-tender, about 1 -2 minutes.
Add the lemon juice and parsley. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
notes: Substitute halved baby carrots for the sliced carrots, if desired.

title: Zesty Tuna Burgers
servingSize: 1 burger patty without toppings or serving vessel
ingredientLines: ¼ medium bell pepper, finely diced (about ¼ cup)
¼ medium onion, finely diced (about ¼ cup)
1 celery stalk, finely diced (about ¼ cup)
Desired serving vessel (e.g. bun, leafy greens)
steps: Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add ½ tablespoon of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the bell pepper, onion, and celery. Sauté until softened, about 2-4 minutes, then transfer to a medium mixing bowl.
Open and drain the cans of tuna.
To the bowl with the cooked vegetables, add the tuna, panko, eggs, mustard, lemon zest, lemon juice, dill or parsley (if using), onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper, and cayenne.
Stir, breaking up any larger pieces of tuna, until the mixture is uniform and holds together. Form the tuna mixture into four burgers, about ⅓ cup each and about 3-4 inches wide.
(Optional) Place the burgers in freezer for 5-10 minutes to help them hold together better during cooking.
Heat the remaining 1½ tablespoons of oil in the now-empty skillet over medium heat.
Add the burgers to the skillet and cook until heated through and golden-brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve warm, with your desired toppings and serving vessel.

title: Zucchini and Corn with Parmesan
ingredientLines: ½ cup corn (drained and rinsed, if canned)
2 tablespoons grated or shredded parmesan cheese
1 tablespoon chopped fresh basil (or 1 teaspoon dried)
steps: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the zucchini and corn. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the zucchini is tender, about 7-8 minutes.
Add the parmesan, lime juice, basil, black pepper, and salt. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
notes: Lemon juice can be used instead of lime juice, if desired.

title: Zucchini Fritters
ingredientLines: 2 medium zucchini, shredded or grated (about 2-3 cups)
½ small onion, grated or finely chopped (about ¼ cup)
steps: Place the zucchini and onion in a colander (strainer) and toss with salt. Place the colander inside a bowl.
Place a clean plate or bowl on top of the zucchini-onion mixture, then weigh it down with something heavy such as cans of food. Let drain for 10-15 minutes, then discard the liquid in the bowl.
Pat the zucchini-onion mixture dry with paper towels to remove any remaining excess liquid.
Wipe out the empty bowl to dry it, then add the zucchini-onion mixture, flour, eggs, black pepper, cayenne, and garlic powder. Stir until just combined and there isn’t any dry flour left.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and coat the inside of the pan with nonstick spray.

Working with ¼ cup at a time, scoop the batter into the hot pan, leaving some space between each portion. Cook on each side until golden-brown, about 2-3 minutes. Repeat with any remaining batter, spraying the pan with more cooking spray in between batches if needed.
Serve warm.

title: Zucchini Muffins
ingredientLines: Nonstick cooking spray or muffin liners
1½ cups white whole wheat flour (or other flour)
1½ cups grated zucchini (gently squeeze out moisture)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Spray muffin tins with nonstick cooking spray or use muffin liners.
In a large bowl combine the oil, sugar, eggs, vanilla and milk. Whisk to combine.
In a medium bowl, combine salt, flour, baking soda and cinnamon. Stir to combine.
Add the dry to the wet ingredients and mix until combined.
Fold in the grated zucchini.
Pour batter into muffin pan filling each well ~¾ full.
Bake in preheated oven for 22-24 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center of muffin comes out clean.
notes: Freeze muffins in an airtight container for up to 4 months.
Substitute your favorite non-dairy milk alternative if desired.
Stir in ¼ cup chocolate chips or chopped nuts in step 6 if desired.
credit: Adapted from Cookie and Kate| Submitted by Robin LaCroix, RD, CSO
